CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.title: Pointwise decay bound at local points, equal-types case
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.summary: For any real constants Cb, C₃ ≥ 0, CΛ ≥ 0, C₀ ≥ 1/2 there are constants C₄, c₃, Cc, Cc', Cc'' such that the following holds for every parameter record P (with integers k, r), every pair of finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces, every 'place' datum p, operator-valued function f on a matrix space, base b ≥ 3, shift n₀ with shift data S (which supplies two shifted places). Assume a list of numerical side conditions (sizes of Λ, n₀, p₀, K, N, and four lower bounds on a decay exponent A₀), smoothness and decay of f, a derivative expansion on the big cell, and for both shifted places the existence of 'wave grids' and 'lift grids' and a limit bound. Then `ThmBpAt` holds: at every local point γ with G(γ) > 0, the quantity E(γ) attached to f is at most b^(C₄(2r+2)⁴) · G(γ)^(−(2p₀+n₀)) times a norm of f.
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.role: Bookkeeping: it is `thmBpAt_eqR_top` from `NormalFormTopDomination` with two extra hypotheses (membership of two auxiliary functions in a function class) added and ignored, so that it matches the packaged statement `AsmEq`. The file first does the same for the companion statement `AsmDiff`.
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.caveat: The statement is a long inequality in the project's `HermitianCurvature` machinery; the meaning of a place datum, of the quantities E and G, of the grids and of the limit bound was not unfolded. 'Equal types' comes from the theorem name and the `CutBPEq` namespace, not from a definition that was read.

literature.basis: The inequality is phrased entirely in the project's own structures (place data, wave grids, lift grids, shift data) and carries no literature naming, but its mathematical content was not unfolded far enough to tell whether it corresponds to a known decay estimate.

CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.title: Uniform rotated weighted bound from two Bessel inputs
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.summary: Hypotheses: `In91`, a two-part input (existence of a branching family for discrete-series representations under numerical conditions, and a big-cell derivative expansion with a moment bound for coefficient functions), and, for every datum D, the one-place statement `OneBesselTor D Cgf` with a common constant Cgf. Conclusion `WeightedBoundRotatedUniform`: for every Aw ≥ 0 and every Ch there are constants Cb and Cg₀ such that for all Cg ≥ Cg₀ and every datum D, whenever all local parameters have gaps at least Cg·(2r+2)⁴, the weighted sum `BSumR` with weight normWt^(Aw·(r+1)²) is at most exp(Cb·(2r+2)⁵·(number of elements of Tau)·log b) times `jSqG`.
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.role: A specialisation of the preceding theorem `weighted_bound_rotated_uniform_of_cubic_threshold` to the explicit threshold function `thrS`, which the file bounds by 43·n³; the two Zuckerman tensor-product statements for this threshold (`zuckT_thrS`, `zuckDualT_thrS`) are taken from elsewhere. It reduces the uniform bound to two named inputs.
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Bessel.caveat: I read `WeightedBoundRotatedUniform`, `theoremBRotated`, `In91`, `ZuckT`, `thrS` and the first half of `OneBesselTor`. Not unfolded: `BSumR`, `normWt`, `jSqG`, `BData`, `AllGaps`, and the orbital-integral part of `OneBesselTor`. The summaries of `In91` and `OneBesselTor` are partial. The phrase 'rank three' in the theorem name is not explained by the statement itself.

literature.basis: It is conditional on two project-named inputs (`In91`, `OneBesselTor`) and concludes the project's uniform rotated weighted bound over its own data type. Standard results enter only inside the proof (discrete-series and Zuckerman tensor statements); the conclusion is proof-specific.

CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Unifor.title: Uniform weighted point-sum bound (Theorem B, generic variant)
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Unifor.summary: The statement has no hypotheses. It asserts `StepThmBG`: for all real constants Cg, cb, Cw, cT, CT, C0 and every natural number A there are a constant CB ≥ 0 and thresholds such that, for all larger auxiliary constants, every datum D with size data, setting X, full data Y and word u satisfying the context bundle `Ctx` (taken with u = u'), and all auxiliary mass data satisfying tie, admissibility and pinning conditions, a point-sum bound holds. The bound is: over any finite set of admissible points γ, the sum of blockMinorWeight(γ)·n(γ)·(NG(γ)·ND(γ))^(A(r+1)²)·jacobianSquareBound(γ) is at most exp(CB·(2r+2)⁵·f·log b)·Ire, for the 'generic' variant of the (u,u) term system.
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Unifor.role: Final assembly: `stepThmBG_ofN` is applied to the rotated uniform Theorem B (from `weighted_bound_rotated_uniform`), the uniform amplitude statement `ampUnif_holds`, the uniform point facts `ptUnifG`, and uniform row data built from `besselOfW_holds` and the uniform restriction bound. The restriction bound is derived earlier in the same file from the finite-energy statement `energyFin`.
CompanionTheory.AutomorphicTheory.Unifor.caveat: I read `StepThmBG`, `PointSumInput`, `genT` and the four uniform inputs. The individual factors of the summand (`blockMinorWeight`, `n`, `NG`, `ND`, `jacobianSquareBound`), the hypothesis bundles `Ctx`, `MassDataTie`, `MassDataAdmissible`, `Pinned`, and the quantity `Ire` were not unfolded. Here r, f and b are the fields `D.R.rS`, `D.R.f` and the scale parameter of the size data.

literature.basis: The statement is the project's own 'Theorem B' step (`StepThmBG`): a weighted point-sum bound quantified over the project's data, settings and context bundle. Nothing in the naming or the files read marks it as a published theorem, and it does not restate a result with a standard name.

CompanionTheory.FamilyDerivativeExpansio.title: Bessel integral of a discrete series is a rank-one operator
CompanionTheory.FamilyDerivativeExpansio.summary: Setting: the unitary group of a fixed Hermitian form of signature (r+k, r+1) on C^n, n = 2r+k+1, k ≥ 1. Let σ be a discrete series representation with Harish-Chandra parameter λ (strictly decreasing, integral after the usual half-integer shift) such that compact and noncompact entries of λ differ by at least h, where h ≥ 120·n³. Let z be a vector in the middle (k+1)-dimensional block with negative norm, π a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation of the stabiliser U_W of z and of the chosen isotropic vectors (a compact unitary group in k variables), and μW, μN Haar measures on U_W and on the unipotent subgroup N. Conclusion: there is a map L from the space of σ to the space of π such that for all smooth vectors w, v of σ, the Bessel integrand ⟨v, σ(hn)w⟩·conj ψ(n)·π(h)⁻¹ is integrable over U_W × N, and its integral, an operator on the space of π, equals the rank-one operator ξ ↦ ⟨L v, ξ⟩·L w.
CompanionTheory.FamilyDerivativeExpansio.role: Derived from the project's multiplicity-one theorem `thmM` applied to a normalised 'diagonal' real-place datum, together with decay bounds for discrete-series matrix coefficients, a convergence result for the Bessel integral, and measure bookkeeping (rescaling μW to total mass one and a change of variables on U_W × N). It establishes existence of the functional L with a factorisation identity.
CompanionTheory.FamilyDerivativeExpansio.caveat: The integral, the Hermitian form, the sets U_W and N, and the predicates for discrete series and for π were read. The Bessel character ψ (defined through a linear functional `ell` and the constant −2i) and the precise form of `thmM` were not unfolded.

literature.basis: The statement is the integral form of uniqueness of Bessel models for real unitary groups (multiplicity one, as in Sun–Zhu and Jiang–Sun–Zhu) applied to discrete series; the specific gap condition and normalisations are the project's, so I cannot point to a verbatim reference.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.title: Existence of a pinned source family of unitary moduli data
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.summary: Setting: one of the project's global records D (type `D7`) and a `Host` structure A on its CM field matching the record (same prime d, same square root of −d, same complex embedding). Hypotheses: for every unitary lattice datum of rank at least 2 and every family of moduli schemes, a system of local integral models together with global toroidal models exists (`SysEx`); the coefficient ring of D is the full ring of integers of its field and contains the root of unity of order g0·g1 (`OFull`, `OZeta`); two primes of the quadratic subfield lie over the two primes g0 and g1 of D; an exponent ex > 0; and the coefficient field is large enough for levels g0·g1 and lcm(g0·g1, 15^ex) (it contains the relevant root of unity and a certain CM curve with torsion is defined over it). Conclusion: there is a `SrcFam`, a package giving for every rank N ≥ 2 and every j ≤ N a signature-(j, N−j) datum with moduli schemes, model systems and toroidal systems, complex uniformisation families at every admissible level, and two distinguished levels (one of conductor g0·g1, one with extra level 15^c), such that the first level's ideal is the product of the two chosen primes and the second has auxiliary level exactly 15^ex.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.role: Existence of an object: it builds the two levels with `levelPb_exists` and `exists_lv_iff`, chooses data of each signature with `exists_datum_tied` and `exists_sig`, and fills the uniformisation fields with `nonempty_unfFam`; all of these are proved earlier in the file or imported.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.caveat: I read `SrcFam`, `Sig`, `Lv`, `Amb`, `Sys`, `TorSys`, `UnfFam`, `Pinned`, `IsLargeFor`, `OFull`, `OZeta` and `CurveOver`, but not the record `D7`, `TorModel`, `IsRecTor`, the uniformisation type `Unf` or `IsDatW`; the reading of those parts follows names. The file name refers to a field of `Amb`, not to this last theorem.

literature.basis: The statement asserts existence of a package (`SrcFam`) tied to the project's own record `D7`; it is bookkeeping inside this construction and not a statement from the literature.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.title: Definition: eventual equality of cuspidal multiplicities
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.summary: The file contains no theorem; its last declaration is the definition `MultQ`. For a parameter record p (four components, depending on a local Langlands hypothesis for GL_n), `MultQ p` is the proposition that eventually, in the project's nested sense of 'for all sufficiently large constants and scales', every witness point q over a scale context has real datum satisfying `MultEq`. `MultEq` says: for each index i, each discrete-series model M0 and each topological isomorphism Phi between the finite-adelic groups of two Hermitian spaces Y0 and W_i that is compatible with the level data, and for every irreducible admissible representation sigma of the first group having a nonzero vector fixed by the level group and by a certain averaging operator, the multiplicity of sigma in cusp forms on Y0 with archimedean type M0 equals the multiplicity of sigma transported by Phi in cusp forms on W_i with the corresponding archimedean type. Earlier in the file three hypothesis bundles are defined: `HypA` (22 fields) and `HypE` (25 fields), mostly named after published theorems, and `HypN` (6 fields of project statements).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.role: A definition, used as a hypothesis downstream (for example in `member_built_linked_geometric`). It is proved for the standard parameter record in `GlobalTheory.Mem.Top.Bl.MultQClose.multQ_prmR` from fourteen hypotheses named after published theorems (Harish-Chandra, Langlands classification, Labesse-Waldspurger, ...).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.caveat: `MultQ`, `EvP`, `WPt`, `Prm`, `MultEq` and `IsGoodRep` were read. `cuspMult`, `IsFinIso`, the Hermitian spaces `Yc`/`Wc`, the witness structure `Wit` and the slot system were not unfolded, so 'multiplicity in cusp forms' follows the name `cuspMult`. The contents of the bundles rest on field names.

literature.basis: This is a definition, not a proved statement. The property it names (equal cuspidal multiplicities on two unitary groups with matching finite parts) is of the kind obtained from trace-formula comparisons, and the project derives it from hypotheses named after published theorems, but it is phrased for the project's own data.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.title: Definitions of row conditions holding at constructed bundle points
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.summary: The file contains no theorem; it is a list of definitions. The last one, `PredicateAtBundlePoints`, takes a 'slot' Q, a linking relation Lk on bundles and a predicate N on classes of parameter families, and says: there is a property E of bundles that eventually holds at every constructed base point of slot Q linked by Lk, and for every family class A with a bundle selection compatible with E, the predicate N holds for the refined class `D3 3 A` (families in A that also satisfy a fixed list of design, smoothness, twisting and size conditions). The definition the file is named after, `CountsIrreducibilityConstants`, is the same pattern specialised to: existence of counting constants (depending only on a list of output constants of the family) and a positive constant such that two point-counting statements hold for all sufficiently large families in the refined class.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.role: Bookkeeping definitions: each one packages one hypothesis ('row') of the project's main construction in a uniform shape 'holds at all bundle points of the constructed families', so later files can prove and consume these rows one at a time.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Definit.caveat: No theorem in the file; the last definition was described. The wrappers `Row`, `Closed`, `D3`, `Des` were read, but the underlying notions (family `FamP`, `Bundle`, slot, the counting statements `CountAllPointsClass`, `CountAllRows`, `AllJoinA`) are large project structures that were not unfolded, so the mathematical content of the individual conditions is not determined. The word 'irreducibility' in the file name is not reflected in anything I could read in the definition.

literature.basis: This is a definition, not a theorem, and it quantifies only over objects of the project's own construction (families of data `D7`, bundles, slots).

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Level subgroups act by characters on the finite datum
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Setting: the project's base data with its chain of Hermitian spaces X_0, ..., X_m, a twist datum A that attaches to each step j and each chart class a subgroup U of the adelic unitary group of X_j with a character χ of it, a Weil-type representation `kom j` of the product of the adelic unitary groups of X_j and X_{j+1} on functions on the adelic matrix space between them, a vacuum function `vac j`, and finitely supported coefficient data `dd`. Hypotheses: the chain data are admissible (`I.Ok`, `TC.Pins`) and the pinning conditions `PinX` and `PinColL` hold; these say, among other things, that the additive character is standard, the vacuum functions are the vacuum vectors of the integral lattices, `kom j` is a Weil datum for the character, and the combination built from `dd` is the prescribed rational theta datum. Conclusion: for every step j < m, every pair of live chart classes and every pair of elements k of U_j and k' of U_{j+1}, the operator `kom j (k, k')` multiplies the vector obtained as the finite combination of Heisenberg translates of the vacuum function by the scalar χ_j(k)^(-1) · χ_{j+1}(k'). So that vector is an eigenvector of the pair of level subgroups with an explicit character.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: A restatement under a descriptive name: the proof is a one-line appeal to `GlobalTheory.AdForm.LevLaw.lev_law` in `ChartLevelPairActionFiniteDatumLaw.lean`, where the real argument is (it uses `trueColumnSteps_are_standardHermitianPairs` and the properties of the level subgroups recorded in the pinning hypotheses).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The types of the objects (`Om`, `comb`, `heisO`, `WO`, `GA`, `TwDat`, `PinColL`, `PinX`) were read, but the predicates inside the pinning hypotheses (`IsWeilDatumO`, `IsRatDatum`, `IsVacO`, `A.Is`) and the chain construction `TC` were not unfolded; their description above partly rests on names.

literature.basis: It is an equivariance property of specific vectors in the project's own chain of twist data and level charts; although it has the flavour of standard Weil-representation calculations, the objects exist only inside this construction.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Bounds for degenerate terms and collision terms, unconditional
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: No hypotheses. For each fixed value c of one size constant, and for all choices of the other constants, there is a threshold such that for every datum whose parameters satisfy the project's size hypotheses above that threshold (together with standing tie, volume and absolute-convergence conditions), and every word u, two bounds hold for the diagonal term operator attached to u. First, the terms with vanishing Gram value that lie outside a distinguished set are norm-summable, and the squared norm of their sum is at most dim(u)·exp(−k·f·log k), where dim(u) is the dimension of a complex vector space attached to u. Second, the pairing of the 'big' part over the non-zero terms is at most (g₀g₁)^(−k·f/2)·dim(u)²/D* plus exp(−k·f·log k/2)·dim(u).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Assembly of two bounds from results proved elsewhere and now available without hypotheses: the Siegel mass ratio, a positivity statement `TypeP`, uniform amplitude bounds, corank-two count bounds, a smallness statement valid for all widths, and a tie statement on singleton widths.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The wrapper `On`, the two bounds and the sets of terms were read. The term operator itself, the pairing `pairAbs`, the 'big' part and the size hypothesis `Cnt.Hyp0` were not unfolded; k, f, g₀, g₁, D* are fields of the project's master datum.

literature.basis: The two bounds concern term operators, words and size hypotheses attached to the project's master datum; nothing in the statement or its naming points to a published result.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Diagonal Gram bound from the unitary Siegel–Weil formula
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups in the convergent range, for every CM extension E/F and every non-degenerate Hermitian form of size M (the adelic quotient has finite volume, and for 2n < M the average of the theta series over vectors with a given non-degenerate n×n Gram matrix equals an archimedean density times a convergent product of local densities). Conclusion: a uniform 'diagonal row' bound. For any auxiliary constants there are thresholds and a constant C ≥ 1 such that, for every datum `D` produced by the project's construction, every scale L and every index u, if the scale condition `IsScaleWithBoundedGamma`, the rank identity `RankMu` (for all indices) and the standing hypothesis bundle `HD` hold, then the squared Hilbert–Schmidt distance from the identity of the normalized Gram operator on the finite-dimensional space attached to u is at most 4(exp(C·m^5·f·L) + 1)·d²/D* + (4·exp(−k·f·log k / 2) + 2·exp(−k·f·log k))·d, where d is the dimension of that space.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Final assembly of this bound: the Siegel–Weil hypothesis is fed into the corank-one pair bounds at window width 3, the degenerate-term and collision bounds are taken at width 3, and together with a decay input (`wuDecayOfGap`) they are passed to `diagonalRow_bound_from_windowWidthThree`.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: `D7`, `HD` and the condition `TrueE` (the datum comes from the project's construction) are large structures I did not unfold. m, f, k are rank parameters of the datum and D* a normalizing constant; their meaning is taken from field names. That the operator is a normalized Gram operator comes from the definition `Kmat` (a map `Pu` composed with its adjoint, rescaled).

literature.basis: The hypothesis is a literature statement (the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups in the convergent range), but the conclusion is a bound on a Gram operator attached to the project's own datum `D7`, with project-specific constants; a conditional statement with a proof-specific conclusion.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Transformation law of the kernel function ξ under level groups
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Setting: the project's column datum I (with its conditions `Ok` and `Pins`), the global datum built from it, and a 'twisted datum' A satisfying the bundle `A.Is` (about a dozen conditions tying level charts, base points, characters χ, a Hecke-type character chr and an idempotent e of the adelic algebra). For consecutive Hermitian spaces X_i and X_(i+1) of the chain, ξ is a complex-valued function on matrices over E attached to two chart indices. Assume ξ is unchanged when the e-projection of its argument changes by k times an e-fixed element of the standard integral lattice (k a positive integer). Let κ, κ' be elements of the level groups U_i and U_(i+1) whose components at the primes in the set Q(a) are matrices over E, with determinant roots x and y. If acting by (κ, κ') inverse on the e-projection of z gives the e-projection of z' plus k times such a lattice element, then chr(x)⁻¹ · chr(y) · ξ(z') = χ_i(κ)⁻¹ · χ_(i+1)(κ') · ξ(z).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Combines the law between base points and moved points (`finiteDatum_law_between_basePoints_movedPoints`) with the lemma `transport_base` of the same file, which transports ξ from the moved points back to the base points using a congruence lemma at the idempotent, a transport statement for twisted residues and a decomposition of half-lattice elements. It is a bookkeeping step in the construction of automorphic kernel functions.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: Only the structure `TwDat`, its predicate `Is` (field names) and the definitions of `xi`, `actO`, `IsHalf`, `stdHom` were read. The meaning of the underlying point-level function `xiAt`, of the column datum `TC`, and of 'determinant root' rests on names and types. The description of χ and chr as characters is from their types (group homomorphisms to nonzero complex numbers and to the circle).

literature.basis: The statement is an equivariance property of a function defined only inside this project's construction (column data, twisted data, level charts).

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Isometric period identity from thirteen published theorems
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Thirteen hypotheses named after literature results are assumed: Harish-Chandra finiteness, rapid decay of cusp forms, covering by discrete series, Harish-Chandra modules, Casselman–Wallach, Howe duality at unramified places, the Weil representation of a unitary dual pair, the Weil–Siegel formula for unitary groups, the convergent Siegel–Weil formula, the doubling method, the unramified doubling computation for GL, the classification of discrete series, and strong approximation for SU. Further, a project datum is given (a base, column data I, laws, a 'real pack' W over the resulting global datum) satisfying the six-field bundle `AllTrue W`, with the rank parameter rS at least 1 and the non-vanishing condition `PuNZ` on period functionals. Conclusion: the property `MIstar2` holds for the complex data of W. That is, there exist a linear map V preserving norms on a level subspace, norm-preserving matrices U(u), nonzero scalars a(u) and nonzero scalars ζ(u, t) (equal to 1 at the base tuple and of valuation zero where they are algebraic) such that ζ(u, t) times the embedded algebraic period number Pt(u, t, φ, F) equals a(u) times the inner product of a theta-type vector (transformed by V) with the period vector Pu(u) applied to U(u)φ.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: This file is a one-line restatement; the proof is `GlobalTheory.Fam.miStar2_of_allTrue` in `MainTheoremFromPublishedResults.lean`. That proof combines surjectivity of the theta lift (`theta_lift_onto_all`, using eleven of the hypotheses), the family row data (`true_geometry_family_row_data`), `servedQ_of_bot`, and `star_product_nonvanishing_levels`.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: `MIstar2`, `MIDat`, `MIid`, `AuNZ`, `AllTrue` (field names) and `PuNZ` were read, but the objects they refer to (`RealPack`, `cxW`, the period numbers `Pt`, the vectors Θ and Pu) were not unfolded, so the gloss 'period identity' rests partly on names. The contents of the thirteen hypotheses were not read; their description follows their names and their location in the `PublishedTheorems` folder. Despite the name, this is not the top-level theorem of the project.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are marked by the project as published theorems, but the conclusion concerns data that exist only inside this project's construction, so the statement as a whole is proof-specific.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Period-isometry condition holds along the project's selection row
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypotheses: fourteen propositions named after published theorems (Harish-Chandra finiteness, rapid decay of cusp forms, discrete series existence and classification, Harish-Chandra modules, Casselman-Wallach, Howe duality at unramified places, the Weil representation for unitary pairs, the Siegel-Weil formula for unitary groups in two versions, the doubling method and its unramified computation, strong approximation for SU), plus the local Langlands correspondence for GL(n) and three arbitrary auxiliary parameters. Conclusion: for the project's parameter package built from these, the condition `MIstar2` holds at every 'bundle point' of every admissible selection, stated in two packagings (a direct one and the project's `MultiplicityCondition'`). `MIstar2` asserts the existence of a datum (norm-preserving maps and non-zero scalars, some required to be units at the relevant places) for which algebraic period pairings, embedded at a base place, equal a scalar times Hilbert-space inner products of theta lifts.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Bookkeeping step. It applies `main_theorem_published_inputs_variant` (the same conclusion in an 'eventually for all points' form), feeds it a diagonal-row statement derived from the unitary Siegel-Weil hypothesis, and repackages the result into the two row formats with `RowE.row` and `RL.At.of_row`.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: `RL.At`, `Row`, `AtAll`, `RowE`, `Bundle`, `MIstar2`, `MIUnit2`, `MIid` were read, but the selection framework (`Prm`, `prmR`, slots, links, family classes) and the objects inside a bundle were not unfolded; the description of `MIstar2` as a period-versus-inner-product identity follows the shape of `MIid` and field names. The published hypotheses were identified by name only.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are literature statements (namespace `Published`), but the conclusion is about the project's own bundles, selections and period data, so it is a conditional, proof-specific statement.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Pointwise formula for the kernel entry operator
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Setting: a column system I over a base B with its laws, a word u, an index a, a level i, and decoration data q, q' at levels i and i+1. The operator `ent` sends complex functions on frames of rank N_i (tuples of invertible matrices, one per embedding) to functions on frames of rank N_(i+1). The statement says that for every function x and frame y', the value of `ent` applied to x at y' equals the product of two scalars rho and rho' times `opOf` of the theta kernel `th`. `opOf` is: multiply x by powers of frame determinants, convert to a polynomial, apply the jet map given by the Taylor coefficients of the kernel at 0, convert back to a function, and divide by powers of frame determinants.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Bookkeeping: an unfolding lemma proved by definitional equality, giving the explicit form of `ent`. The file before it proves supporting facts (smoothness of the kernel, its transformation law `th_move`, equivariance of `opOf`).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The scalars `rho`, `rho'` and the kernel `th` (`thAt`) were not unfolded, and the column system `TC` is a large project structure read only by signature. The module is named after an earlier lemma `polOf_fnOf_one`; the last theorem is `ent_apply`.

literature.basis: It is a definitional identity about an operator that exists only inside this project's construction.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Uniform amplitude bounds for a single value of one constant
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: For every real number c, the property `AmpOn {c}` holds. Unfolded: for all real constants Cg, cb, Cu, cT, CT with cb, cT > 0 there are constants C, C2, Ch (C, Ch ≥ 0) such that for every Cpr and every δ > 0 there is a threshold beyond which, for every project datum `D7` with size data satisfying three standing conditions (`Ties`, `FamilyMidVolume`, `TFrameAt`, and a normalisation ≥ 1), three amplitude statements hold with the parameter C0 equal to c: two product bounds over the archimedean places for 'loss' factors, and a decay bound for the norm and Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the real-place amplitude operators in terms of a size function raised to a negative power.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Assembly step: it collects about ten earlier results (a theta-range bound, a Schur-type bound, an absolute bound, a lower bound at a critical level, formal degree expressed by a Vandermonde ratio, a real-place amplitude bound by the inverse formal degree, and a Weyl dimension formula proved in the same file) and feeds them to the lemma `ampAt_of_admitted_bounds`, taking the maximum of the thresholds.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Pinned family columns yield class data for all members

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Existence of a column choice satisfying the family laws

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel for nef bundles from principalisation
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: principalisation of ideal sheaves in characteristic zero (for a smooth projective integral variety over a field of characteristic zero and a non-zero ideal sheaf, there is a sequence of smooth blow-ups, an isomorphism away from the support, after which the ideal becomes an effective Cartier divisor with simple normal crossings support). Conclusion (`ArithHilbertSamuel`): for an arithmetic variety X of relative dimension D over a ring k finite over the integers, a nef Hermitian line bundle L with arithmetic self-intersection number a, and any Hermitian line bundle N, the set of small sections (sup-norm at most 1 at all complex points) of L^m ⊗ N is finite for all large m, and the log of its cardinality equals a/(D+1)! · m^(D+1) + o(m^(D+1)).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Reduction to one literature input: it applies `arithHilbertSamuel_nef_of_ample` (the nef case from the ample case) to three consequences of principalisation proved elsewhere: the arithmetic intersection calculus `ArCalc`, the ample case `AmpleHS`, and preservation of semipositivity under pull-back `SemiPull`.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The definitions of `IsArithVar`, `HermLB`, `smallSec`, `IsNef` and `IsSelfInter` were read at the top level; the notion of arithmetic height behind `IsSelfInter` and of regular semipositivity behind `IsNef` were not unfolded.

literature.basis: Both hypothesis and conclusion are placed by the project in its `Published` namespace: the hypothesis is Hironaka-type principalisation and the conclusion is the arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel theorem for nef Hermitian line bundles (Gillet–Soulé, Zhang, Moriwaki). The match of the project's formulation with the published one was not checked in detail.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: De Rham and l-adic characteristic polynomials of an endomorphism agree
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Let k be an algebraically closed field, A an abelian scheme over k (smooth, proper, geometrically connected commutative group scheme) and f an endomorphism of A. Let l be a prime invertible in k and let L be a finite free Z-module with an endomorphism φ, together with maps from L to the k-points of A, one for each j, that are additive, carry φ to f, have kernel l^j L and image exactly the l^j-torsion points; in other words L with φ is an integral model of the l-adic Tate module of A with the action of f. Assume the de Rham homology of A (defined as the dual of the primitive part of first crystalline cohomology for the trivial divided-power structure) is finite-dimensional over k. Then the characteristic polynomial of the map induced by f on de Rham homology equals the characteristic polynomial of φ, reduced from Z to k.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Pure restatement under a new name; the proof is `GlobalTheory.DeRham.charpoly_push_eq` in the sibling file `CharpolyDeRhamHomologyEndomorphismEqMapLadic`, which identifies the characteristic polynomial of φ with the project's characteristic polynomial of f and then treats characteristic zero and characteristic p separately.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The crystalline cohomology `Cris.H1` and its primitive part behind `HdR` were not unfolded beyond their definition as a dual space; that this is the usual de Rham H_1 rests on the project's construction.

literature.basis: Independence of the cohomology theory for the characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of an abelian variety is classical (Weil, Mumford's Abelian Varieties; Katz-Messing and Oda for the de Rham and crystalline side).

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Spanning set of integral cusp forms with bounded Petersson norms
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: A bundle of published results (`Hypotheses2`, about 17 named assumptions) is listed as a hypothesis but is not used in the proof. Statement: there is an absolute constant C ≥ 0 such that for every master datum D with its core data T satisfying the laws `LawsJ`, every step j between 1 and m whose Hermitian signature (p, q) has p, q ≥ 1, with the degree of the CM field E over Q greater than 4, every good deep level structure Y, every Lb ≥ 1 bounding the logarithms of the level, the field size of E, the product f·r and (through 391·(f·r·Lb)²) the coefficient field size, and every even dominant weight parameter (a, n) with n ≥ 8·f·r + 4, sufficiently positive on the first p coordinates and with the logarithm of its size κ at most 20·Lb: the space of cusp forms of that weight has a spanning set over the coefficient field consisting of integral forms (elements of the lattice of forms that are non-negative at all the chosen valuations) each of whose norm, and Petersson norm on every connected component, under every complex embedding is at most exp(C·(f·r·Lb)²·κ).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Bound obtained by assembly: it combines `span_thFam` (theta series span the space), `homN_smul_raw_le` (pointwise norm bound for scaled theta series) and an integrality statement giving a bounded integer multiple that lies in the lattice, with the two small lemmas of this file that pass from a pointwise bound to L2 bounds and from multiples of a spanning set to a spanning set.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: `Deep`, `Deep.Good`, `cuspW`, `latW`, `supLat`, `petW`, `petOn`, `homN`, `fieldSz`, `sizeK`, `laOf` and the hypothesis bundle were read; `CoreJ`, `LawsJ`, the uniformisation data inside `Deep` and the weight `wtZ` were not unfolded, so calling the elements cusp forms on a unitary Shimura variety and the norm a Petersson norm follows the project's names (`cuspW`, `petW`) and the visible L2 definition. The identification of which `Hypotheses2` is meant rests on the file's imports.

literature.basis: The statement is a quantitative bound with explicit project constants for lattices of forms attached to the project's own data (`D7`, `Deep`), not a statement found in the literature in this form; the literature bundle in its hypothesis is unused.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Degree of flat sections on unitary moduli spaces
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypotheses, all filed by the project as published theorems: the Scholze–Weinstein description of p-divisible groups over the ring of integers of an algebraically closed complete field by their Tate module and Hodge–Tate map; the bundle `CovTop.Hypotheses2` of 17 further statements (toroidal compactification, arithmetic volume and intersection calculus, strong approximation, semistable reduction and others); a rank-one canonical extension statement for horizontal functions across a normal crossings divisor; existence of a smooth model with normal crossings boundary and canonical extension of de Rham cohomology; and a prismatic Dieudonné statement over such rings. Conclusion (`FlatDegreeSt`): for a CM field E with host data, a Kronecker character χ, and any unitary moduli datum of signature (p, q) with level, coefficient field and complex uniformisations satisfying the project's `Laws`, on every component and for every embedding type there exists a flat section (an invertible section of the line of the corresponding weight with constant archimedean norm and prescribed valuations at finite places), and every such section has degree ((p − q)/2) · logΩ + q · (log d − lrd E). Here logΩ is the real part of γ + log(2π / root discriminant of E) − L'(1, χ)/L(1, χ).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Assembly: from the hypotheses it derives a place-shift statement, the CM degree formula `cm_different_from_ideal`, existence of archimedean sections, constancy of the Hodge–Tate valuations and their shift at CM points, hence constancy of finite valuations and the frame degree `frame_degree_cm_log_period`, and combines them with `flatDegree_of_steps`.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The moduli formalism (`Datum`, `Level`, `Moduli`, `Coeff`, `Unf`, `Comp`, `secZ`, the degree of a section, `flDefect_vw`, `lrd`) was not unfolded; the description of a flat section and the reading of `lrd E` as a log root discriminant rest partly on names. The sign conventions were taken from `FlatExistsAt` and `flatDegVal` as written.

literature.basis: The constant logΩ is the classical Chowla–Selberg / Faltings-height constant of CM elliptic curves, so the formula resembles known degree computations for automorphic line bundles, but the statement is formulated for the project's own moduli and section formalism and is conditional on literature hypotheses.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Degeneration data over a complete normal local base are uniformised
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Let R be a local domain of characteristic zero that is Noetherian, integrally closed and complete for its maximal ideal. Let D be degeneration data over R with respect to the maximal ideal: a polarised abelian scheme over R with a rigidified, cubical, symmetric line bundle, a finitely generated free abelian group X with a homomorphism to the abelian scheme, and trivialisations ψ, τ satisfying evenness, bimultiplicativity, positivity and a convergence condition. Then there exist a commutative semi-abelian group scheme G over R and a polarised abelian variety A over the fraction field of R together with a uniformisation structure linking D, A and G (G is smooth and separated with generic fibre A, carries a cubical line bundle extending that of A, and its formal completions along the maximal ideal are compatibly described by D).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Existence of an object, by reduction. When X is trivial it uses `has_of_subsingleton`; otherwise it embeds D as a factor of unitary-PEL-type data for some CM field, passes to a finite extension where a 'labelled cover' gives a uniformisation, descends along the finite extension, extends the ring action to the uniformised group, cuts out the image of an idempotent, and descends once more.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The structures `DegData`, `UnifPre` and `Unif` are long; I read their field lists but did not check each compatibility condition, so 'uniformisation' is summarised rather than stated exactly. The file imports a `Published.MumfordConstruction` hypothesis, but the theorem itself has no such hypothesis in its statement.

literature.basis: This is the content of Mumford's construction of degenerating abelian varieties as generalised by Faltings and Chai (degeneration data over a complete normal base give a semi-abelian scheme); the project itself names a related hypothesis `Published.MumfordConstruction`. The exact encoding of the data is the project's own.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Rational forms uniformise the complex models at every embedding
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypotheses: rapid decay of cusp forms (a proposition from the project's published-theorems list), a long chain of project data ending in a bundle B of type `RealTB`, and the rank inequality 8·f·r + 4 ≤ nV. Conclusion (`LUnif` for the real datum inside B): for every level i and every complex embedding σ of the coefficient field LL, the comparison map from the LL-rational space of forms to the complex model space sends LL-linearly independent families to complex-linearly independent ones, has image spanning the complex space, and intertwines the rational group action, twisted by a character, with the action on the complex model.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Projection step: a direct application of `uniformisation_every_embedding_thirdKind` to the fields of the bundle B, together with the finite-volume fact `finVol` for the adelic unitary quotient.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The conclusion `LUnif` and the hypothesis `CuspRapidDecay` were read. The bundle `RealTB` and the data it depends on (`Extra`, `RecT`, `RowSideFamily`, spectral ties and so on) were not unfolded, so what the rational and complex spaces of forms are precisely rests on field names (`FW`, `HW`).

literature.basis: The only literature input is the rapid-decay hypothesis; the conclusion concerns rational structures on spaces attached to the project's own data bundle.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Small-sections inequality for a nef Hermitian line bundle
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Assume three hypotheses about arithmetic intersection theory: `ArCalc` (a bundle of seven statements: existence of arithmetic heights and intersection functionals, and their behaviour under change of metric, constant shift, mixing, pullback, isometry), `AmpleHS` (the arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel asymptotic for ample semipositive Hermitian line bundles) and `SemiPull` (semipositivity is preserved by pullback). Let X be an arithmetic variety of dimension D+1 (integral, projective and flat over a domain finite over the integers), B a nef Hermitian line bundle on X with arithmetic self-intersection β, x_1..x_D algebraically independent rational functions, Δ > 0, and e_j (j in a finite nonempty set J) rational functions linearly independent over the integers with natural numbers n_j. If every product e_j · ∏_{i in S} x_i (S a subset of {1..D}) is a section of B of sup-norm at most exp(−n_j Δ) at all complex places, then (D+1)! · Δ · Σ_j (n_j + 1) ≤ β + (D+1) · (Δ + D·log 2 / 2 + log|J| / 2) · gdeg(B), where gdeg is the generic (geometric) degree of B.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: A re-export: the real proof is `GlobalTheory.HSNefCore.key_ineq` in the sibling file `NefHermitianSmallSectionsKeyInequality`. That proof passes to a birational model where the family is totally ordered, builds a Fubini–Study-type Hermitian bundle from the family, bounds its self-intersection from below by a chain argument (`boxFamily_movingParts_chain_bound`), and compares with B by monotonicity of arithmetic self-intersection for nef bundles.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The internal definitions of Chern-form integrals and of semipositivity were not unfolded; 'arithmetic self-intersection' is the project's `IsSelfInter` (value of an axiomatically characterised height at the generic point).

literature.basis: The inequality is conditional on hypotheses the project labels as published (`Published.ArCalc`, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel) and has the shape of known small-section bounds for nef Hermitian bundles, but this exact 'box family' formulation is not a named theorem I can identify.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Existence of the main hypothesis package from published theorems
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypotheses: the bundle `HypothesesUE` of about seventy propositions, almost all named after published theorems (automorphic forms, local and global Langlands-type results, Siegel–Weil, discrete series, class field theory, p-adic Hodge theory, local Galois cohomology); an internal statement `RowRat`; the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n in the project's formulation; a real constant and an eventually-large auxiliary predicate; and three row statements for the resulting parameters (a bound at the primes two and three, a functoriality condition, a covolume bound). Conclusion: the structure `Hyps` is inhabited. `Hyps` is a package consisting of a class of parameter families, a selection of a bundle at every point of every family in the class, a constant function, and several dozen properties of these (row conditions at the selected points, counting and volume statements, period and twist statements).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Final assembly of the hypothesis package: it obtains a linked bundle construction, converts the published statements into the 26-row package through `allRows_of_open0`, adds the norm row from `NLink.Final.main`, and concludes with `nonempty_hyps_of_allRows` plus several unconditional results. `Nonempty Hyps` is one of the three inputs of `UpperTheory.Top.plugAll`, which gives non-vanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions to the right of 1/2.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are a bundle of about seventy propositions named after published theorems, but the conclusion is that the project's own package `Hyps` is inhabited, and that package is an input from which non-vanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions right of 1/2 is derived.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Twelve open row conditions hold for the first parameter set
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Assume the bundle `HypothesesUE`, a structure with 71 fields. Almost all fields are statements the project files as published theorems (Harish-Chandra finiteness, Casselman–Wallach, the Weil representation for unitary pairs, Siegel–Weil, the doubling method, Bernstein–Zelevinsky finiteness, Jacquet–Shalika, class field theory, Chebotarev, local Tate duality and others); a few fields are further nested bundles. Then for every real constant the structure `Open0` holds for the specific parameter set `prm1` built from that constant. `Open0` is a conjunction of twelve conditions; each says that one named property (period admissibility, lambda positivity, a divisor condition, a decomposition condition, a J-selection, existence of a tie, a label condition, good reduction, a weak geometric compatibility, a multiplicity condition, a kappa condition, a differential condition) holds at the auxiliary objects (`Bundle`) that the project's selection machinery attaches to the points of its parameter families, under an existentially chosen side condition on the base.

Each of the twelve fields is supplied by one earlier theorem (`entry_hPA_at_parameters`, `real_group_inputs_combined`, `bk_law_entries`, `entry_point_g_at_parameters`, `entries_combined_real`, `nonempty_extension_entries`, `good_ft_entries`, `linked_bundles_good_of_local_langlands`, `geometric_zero_condition_all`, `main_theorem_published_inputs_third`, `harish_chandra_inputs_combined`, `weil_unitary_entries`), each fed the fields of the hypothesis bundle it needs.

The parameter set `prm1` (extension data `NEl`, no extra S-extension, closure of the trivial geometry predicate) was read only at the level of its definition.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are literature statements, but the conclusion is about objects (parameter sets, bundles at family points, row conditions) that exist only inside this project's construction.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Published inputs imply the twisted-place inequalities `OntoX`
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: The hypotheses are fourteen propositions from the project's `Published` namespace, named after literature results (Green's cuspidal characters, Clozel's cohomological representations, temperedness of cohomological conjugate-self-dual representations, l-adic characters attached to Hecke characters in two forms, Chebotarev for degree-one primes, the discrete spectrum of GL_n, Galois representations of polarized cuspidal representations, base change for definite unitary groups, Bhatt-Scholze crystalline lattices, rapid decay of cusp forms, local Langlands for GL_n, a discrete-series cover statement, Casselman-Wallach). The conclusion `OntoX` is a statement about the project's parameter families: for all small enough eps and every family satisfying the family hypotheses `FamHyp` with large enough constants, if the divisor-sum bound `DIVinN` holds (a weighted sum over non-base places is at most D0 times C times x^eps times (B0 + Nc) for large x), then there is C0 >= 0 such that for all large x, at every point of the family satisfying the side conditions `More`, and every C >= C0, the inequality system `ON` holds. `ON` consists of three inequalities over the 'twisted' places: a bound for sums of index-type quantities at a place and its conjugate, non-negativity of error terms, and a bound for a weighted sum of errors by a budget E1.

The module name mentions Galois, but the statement proved concludes `OntoX`.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Arithmetic intersection difference on a rank-two flag bundle
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: `ArCalc`, a bundle of seven statements about arithmetic (Arakelov-type) intersection numbers of Hermitian line bundles on arithmetic varieties (existence, change of metric, shift by a constant, a mixed formula with a rational section, projection formula, invariance under isometry, metric change). Conclusion: there is one family of real polynomials G(D, a, b) in three variables, homogeneous of degree D, that works for every arithmetic variety B of relative dimension d over a base ring k (k a domain finite over the integers; B integral, projective, flat over the integers) with regular local rings, every rank-2 vector bundle E on B with a smooth Hermitian metric and a full flag, the flag bundle Y of E over B with its tautological flag, and every Hermitian line bundle A on B. If Φ is the arithmetic intersection functional on Y of five Hermitian line bundles (the two graded pieces of the tautological flag, the pullback of A, the pullbacks of the two graded pieces of the base flag) and Ψ is the geometric degree functional of the first three, then for all integers a, b the value of Φ on the difference of two explicit degree d+2 polynomials equals Ψ(G(d+1, a, b)). The two polynomials are the symmetrised power (a x0 + b x1 + x2)^(d+2) + (b x0 + a x1 + x2)^(d+2), written once in the tautological classes on Y and once in the classes pulled back from the base flag.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Reduction step turning a difference of arithmetic intersection numbers into a geometric intersection number. It combines `flag_bundle_pullback_height_compare` (which supplies G), a factorisation of the polynomial difference (`homogeneous_line_base_difference`), existence of rational sections adapted to the rank-two flag, the expansion of a homogeneous form as a combination of powers of linear forms, and `arithmetic_function_swap_line_family`.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: `IsArithVar`, `IsArFun`, `IsGeoFun`, `IsFlagBundle`, `ArCalc`, `onLine`, `onBase`, `fam5` were read; the metric notions (`VMetric`, `IsCInf`, `grLB`, `HermLB` weights) and the notion of arithmetic height behind `IsSelfInter` were not unfolded, so calling Φ an arithmetic intersection functional relies on the shape of the definitions and their names. The polynomial G is only asserted to exist; it is not given explicitly.

literature.basis: The hypothesis `ArCalc` sits in the project's `PublishedTheorems` folder and the statement concerns general arithmetic varieties, so it has the flavour of a standard computation in arithmetic intersection theory, but it is not a named theorem and I could not match its particular form (an unspecified universal polynomial for a specific difference) to a reference.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: A property holding everywhere holds eventually along families
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Let q be a property of the project's bundle objects and σ a selection that assigns such an object to every index of every parameter family in a class 𝒜. If q holds for the selected object at every index of every family in the class (`AtAll`), then q holds in the project's 'eventual' sense (`EvW`): for all sufficiently small ε and all sufficiently large families in the enlarged class `W3 𝒜`, there is a threshold x0 beyond which q holds at every index.

The file name ('row of covolume onto grid') does not describe this last theorem.

literature.basis: It is a formal weakening between two quantifier patterns defined only in this project.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Archimedean data exist for every model of a run
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: The statement is quantified in the project's uniform way (`AtRuns`): for all sufficiently small ε, all sufficiently large parameter families satisfying the standing family hypotheses, eventually in the size parameter x, at every point of the construction satisfying the extra point conditions (`More`) and for every pair of 'runs' satisfying the run conditions. For such data, take any index i and any 'two-level model' M with weight ka that models the run at index i (`RunModel`); M is a finite family of arithmetic data for a rank-r Hermitian form over the CM field (lattices, arithmetic subgroups, signature index p0) with a compatible group action. Conclusion: either p0 is 0 or r, or 0 < p0 < r and `ArchOn` holds: ka = Fp + T·L for integer weights L, Fp with prescribed gap inequalities between consecutive weight entries, and every component of M carries archimedean input data with weights L, Fp and parameter T (a large structure of auxiliary sections, a potential function and positivity inequalities for Levi forms), satisfying the margin inequalities and admitting a 'flat' structure.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Assembly step. It combines the weight-gap part `run_weight_arch` and the per-component existence `archOne_of_run` (both in this file) through `archOn_of_comps`, after obtaining the numerical run conditions along the family from `runNumericalConditions_hold_along_family`, `runHolds_of_parOK` and `exists_pageRun_record_sub_four`.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Smooth projective toroidal compactification of Siegel moduli with polarised charts
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: For every genus g ≥ 1, every odd level n ≥ 3 and every polarisation function φ on integral symmetric forms that defines an admissible polarised cone decomposition in rank up to g with no self-intersections, the statement produces, over the ring Z[ζ_n, 1/n], a fine moduli scheme of principally polarised abelian schemes of dimension g with full level-n structure and an open immersion of it into a scheme S that is projective and smooth of relative dimension g(g+1)/2 over the base, with the moduli scheme fibrewise dense. Over S there is a semi-abelian group scheme of relative dimension g extending the universal abelian scheme, abelian exactly over the open moduli part. There is an effective Cartier boundary divisor such that every point of S has a complete regular local chart in which the degeneration is a Mumford-type uniformisation with monomial periods given by a cone of φ and the divisor is the corresponding monomial; and some power of the Hodge line bundle is globally generated and becomes ample after twisting by the inverse of the boundary divisor.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Final assembly: it feeds five earlier results (existence of the Siegel moduli family over Z[ζ_n, 1/n], existence of the minimal compactification, the normalised blow-up along a boundary ideal with an ample divisor, smoothness of that blow-up with semi-abelian charts, and descent of the semi-abelian scheme) into `siegelToroidalPolCharts_of_steps5`.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: I read the statement `Published.SiegelToroidalPolCharts` and the definitions of the moduli family, the polarised fan conditions and the chart predicate `HasPolChart`, but not the inner predicates (`IsMumfordOf`, `IsUnifOf`, `IsCone`, `IsRelParam`); the description of the charts as Mumford uniformisations with monomial periods follows those names and the visible shape of the definition.

literature.basis: The project places the statement in its `Published` namespace under `PublishedTheorems`, and it matches the Faltings–Chai theorem on smooth projective toroidal compactifications of the Siegel moduli space attached to a polarised admissible cone decomposition.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Valuation bounds for the theta key section via the different
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Setting: a CM field E with a project `Host` (a prime d ≡ 7 mod 16 with a square root of −d in the integers of E, plus related choices), a unitary PEL-type datum (a unimodular alternating lattice with an action of the integers of E and signature (p,q), p+q ≥ 1), a level all of whose primes are 'good', a moduli scheme Xo of the corresponding abelian schemes, and a coefficient number field F inside the complex numbers. A 'rule' assigns, functorially, a scalar to every framed point of Xo (a point together with eigen-bases of tangent vectors of the universal group scheme and a generator of the fibre of its line bundle). Hypotheses: κ is a 'key rule' (a unit attached to every polarised abelian variety with a rigidified theta section and a Lie-algebra basis, satisfying five axioms: homogeneity a^8 against det^4, base change, unit values over discrete valuation rings, value 1 at classical theta-characteristic data over the complex numbers, and a norm identity), and K is an invertible rule of weight four times the 'key' weight whose value at every framed point equals κ of the matching fibre data. Conclusion: for every finite place w of F and every valuation v in the project's set of valuations at w (obtained by evaluating rules at integral framed points over complete discrete valuation rings above w, normalised by ramification index), 0 ≤ v(K) ≤ 4 · Σ over embeddings τ of E of mult(τ) · ord_w(τ-image of the different of E), where mult(τ) is p or q.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: A bound. It evaluates K at an integral framed point, uses `exists_tied_det` (same file) to write the value as a unit times the fourth power of a determinant of eigenvector coordinates, bounds that determinant by a divisibility lemma involving elements of the different (`ColengthDifferent.colength_dvd`), and converts to valuations with `nval_bounds`; the unit statement comes from `thetaKeyScalar_isUnit_on_integralModels` and the existence of integral models of the moduli space.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The definitions of rules, framed points, weights, the valuation set and the five key-rule axioms were read, but the fifth axiom (norm identity), the notion of 'tied' fibre data and the class `algCls` of admissible integral points were only skimmed. The interpretation of K as a theta-type section of an automorphic line bundle is my reading of these definitions.

literature.basis: The statement is about objects defined inside this project (rules on framed points, the key rule κ, the project's valuation set); no standard named theorem matches it.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Three local rows from the Siegel–Weil formula
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups in the convergent range, stated as a proposition (for a CM extension and a non-degenerate Hermitian form, the adelic quotient has finite volume and the mean of theta sums over vectors with a given Gram matrix is a product of local densities). Conclusion: for every base predicate, every pair of slot conditions Q, Q' and every linkage, three row statements hold in the project's 'eventually large' form. The three rows are named Lp-selection, integral selection and torsion-freeness at bundle points; unfolded two levels they are, respectively, a pair of bounds (row is big, row is not scalar) for certain term operators, an off-diagonal norm bound for distinct words, and a lower bound 1 ≤ Tr(w)·κ^(2r) for a frame.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Bookkeeping wrapper: the auxiliary condition is taken to be trivially true, and the rows come from `what₂`, which in turn comes from `at_choice` in the same file. `at_choice` derives the three properties for an arbitrary family class and selection from the Siegel–Weil hypothesis via earlier results (`bothRowsFromSiegelWeil`, a volume-ratio theorem, `rowsFinDim_link`, an off-diagonal 'carrier gap' lemma).
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The Siegel–Weil hypothesis was read. The row conditions were unfolded only to the level of which inequalities they assert; the term operators, words, frames, bundles and slots they refer to were not unfolded, and the row names are the project's.

literature.basis: The only hypothesis is the Siegel–Weil formula, a literature statement, but the conclusion consists of three of the project's row conditions about selected bundles in its parameter families, objects defined only in this construction.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Torus translation rescales Bessel orbital integrals of K-finite coefficients
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: the bundle `GapIn.Hyp` of four representation-theoretic assumptions (a branching package, uniqueness up to scalar of Bessel maps on discrete series with large parameter gap, a multiplicity-one statement for low K-types, and one further condition on discrete series). Take local Bessel data L for the real unitary group of size 2r + k + 1 (a discrete series representation, two finite-dimensional representations of Harish-Chandra type, two vectors z, z′ and a character constant), with r and k read from D, whose Harish-Chandra parameter has gap at least Cgf times an explicit polynomial in r and k, and positive reals κ0, κ, τ with the normalisations required. Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Crystalline lattices come from prismatic F-crystals, fully faithfully
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Let l be a prime, K a finite extension of Q_l inside a fixed algebraic closure, and P0 any prism over the ring of integers O_K that is identified with the A_inf prism (Witt vectors of the tilt of O_C, with ideal the kernel of θ) compatibly with Frobenius and the structure map. Then: (1) for every finite-dimensional continuous crystalline Q_l-representation of the Galois group of K and every Galois-stable Z_l-lattice T in it, there is a prismatic F-crystal over O_K whose value at P0, after base change to the Witt vectors of the fraction field of the tilt, is identified with W ⊗ T compatibly with Frobenius and the Galois action; (2) for two F-crystals so realising lattices T and T', every Galois-equivariant Z_l-linear map T → T' is induced by exactly one morphism of F-crystals.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma for Lie algebras, all ranks
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Let F be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero and E an unramified quadratic extension with its conjugation, and let r be any natural number. On one side take quadruples (r × r matrix, column vector, row vector, scalar) over F, acted on by GL_r(F); on the other side take triples (Hermitian r × r matrix over E, vector in E^r, scalar in F), acted on by the unitary group. Haar measures give integral points volume one. For every tuple of invariants a (characteristic polynomial coefficients, moments, scalar) that is regular in the sense that a Hankel determinant is nonzero: the orbital integral of the indicator of integral points on the general linear side, weighted by a quadratic-character transfer factor and taken at the companion-matrix representative of a, equals the orbital integral of the indicator of integral points on the unitary side at any element with invariants a; and it is zero if no element of the unitary side has invariants a. There are no further hypotheses, in particular none on the residue characteristic.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: One-line restatement of `GlobalTheory.JR.unitMatch_all`, which applies `jacquetRallisUnitMatch_of_weilRep_quadratic` to `weilRepresentation_quadraticField_exists` (existence of a Weil representation of SL_2 over a field extension K with a prescribed quadratic character). It is used downstream for a 'unit lemma' on unitary groups.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: The definition file `FourierMatch.lean` was read in full; the proofs of the two inputs were not examined. That the 'Unram' class describes exactly an unramified quadratic extension is my reading of its fields (degree 2, conjugation fixing F, equal value groups).

literature.basis: This is the Lie-algebra form of the Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma, proved by Yun (with Gordon's transfer to characteristic zero) for large residue characteristic and later by Beuzart-Plessis and by W. Zhang with weaker restrictions; the Lean statement imposes no restriction on the residue characteristic, and I could not confirm that every case (for example residue characteristic 2) is covered in print.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: p-adic monodromy theorem in matrix form
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Fix a prime l and the project's period-ring data (rings playing the role of B_cris, B_dR and B_st with Galois actions and Frobenius, tied by isomorphisms to the project's concrete period rings). Let K be a finite extension of the l-adic numbers and ρ a continuous n-dimensional representation of the absolute Galois group of K whose matrix entries lie in the maximal unramified extension and are fixed by the r-th power of Frobenius, where the fixed field of that power lies in K. If ρ is de Rham in matrix form (for every Frobenius twist m of the coefficients there is an invertible matrix Q over B_dR with ρ(g)·g(Q) = Q for all g), then ρ is potentially semistable in matrix form: after restricting to the Galois group of some finite extension K' of K there is an invertible matrix Q over B_st with ρ(g)·g(Q) = Q.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: A re-export of `GlobalTheory.PMon.matThm_holds`, which assembles the theorem from five earlier results: an induction scheme, 'de Rham iff framed', a Lubin–Tate twist to total weight zero, the weight-zero case via Sen's theorem, and the reducible and irreducible induction cases.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: `MatThm`, `IsRat`, `AdmDR`, `AdmSt` and the field lists of the period-ring bundles were read; the bundles `LocPrime`, `LocAinf`, `LocTied` have many fields that I did not check, so the identification of the abstract rings with the usual period rings rests partly on field names. The five ingredient proofs were not examined.

literature.basis: This is the p-adic monodromy theorem (de Rham representations are potentially semistable; Berger, via André, Mebkhout, Kedlaya; another proof by Colmez), stated for matrix cocycles; the project elsewhere lists the same fact as a published hypothesis `DeRhamPotSemistable` under the field name `berger`.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Integral forms on an unramified tower cover descend
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Setting: a project datum D with a tower T satisfying the law bundle `LawsJ`, real data R satisfying several structural conditions (`IsGrp`, `IsFam`, `IsModels`, `IsThP`, a tie bundle `TieIn`), a level i whose Hermitian space is standard, and a frame-pinning condition on theta values. Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Rationality and integrality of the theta series, given Artin reciprocity
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: global Artin reciprocity (for every number field there is an Artin map from the ideles to the abelianised Galois group with the expected properties), which the project labels as published. Conclusion: two project statements hold. `SeriesRatS`: for the project's standard data and each index i, there is a complex number of absolute value 1 such that, on every 'good cover' (a level cover of auxiliary squarefree level whose field contains a suitable ray class field), the theta series built from rational level data, multiplied by that phase, are rational forms, and remain so after the allowed character twists. `SerInt`: for every prime l the same series, multiplied by a power of l depending only on the finitely generated lattice of coefficients, are l-integral forms on all tower covers of level prime to l, and integral forms invariant under the base level group descend to integral combinations of base forms.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Semistable reduction implies the compactified integral models package
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Hypothesis: the semistable reduction theorem for polarised abelian varieties over finite extensions of Q_p (after a finite extension the variety is the generic fibre of a semi-abelian scheme over the ring of integers). Conclusion: the project's statement `PartI`. It says, first, that Siegel moduli families exist at suitable prime-power levels away from p; and second, that for every CM field with the project's fixed auxiliary data, every unitary-type lattice datum of signature (p, q) with p + q ≥ 1 and every family of moduli schemes indexed by level, there are normal, flat, projective models over the p-adic valuation rings, each carrying a semi-abelian scheme with endomorphisms that extends the universal abelian scheme. These models are required to satisfy a long list of conditions: extension of level structures and of good-reduction points, compatibility between levels and with Siegel moduli families, split toric parts at boundary points, a Mumford-type uniformisation with a torsion isomorphism at complete local points meeting the boundary, existence and uniqueness of arcs with prescribed degeneration data, and domination by a global model over the ring of integers of the coefficient field.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..role: Reduction step: it specialises `partI_of_semistableReduction_of_arcFam`, which assembles `PartI` from many earlier results on abelian and semi-abelian schemes, by supplying the arc-family statement `arcFam_closed` proved elsewhere, so that only the semistable reduction theorem remains as a hypothesis.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..caveat: `PartI` is a conjunction of several large project-specific conditions (`N0`, `N2`, `SplitFibres`, `N3`, `N4`, `N6`); I read their definitions at the top level but did not unfold the inner predicates (uniformisation data, arc data, level conditions) in full, so the summary of each condition is approximate.

literature.basis: The hypothesis is Grothendieck's semistable reduction theorem, filed under the project's `PublishedTheorems`. The conclusion resembles the known theory of compactified integral models of unitary Shimura varieties (Faltings–Chai, Lan), but it is a project-specific bundle of conditions that I cannot match to a single published theorem.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Adelic chain datum and step characters satisfy all kernel laws
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..summary: Setting: the project's master datum D (a bundle containing a CM extension E/F and a chain of Hermitian spaces of ranks N_0, N_1, ..., N_m), a kernel-chain object t tied to it, a word u, a tuple μ, charts for every step of the chain, an auxiliary package A of adelic data, a homomorphism from the norm-one finite adelic unitary group of rank one to a fixed finite-type group, and an integer a of E. Two bundles of compatibility hypotheses are assumed (`AdPins`, about 10 fields, and `AdTie`, about 8 fields: they tie A to the kernel chain t by matching lattices, frames, cosets and class representatives). Those fields say that `xiAd` reproduces the chain's kernel entries at class representatives, is invariant under rational unitary points, transforms by characters under the level subgroups, depends only on the components at the bad places, is supported on a lattice and integral outside a finite set of primes, and that each `muOf` is multiplicative on norm-one ideles, algebraic-valued, trivial on integral elements that are 1 at the bad places, and on rational norm-one elements equals a product of complex embeddings raised to prescribed integer exponents.

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Kernel-service row from standard kernel tie and six hypotheses

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Vanishing of non-positive-weight cocycles for host frames
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.summary: Hypotheses: the literature bundle `LitN` and `KBridge`, which says that for a totally complex number field L containing the l-th roots of unity (4th roots if l = 2) and e >= 1, the second cohomology of Z_l(e+1) is a quotient of a finite Z_l-module that maps to Z_l tensor the degree-2e integral homology of GL_(4e+4) of the ring of integers of L, with kernel killed by a fixed power of l. Conclusion (`HostVanE`): for an odd prime l, e >= 1, an even modulus N and a Dirichlet character psi satisfying the host-data conditions, and any host frame (ramification data for the Galois group of Q unramified outside lN, with sign character the character mod 4 and Psi equal to the e-th cyclotomic power times psi), the frame satisfies `VanE`: every continuous 3x3-matrix-valued cocycle for the reducible base representation r0, lying in the graded piece of weight j <= 0, vanishing on prescribed subgroups away from the bad set, vanishing on inertia at bad places when j = 0, and a coboundary on the decomposition group at l when j < 0, becomes a coboundary after multiplication by a nonzero scalar.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.role: Derives `LemmaK` from Poitou-Tate duality, the local finiteness and duality statements in `LitN` and `KBridge` (through `K.lemmaK`), then applies `X.So.hostVanE`, which treats j < 0 by `So.lineNeg` and j = 0 by `So.lineZero` with a class-number-one property of the frame. It is a vanishing statement for a Selmer-type group.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.caveat: `HostVanE`, `Frame.VanE`, `HostData`, `IsHostFrame`, `KBridge`, `HGL`, `LemmaK` and the proof were read. The `Frame` structure, the grading `gw`, the base representation `r0` and the coboundary map `cob` were not unfolded, so the description of the local conditions follows the shape of the definition. The inputs (`LitN`, and `KBridge`, which resembles the comparison between K-theory or group homology and Galois cohomology) are of literature type, but the statement itself is not a named result.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Polynomial bound on Selmer lengths in Case I
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.summary: Hypotheses: `LitN` (a literature bundle with four sub-bundles: local, automorphic, Galois cohomology, CM theory); existence of a constant for `LemmaK` (over a totally complex field containing the l-th roots of unity, the second cohomology of Z_l(e+1) is finite with an explicit size bound); `KatoUseN` (Bloch-Kato Selmer vanishing for finite-order twists of ordinary representations attached to newforms of weight 2e+1); adjoint Selmer vanishing statements over imaginary quadratic fields and over Q; automorphy over imaginary quadratic fields of newform representations; a congruence-number bound in rank three; and `AutomorphyUnramifiedCoefficients` (finiteness and automorphy for the rank-three deformation problem with unramified coefficients). Conclusion (`CountI`): for every primitive Dirichlet character chi there are an exponent C and primes r1, r2 such that for every host (chi with an exponent and two auxiliary primes q1, d exceeding r1 and r2, giving a modulus N), every t for which the host is big, every 0 < e < t and every finite set of odd primes l outside the bad set of chi with l-1 not dividing 2e: for each such l and each character psi mod N in the host's set (trivial on a fixed subgroup, parity (-1)^e), the Selmer-type module of the rank-one twist by the inverse of psi times the e-th power of the cyclotomic character, with divisible coefficients, has finite length, and the sum over l of log l times the sum over psi of the normalised lengths is at most (N*t)^C.

It is a bound; it is one of several case counts (I, II, III, V, Z) combined later in `JointWinOfCounts`.
