Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Automorphic induction from GL(2) over a quadratic extension
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.summary: Let M/K be a quadratic extension of totally complex number fields and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over M (an irreducible stable space of cusp forms). Assume that above every complex embedding of K the two embeddings of M carry integral infinitesimal characters whose four integers are pairwise distinct, and that at every place of K that does not split in M the extension is unramified and π has Satake parameters at the places above. Then there is a cuspidal automorphic representation P of GL(4) over K whose Satake parameters match those of the induction of π at almost all places (at split places the union of the two parameter multisets; at inert places the square roots of the parameters together with their negatives), and whose infinitesimal character at each embedding of K is the sum of the two infinitesimal characters of π above it.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.role: Final step of a reduction: it applies `indCs_of_bcfl`, which derives this induction statement from the base change fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra for unramified cyclic extensions, to the project's proof `bcflUnit` of that lemma.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.caveat: I read `IndCs`, `IndSys`, `MixWtC`, `SplitBad`, `CuspSub` and `BCFLUnit`; the notions of Satake parameter (`HasSat`) and infinitesimal character (`HasInfChar`) were read only at the top level. The module name `WsIIOfPrintsH` does not describe the content.

literature.basis: The statement is a special case (quadratic extension, GL(2) to GL(4), regular weights, extra unramifiedness assumption) of automorphic induction for cyclic extensions as in Arthur–Clozel, and its input is the base change fundamental lemma for the unit (Kottwitz, Clozel, Labesse); the exact formulation is the project's.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Bloch-Kato Selmer vanishing for W and its quadratic twist
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.summary: Hypotheses: `LitCoh`, a bundle of twelve Galois-cohomology statements named after published theorems (Poitou-Tate, local finiteness, local Tate duality, local and global Euler characteristics, Greenberg-Wiles, Bloch-Kato local conditions, ...), and the project statement `SrcS` (for an admitted two-dimensional l-adic representation that is 'spherical at l', an ordinary source newform exists and a non-degeneracy condition at l holds). Conclusion (`KatoTwoS`): let l be an odd prime, e >= 1 with l-1 not dividing 2e, K an imaginary quadratic field with l not dividing its discriminant times class number, theta the quadratic character of K, and W a two-dimensional representation of the absolute Galois group of Q over an algebraic closure of Q_l with determinant theta, ordinary at l with weights e and -e, and satisfying the further conditions of the roughly twenty-field bundle `Used`. If the twist of W by the (-e)-th power of the cyclotomic character is attached to a newform of weight 2e+1 and W satisfies the sphericity condition `SphAt`, then every Bloch-Kato cocycle of W and of W twisted by theta is a coboundary, i.e. both Bloch-Kato Selmer groups vanish.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.role: Reduction. It obtains the statement `VanishOrdL` from `LitCoh` and the Euler-system theorem `Final.zetaUr` (through `vanishOrdL_of_zetaUr`), and applies it to W and to the twist of W by its determinant; `SrcS` supplies the source newform, `admissible_twist_by_det` keeps admissibility, and the private lemma `sphAt_tw` in this file shows sphericity is preserved by finite-order twists.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.caveat: `Used`, `SphAt`, `KatoTwoS`, `SrcS`, `SrcL`, `admitted`, `Newform`, `Att` and `BlochKatoSelmerVanishes` were read. The local condition at l inside `IsBK` (via `finiteCocycles`), the level condition `Af.Level` and `OrdPoly` were not unfolded, so 'Bloch-Kato' and 'ordinary' follow the project's names. The contents of `LitCoh` rest on field names.

The implication proved here, with the project-specific hypothesis `SrcS`, is an internal re-derivation.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Euler system for ordinary representations attached to newforms
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.summary: No hypotheses beyond the data. Let l be an odd prime, e >= 1, S a finite set of primes, and W a continuous integral two-dimensional l-adic representation of the absolute Galois group of Q that is unramified outside S, has odd determinant of square 1, is irreducible on the common kernel of the cyclotomic character and the determinant, and is upper triangular on a decomposition group at l with inertia acting on the first diagonal entry by the e-th power of the cyclotomic character up to finite order (bundle `Nf`, 13 fields). Let g be a newform of weight 2e+1 of level prime to l whose l-th coefficient is an l-adic unit and which is attached to a prescribed twist of W (`SrcUr`). Then `ES` holds: there are an integral 1-cocycle y of W, unramified outside l and not of coboundary type in the quotient line at l, and a finite set S' of primes such that for every n >= 1, every prime w outside S' with l^n dividing N(w)-1 and every surjective character psi onto Z/l^n that is trivial on the Galois group of the field of N(w)-th roots of unity, there is a 'tame' family of integral cochains indexed by Z/l^n, satisfying a psi-twisted cocycle relation, whose sum equals P*y up to a coboundary with P congruent modulo l^n to a unit times det(Frobenius_w - 1), and which is locally a coboundary on inertia at the primes other than w and l.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.role: Final assembly of the zeta-element part: `zetaUr_of_halves2` combines existence of the system together with Iwasawa-type data (`kato_global_unit_law_of_smoothed_classes`, built from an integrality statement, a Hodge-Tate law for smoothed zeta classes and a non-vanishing Hecke projection) with a non-vanishing statement at l (`pLocu`). Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Commut.title: Crystalline Frobenius at primes above l satisfies the Hecke polynomial

Let w be a place of E above l at which Z has a smooth projective integral model on which chosen correspondences T_0..T_n satisfy a pointwise Frobenius identity (an Eichler-Shimura type congruence relation) with eigenvalues ϑ_j, and let R be the multiset of complex roots of the polynomial Σ (−1)^j q^{j(j−1)/2} ϑ_j X^{n−j}, q the residue cardinality. Then ρ restricted to the decomposition group at w is crystalline, and for some Weil group element g of degree −1 the characteristic polynomial of g on the associated Weil-Deligne representation divides a power of the product of (X − r) over r in R.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Founda.title: Geometric construction of Galois representations for unitary groups
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Founda.summary: No hypotheses. The statement `GeoOne` concerns a CM field E containing a square root of −d, a prime l, an odd integer a, and an automorphic representation U of a unitary group in a variables, under conditions on the field, on two chosen places above l, and on U (unramified at non-split places outside a finite set, a type condition at one place above l, spherical at the other split places, a lacunary weight). It asserts three things. There is a continuous semisimple l-adic representation of the Galois group of E attached to U, in the sense that at almost all good split places the Satake polynomial of U annihilates Frobenius. For each good split place not above l such a representation can be chosen unramified there with inverse Frobenius annihilated by the Satake polynomial. Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Founda.title: Proper base change from its affine analogue
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Founda.summary: Hypothesis `E1` (the affine analogue of proper base change): for every Henselian pair (A, I) and every integer q invertible in A, the closed immersion Spec A/I → Spec A induces isomorphisms in all degrees on étale cohomology with coefficients in every Tate twist of Z/q. Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Founda.role: Applies `UpperTheory.Et.E2.main` to a bundle of fifteen inputs: fourteen structural properties of the project's étale cohomology that are proved elsewhere (invariance under quasi-isomorphism, descent, Mayer–Vietoris, long exact sequence, change of coefficient ring, continuity under filtered colimits, acyclicity of strictly Henselian and of absolutely integrally closed rings, and so on) plus the hypothesis `E1`. Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.ThetaC.title: Siegel-Weil formula for anisotropic unitary pairs, Fock test vectors

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.ThetaC.title: Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions from three inputs
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.ThetaC.summary: Three hypotheses. (2) `VWin`: for every primitive Dirichlet character ψ, a quantitative bound, along a specified family of abelian number fields (subfields of cyclotomic fields cut out by ψ and by Jacobi symbols for two auxiliary primes), on the sum over primes ℓ of log ℓ times the lengths of Tate–Shafarevich groups of Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ twisted by powers of the cyclotomic character. (3) Existence of a very large package `HypsAlt` (about fifty fields) of selections and bounds for a class of the project's parameter families. Conclusion: L(χ, s) ≠ 0 for every Dirichlet character χ and every complex s with real part greater than 1/2, apart from the case χ trivial and s = 1; this is the Riemann hypothesis for all Dirichlet L-functions, including the zeta function.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.ThetaC.role: Top-level plug-in step. Zero-freeness for all primitive characters is obtained from `zeroFreeAll_of_topG` (with parameter 3/2), using the shape result derived from `Green`, the package `HypsAlt`, and `supplyChi` applied to `VWin`; then `UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive` passes from primitive characters to all characters.

Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.B.title: Bernstein–Zelevinsky exact sequence for Φ⁻ of a product
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.B.summary: Let k be a non-archimedean local field and ψ a non-trivial continuous additive character. For a smooth complex representation τ of the mirabolic subgroup of GL(i+2, k) and a smooth representation σ of GL(t+1, k), form the (normalised) product τ × σ, a representation of a larger mirabolic group obtained by compact induction. The statement says that the functor Φ⁻ (twisted Jacquet module along the unipotent radical of the mirabolic with respect to ψ, normalised by a half-power of the absolute value of the determinant) applied to τ × σ has a subrepresentation isomorphic to Φ⁻(τ) × σ with quotient isomorphic to Ψ⁻(τ) × (σ restricted to the mirabolic), where Ψ⁻ is the untwisted Jacquet functor. In other words there is a short exact sequence 0 → Φ⁻(τ) × σ → Φ⁻(τ × σ) → Ψ⁻(τ) × σ|P → 0.
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.B.role: Final assembly of this exact sequence. It applies a general lemma on twisted Jacquet modules of compactly induced representations with a closed and an open cell (`twisted_jacquet_closed_open_sequence`) to explicit evaluation maps on the two cells, using about a dozen separately stated facts (linearity, equivariance, surjectivity, landing in the induced spaces, vanishing of averages on each cell); the last step only fixes index arithmetic.
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.B.caveat: The definitions of the mirabolic group, Φ⁻, Ψ⁻, the two products and the extension predicate were read; the auxiliary cell lemmas and the exact normalising twists were not checked against the literature conventions.

literature.basis: This is the exact sequence of Bernstein–Zelevinsky, 'Induced representations of reductive p-adic groups I' (1977), Proposition 4.13(c), which underlies the Leibniz rule for derivatives; the project lists it next to the companion statements of 4.13 (`ResSeq`, `PsiGP`, `PhiGP`, `PsiPG`).

Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.D.title: Volume theorem for root towers, from its inputs
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.D.summary: Hypotheses: ten propositions — `Top.Given` (a conjunction of about fourteen named background statements), integrability of fibre sums of densities, the standard properties of the Weil pairing on polarised abelian schemes, existence of constants Ch, Cu with `NineGeoU`, and six further named statements on Hodge lattices, flag degrees, twists and comparisons. Conclusion (`VolumeTheoremX`): there is C ≥ 0 such that for every CM field abelian over ℚ with host data, a datum of signature (p, q) with q ≥ 1 and p ≥ 2q+1, a model, a root tower T with a good origin having the extra property, a full intersection system, and at most 4·|CM type|·(p+q)² bad primes, the tower satisfies six properties. These are: proportionality (positive component volumes, with the geometric degree equal to volume times flag degree and independent of the level), equality of the volumes of all components, limit statements identifying degree and slope (`T1`), an asymptotic formula for top intersection numbers with error O(log B / B) (`ThmB`), and two lower bounds with the constant C (`T2`, `MeanSlope`).

Of the hypotheses only the integrability and Weil-pairing statements and the list inside `Top.Given` were read; the rest rest on names.

literature.basis: It is conditional on named background statements and concludes `VolumeTheoremX`, a package of properties of root towers with good origins, which are objects built inside this project; the theorem lives under `Proofs`, not under a literature folder.

Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.title: Good tower existence and volume theorem from ten inputs
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.summary: Ten hypotheses, each a named statement: existence of a full arithmetic intersection system; Moriwaki's Hilbert–Samuel and bigness statements; a resolution statement with coordinates over fields of characteristic zero; unique extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes over a normal base; Fargues' Hodge–Tate statement for p-divisible groups; a GAGA statement for sections of line bundles; a 'line of large degree' statement; quotients of abelian schemes by finite flat subgroups; and Zarhin's trick. The conclusion has two parts, both about normal projective flat integral models of moduli spaces of abelian varieties with an action of the integers of a CM field E and a unimodular Hermitian lattice of signature (p, q). (1) For every such global model with split components and p, q ≥ 1 there exist a 'root tower' and a 'good origin' for it with extra regularity properties. (2) There is a universal constant C ≥ 0 such that, when E is abelian over Q, q ≥ 1, p ≥ 2q + 1 and the set of bad primes is suitably bounded, every such tower satisfies: geometric intersection numbers are proportional to flag-variety degrees, with positive volumes equal on all components; arithmetic intersection numbers arise as limits of perturbed ones; an asymptotic formula with error O(log B / B); and lower bounds on arithmetic intersection numbers and on the mean slope.
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.role: Final assembly: `given_of_all_inputs` turns the first eight hypotheses into the bundle of intermediate results, and `final_theorem_of_inputs_right` combines these with point-integrability from the resolution statement, an avoidance lemma (`topAvoid`), the last two hypotheses and theta uniformization of abelian varieties (`thetaUnifAV_closed`).
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.caveat: `RootTower`, `GoodOrigin` and the properties `Proportional`, `VolEq`, `T1`, `ThmB`, `T2`, `MeanSlope` were read as definitions, but the underlying `RootModel` functions (`geoFun`, `PP`, `arFun`) were not unfolded, so calling them geometric and arithmetic intersection numbers rests partly on names. The host data also fixes a prime d ≡ 7 mod 16 with a square root of −d in E, and E unramified over its maximal totally real subfield. Three of the ten hypotheses (Hilbert–Samuel, line of large degree, intersection system) were not read in detail.

literature.basis: The ten hypotheses are literature statements (Moriwaki, Fargues, Zarhin, GAGA, resolution, and others), but the conclusion is about 'root towers' and 'good origins', structures defined in this project over integral models of unitary-type moduli spaces, with project-specific bounds. Parts of it resemble known results (proportionality of intersection numbers to flag-variety degrees), but the statement as a whole is not a named theorem.

Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.title: Heights on a root model come from flag degrees
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.summary: Hypotheses: five general statements (existence of the moduli schemes, the compactified-models package `PartI`, a resolution-of-singularities statement over fields of characteristic zero, unique extension of homomorphisms between semi-abelian schemes over a normal base, and a logarithmic bound for the maximal slope of the hermitian Lie-algebra bundle of a principally polarised semi-abelian scheme over a ring of integers); then a CM field with the project's data, a unitary datum of rank p + q ≥ 1, a global integral model Y, a multi-projective `RootModel` R, a compactified Hodge structure 𝔐 over Y with coordinates given by R, and a flag in its Hodge lattices whose graded pieces are the root line bundles of R. Conclusion (`FibreInput`): there is a constant C ≥ 0 such that for every number field L and every L-point of the variety of R, after a finite extension L' there is a hermitian vector bundle over the integers of L' with a pair of orthogonal full flags for which the heights of the point with respect to the root lines agree with the graded degrees of the flags up to C, and the maximal slope of the bundle is at most C·log(2 + C + max(−degree, 0)) + C.

Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.title: Reduction theory and Siegel sets for unitary groups
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.summary: The statement `Published.SiegelSetUnitary` is proved with no hypotheses. Let E/F be a CM extension of number fields, J a non-degenerate Hermitian matrix of size n over E, and X, Y a Witt frame (two families of r isotropic vectors in duality, with anisotropic orthogonal complement). Then for the adelic unitary group G of J there exist a compact subgroup K, a compact subset Ω of the minimal parabolic and a constant c > 0 such that: every element of G is a product of an element of the parabolic, a torus element and an element of K (Iwasawa decomposition); the Siegel set built from Ω, the cone of torus parameters cut out by c, and K is closed and its translates by rational points cover G; conjugating Ω by the torus elements of the cone stays in a compact set; the Siegel set has finite Haar measure, with an explicit bound for integrals over it in terms of an integral over the cone against the inverse modulus; the height of a point of the Siegel set is polynomially bounded by the height of any rational translate; and every smooth cuspidal function of moderate growth decays faster than any power of the height on the Siegel set.
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.role: Final assembly: `siegelCore` is put together from an archimedean maximal compact (`exists_kInf`), a compact adelic Iwasawa decomposition, existence of a Siegel domain, compactness of conjugates, a Siegel bound for cusp forms and their rapid decay; `siegel_of_core` then derives the published form (adding closedness, the Iwasawa form and the measure statements).
Development.AutomorphicSpectrum.Proofs.G.caveat: The definitions of the height function, of `IsCMExt`, and of the adelic group `GAd` and its rational points were not unfolded; the rest of the statement and its auxiliary definitions (`IsWittFrame`, `siegelSet`, `cone`, `minParOne`, `IsTorusElt`, `IsCuspidal`, `IsSmoothModerate`) were read.

literature.basis: This is classical reduction theory (Borel–Harish-Chandra, Godement, Borel's book on arithmetic groups) together with rapid decay of cusp forms on Siegel sets, specialised to unitary groups; the project files the statement in its `PublishedTheorems` folder.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Mean volume-slope lower bound on deep covers, conditionally
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: Hypotheses, all statement-level inputs: resolution of singularities and principalisation in characteristic zero, a Poincaré-Lelong formula for Hermitian line bundles on arithmetic varieties, the triple `HSUse` (an arithmetic Kleiman statement, a statement `G7`, and an arithmetic volume statement for nef bundles), Moriwaki's bigness inequality (arithmetic intersection number at most arithmetic volume), an exactness statement of Fargues for the Hodge-Tate map of a p-divisible group, a Zarhin-type statement that an abelian scheme with a relatively ample bundle is a retract of a polarised one, and an asymptotic Riemann-Roch statement for nef bundles. Conclusion `DeepStR`: there is a constant C ≥ 0 such that for every datum D with m² ≤ k, every core T satisfying the laws `LawsJ`, every 1 ≤ j < m and every deep cover Y at step j that is good and whose auxiliary level M' has at most 15 prime factors, the following holds for every weight u with gap g. One can choose a real number for each connected component, each at most that component's volume slope at weight u, whose average is at least −C·err(u, g), where err is an explicit expression in the weight (its ℓ¹ norm, its spread and log of a bound depending on u and g).
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.role: Assembly by one application of `deepStR_of_use`. The arithmetic intersection system (`ais`) and the resolution statement (`resK`) are derived in the companion file from the first three hypotheses; the semi-abelian homomorphism extension, the Hodge-Tate statement from Fargues's exactness, GAGA for sections and the quotient by a finite flat group scheme are supplied as already proved results.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.caveat: I read all eight hypothesis definitions at the top level, and `DeepStR`, `MeanAll`, `MeanGe`, `WtGap`, `bndB`, `errX`. Not unfolded: the datum `D7` beyond its field list, `CoreJ`/`LawsJ` (large structures), the deep cover structure and its `Good` predicate, and `compVolSlope` beyond one level (a slope of a component volume function against a top degree). The three parts of `HSUse` are named, not read.

literature.basis: All eight hypotheses are literature-type statements (resolution of singularities, Poincaré-Lelong, Moriwaki bigness, Fargues, Zarhin, nef Riemann-Roch), several defined under `PublishedTheorems`. The conclusion `DeepStR` is a mean volume-slope bound on 'deep covers' of the project's own data and cores, so it is conditional on literature and proof-specific.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Covolume bound for families from sixteen literature inputs
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: Sixteen hypotheses, each a named statement from the literature or a bundle of such: resolution of singularities and principalization in characteristic zero; a Poincaré–Lelong formula; a Hilbert–Samuel package (arithmetic Kleiman criterion, an upper bound, arithmetic volume of nef bundles); Moriwaki's inequality that arithmetic volume is at least the arithmetic self-intersection number; Fargues' exactness statement for the Hodge–Tate map of p-divisible groups; Zarhin's trick; asymptotic Riemann–Roch for nef bundles; four statements on toroidal compactifications and semi-abelian schemes; an arithmetic degree statement; a bundle of about thirty further published theorems (`CovTop.Hypotheses2`); a Scholze–Weinstein statement; and Grothendieck's deformation theorem. Conclusion `CovolX`: for the class `FamHyp` of the project's parameter families, once the family's constants are large enough, there is C0 ≥ 0 such that for all large x, at every admissible point of the family and for every C ≥ C0, the logarithmic covolume divided by the dimension, for each of a finite collection of lattices, is at most an explicit bound.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.role: Assembly: the hypotheses are regrouped into the bundles `HypothesesX` and `HypothesesH` (a few members are supplied by results proved in the project, such as Green's parametrization of characters and a Chow-height formula), the remaining arithmetic-geometry input comes from `deep_slim_use`, and the general theorem `topCovolG` is applied.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.caveat: About half of the sixteen hypotheses were read (resolution, principalization, Poincaré–Lelong, Moriwaki, Fargues, Zarhin, nef Riemann–Roch); the others are described from their names. In the conclusion, `lcv` is read as logarithmic covolume from its name, and the points of the family (`Pt`), the lattices and the bound `l3` were not unfolded.

literature.basis: All sixteen hypotheses are literature statements or bundles of them (several under `PublishedTheorems` or `GlobalTheory.Published`), but the conclusion `CovolX` is a covolume bound for lattices attached to the project's own parameter families (`FamHyp`); a conditional statement with a proof-specific conclusion.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Arithmetic Kleiman and Hilbert–Samuel bounds from three inputs
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: Assume three statements: (a) projective resolution of singularities in characteristic zero with a simple-normal-crossings boundary in coordinates (`ResKStatement`), (b) existence of an arithmetic intersection pairing for Hermitian line bundles on arithmetic varieties in products of projective spaces over the integers, satisfying multilinearity, a projection formula and a vanishing property (`ArithIntersectionSystemStatement`), and (c) every arithmetic variety has a Zariski-dense set of algebraic points of bounded standard height. Then three results hold for such arithmetic varieties and Hermitian line bundles: an arithmetic Kleiman-type theorem (a relatively semipositive, fibrewise nef, conjugation-invariant bundle with non-negative degree on all one-dimensional arithmetic subvarieties has non-negative top arithmetic self-intersection); and two arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel upper bounds (the limsup of the log-number of small integral sections of the n-th power, divided by n^(D+1)/(D+1)!, is at most the arithmetic self-intersection number), one for 'small generated' data and one for semipositive bundles with bounded monomials.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.role: Projection of the last three components of the long chain `hsChain` in the same file, which assembles about 180 intermediate lemmas of the project's arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel development. The file `Outright` in the same folder then discharges the three hypotheses, so this is a reduction step.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.caveat: The arithmetic varieties and Hermitian line bundles are encoded in the project's own way (multihomogeneous prime ideals of polynomial rings over the integers, metrics as positive homogeneous functions on complex cones); I read the main definitions but not all side conditions (`IsSmallGeneratedDatum`, `IsIntersectionFamily`, `MonomialsBounded` only partly). The identification with the classical theorems is by shape of statement and by the project's names.

literature.basis: The conclusions are formulations of arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel and arithmetic Kleiman/nefness results (Gillet–Soulé, Zhang, Moriwaki), and the sibling theorem is named `moriwakiBig_of_classicalTheorems`; however the exact formulation in multi-projective coordinates is the project's own, so an exact reference match was not verified.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Arithmetic nefness and Hilbert–Samuel upper bounds, unconditionally
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: The statement `HSUse` is proved with no hypotheses. It is a conjunction of three statements about an arithmetic variety given in multi-projective coordinates (a horizontal multihomogeneous prime ideal of a polynomial ring over the integers, of relative dimension D), a Hermitian line bundle A on it (a multidegree together with a positive, suitably homogeneous function on complex points), and any intersection pairing satisfying the project's axioms for an intersection system. (1) If A is semipositive, nef on fibres, invariant under complex conjugation and has non-negative height on every arithmetic curve in the variety, then its top arithmetic self-intersection number is non-negative. (2) If A is semipositive, has positive generic degree and is generated by finitely many small sections, then the limsup of log(number of small sections of the n-th power) divided by n^(D+1)/(D+1)! is at most the self-intersection number. (3) The same upper bound for sections in the normalised lattice, when all monomials of the given multidegree are bounded by the metric. The theorem just above it in the file, `moriwakiBig_outright`, proves the matching lower bound (self-intersection number at most the arithmetic volume) in the same way.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.role: Final assembly for this block: it plugs three already proved inputs (a resolution statement `resK`, the arithmetic intersection system obtained from a Poincaré–Lelong statement, and a density statement for curves of bounded height `DenseCurves.main`) into `hsUse_of_hypotheses`, which is a projection of the long chain `hsChain` (about 180 intermediate results in `HSChain.lean`).
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.caveat: The axioms of an intersection system (`IsIntersectionFamily`), the precise meaning of semipositivity (`IsSemipositiveRel`) and of the generic degree were not unfolded, and the chain `hsChain` was not examined. Two different definitions named `G7.Statement` exist in the tree; part (2) describes the one in `StatementsArith.lean`, whose namespace matches the one used here.

literature.basis: The three parts are forms of the arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel upper bound and an arithmetic nefness criterion of the kind due to Gillet–Soulé, Zhang and Moriwaki, and the project itself calls the inputs of the chain classical theorems (`moriwakiBig_of_classicalTheorems`). They are stated in the project's own coordinate formalism, so an exact match with a published statement was not checked.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Nadel vanishing for pairs and isolated non-klt divisors
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: A conjunction of two statements about a normal integral projective scheme X of dimension n over the complex numbers. (1) Nadel vanishing: if Δ is an effective Q-divisor with m(K_X + Δ) Cartier (in the project's sense `IsLogCanonicalMultiple`), N is a line bundle numerically equivalent on every complete curve to K_X + Δ plus (1/r) of a nef and big line bundle, then there is an ideal sheaf J whose zero set is exactly the non-klt locus of (X, Δ) and such that all higher cohomology of J twisted by N vanishes. (2) Isolating a non-klt point: if (X, Δ) is klt, x is a closed point, N₀ is nef and big, and positive numbers c(1..n) satisfy c(e)^e < (N₀^e · Z)/r^e for every irreducible e-dimensional subvariety Z through x together with the sum of e/c(e) over e = 1..n being at most 1, then there is an effective Cartier divisor D₀ and m > 0 with D₀/m numerically equivalent to N₀/r such that (X, Δ + D₀/m) is log canonical near x, klt near x away from x, and not klt at x.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.role: Packaging step: the pair of the two results `nadelVanishingPair` and `isolatedNonKltDivisor`, each of which the project derives from a principalisation (resolution of singularities in characteristic zero) theorem `principalisation_closed`.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.caveat: The notions `KltAt`, `LcAt`, `IsLogCanonicalMultiple`, `IsNef`, `IsBig`, `interNumRed`, `coh` were taken at the meaning suggested by their names and by the shape of the statement; their definitions and the proof via principalisation were not unfolded.

literature.basis: The proposition is defined in the project's `PublishedTheorems` folder under the namespace `Published`; part (1) is the Nadel vanishing theorem for multiplier ideals of pairs and part (2) is the Angehrn–Siu / Kollár construction of a divisor with an isolated non-klt point under the numerical condition sum e/c(e) ≤ 1.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.title: Siegel–Weil formula from Poisson summation and a constant-term identity
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.summary: Two hypotheses are assumed: `TW.Poisson`, an adelic Poisson summation formula for Schwartz functions on m × n matrices over the adeles of E, and `CTSplit`, a statement that a unipotent Fourier coefficient of the Siegel Eisenstein series equals the corresponding coefficient of an Eisenstein series of one rank lower plus a term with an explicit dilation behaviour. The conclusion `SiegelWeilStd` is a Siegel–Weil formula: for a CM extension E/F satisfying the project's `IsGood` conditions, a space A of dimension m that is definite at the infinite places and a space Y of dimension n (one Hermitian, the other skew-Hermitian), a suitable Hecke character and a doubled Weil representation, and any K-finite adelic Schwartz function Φ, the Siegel Eisenstein series on the doubled unitary group of Y built from Φ continues meromorphically, is regular at s = (m − n)/2, and its value there equals c times the average of the theta function of Φ over the automorphic quotient of the unitary group of A, with c = 1 if n < m and c = 2 otherwise.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.role: Reduction step. It first derives the invariance of the theta functional under the Weyl element (`tWeyl_of`, in the same file, from Poisson summation and project-proved facts) and then calls `siegelWeilStd_mid` with K-finite polynomial data and the existence of a lower-rank datum. The next file (`siegelWeilStd_of_ct`) discharges the Poisson hypothesis, leaving only `CTSplit`.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Aut.caveat: `SiegelWeilStd`, `EisValueAt`, `IsDbl` (top level), `Poisson` and `CTSplit` were read; the datum structures `SD`, `RD`, `LD` behind the hypotheses and the condition `ResEtaPow` on the character were not unfolded. That the hypothesis `CTSplit` is the usual constant-term computation is my reading of its shape.

literature.basis: The conclusion is the Siegel–Weil formula for a unitary dual pair with anisotropic (definite) first member, as in Weil and, outside the convergent range, Ichino and Yamana; the two hypotheses are standard analytic facts. The exact normalisations were not compared with a reference.

Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Fla.title: Tower levels are linked to fixed reference models
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Fla.summary: Hypotheses: the bundle `Given` of about seventeen standing assumptions (the compactified-integral-models package `PartI`, existence of moduli schemes, toroidal level and Hecke compatibilities, a key formula, extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes, resolution of singularities, a Hodge–Tate statement attributed to Fargues, a slope bound, and several height-theoretic inputs); a CM field abelian over Q with the project's auxiliary data, a unitary datum of signature (p, q) with p, q ≥ 1, a global integral model Y of the moduli scheme satisfying `IsGlobal`, a tower of multi-projective models indexed by an integer B and finitely many components, a `GoodOrigin` tying the tower to Y with an extra local-immersion condition, and a full intersection system. Conclusion (`RefLinked`): there are a constant C, a potential on each component and fixed reference intersection data such that for every B ≥ 2 and every component the level-B model and a fixed reference model can be realised on a common multi-projective variety with equal degrees, with their hermitian line bundles differing only at a finite set S of primes by exponents α(p), with nefness at those primes, and with the sum of α(p)·log p over S at most C·log B.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Fla.role: Assembly of a comparison bound: it combines the nefness statement `good_tower_M1_nef`, the Hodge–Tate sandwich at each prime in S, a valuation bound `val_bound` and the per-level construction `level` proved earlier in the same file, and then sums the local contributions to get the C·log B bound.
Development.WeilBound.CoreStatements.Fla.caveat: I read `RefLinked`, `RealTower`, `GoodOrigin`, `TowerOrigin`, `IsGlobal`, `Given` and `GoodOrigin.Extra`, but not the inner notions (`PB.Realis`, `PB.VertClose`, `PB.NefAt`, `IntersectionSystem`, `RootOrigin`); the phrases about realisations, vertical closeness and nefness follow those names. The individual members of `Given` were identified by name only. Despite the word 'smooth' in the theorem name, the conclusion is the linking statement, not a smoothness statement.

literature.basis: The hypotheses include several literature-type inputs, but the conclusion is about the project's own tower of models and its `RefLinked` predicate, which exist only inside this construction.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Iwahori double-coset transfer identity at non-split places (`M4`)
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: The file has no theorem; its last declaration is the definition of a proposition `M4`. Setting: a CM field E unramified over its maximal totally real subfield at every finite place, a finite place w that does not split over that subfield, integers a <= n, a matrix b in the standard maximal compact subgroup of GL_n(E_w) whose conjugate-transpose times b is the antidiagonal matrix, a conjugation-fixed uniformizer, and a strictly decreasing integer vector x whose mirrored differences l_i = x_i - x_(n-1-i) are at least 2 with consecutive gaps at least 2. `M4` asserts that the indicator function of the Iwahori double coset of the corresponding torus element in the unitary group U_n(E_w) 'matches' an explicit function `phiX` on GL_a(E_w) x GL_(n-a)(E_w), and that `phiX` is supported on pairs whose twisted norms have characteristic polynomials with separable product. `phiX` is a sum over subsets of the n/2 mirrored index pairs of products of two Iwahori double-coset indicators, with coefficient a power of minus the square root of the residue cardinality times ratios of Iwahori indices. 'Match' means: for every pair of monic conjugate-self-reciprocal polynomials Q1, Q2 of degrees a and n-a with separable product, the twisted orbital sum of `phiX` over elements with norm characteristic polynomials (Q1, Q2) equals a transfer factor (a sign and an absolute value of the resultant of Q1, Q2) times the signed orbital sum of the unitary function over elements with characteristic polynomial Q1*Q2.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: Statement only: the fourth of the local matching propositions `M1`-`M4` used for base change from unitary groups to GL_n. It is proved elsewhere as `m4` (in `...IwahoriFactorisation.TwistedConjugationNorms.Development`) and used in `match_torus_of_twisted_matching`.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.caveat: This is a definition of a proposition, not a proved theorem in this file. The orbital sum `clSum` and the sign `kapSign` were only skimmed, so the words 'twisted orbital sum' and 'signed orbital sum' are an interpretation of those definitions.

literature.basis: It has the shape of an endoscopic transfer (fundamental-lemma type) identity between a unitary group and a product of general linear groups for Iwahori-level functions, but I could not identify this explicit formula with a named published theorem.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Block candidates for base change, from three spectral inputs
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Hypotheses are three project-defined statements: `ChiTr` (a property of a certain commutative family of operators can be read off from the characters of the star-algebra they generate), `LimAt` (for every such character a limiting block object exists) and `Ident` (that limiting object has the infinitesimal characters prescribed by the archimedean data of the frame). Conclusion (`BlockCand`): for a CM field E unramified over its maximal real subfield at every finite place, n ≥ 1, an automorphic representation π of the rank-n unitary group, finite sets of places S and T and a structured frame of auxiliary data, the following holds in the project's reading sense (for every bounded character of the operator algebra that matches the eigenvalues on the fixed vector and is nonzero on a specified positive operator): there are a block index i with sizes a and n − a, two trees of discrete automorphic pieces on GL_a and GL_{n−a} over E combined by parabolic induction, associated data on GL_n, and a finite family of functions in the product space of the prescribed level whose iterated convolution is nonzero, such that the candidate has the infinitesimal character determined by the weight of π and matches π at almost all split places.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: Reduction: it calls `blockCand_of` with the three hypotheses and six further inputs that are already proved (non-vanishing of convolution powers, a tree precursor statement, existence of joins, the level-reading statement proved just above in the file, and two frame statements derived from it).
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.caveat: `BlockCand`, `GRead`, `GenIn`, `Frame0`, `Frame0.Cand`, `ChiTr`, `LimAt`, `Ident`, `Tr.space` and `pairSpace` were read, but `RunFrame`, `Ctx`, `Pre`, `SplitAt`, `BlockOut`, `IsAutRepU` and the hypotheses `Rd.ReadLimit` and `DiagAlg` that `BlockCand` itself quantifies over were not unfolded. That the candidates serve a base change from the unitary group to GL_n is inferred from the folder and namespace names and from the shape of the data.

literature.basis: Hypotheses and conclusion are all project-defined statements about the project's frames and operator algebras; nothing in the naming marks them as literature results.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Siegel–Weil coefficient identity for singular Hermitian matrices
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Setting: a Hermitian space V of rank n over the CM field E of the project's datum, an integer r with 2r < n, a nontrivial additive character of the adeles of F, self-dual-type Haar measures (covolume one) on adelic n × r matrices and on adelic Hermitian r × r matrices, a Haar measure on the adelic unitary group of V, and an adelic Schwartz function φ on V^r whose theta integral converges absolutely. For every Hermitian r × r matrix β over E with determinant zero, the β-part of the theta integral (the average over the automorphic quotient of the sum of φ over rank-r tuples x in V(E)^r with Gram matrix β) equals the β-th Fourier coefficient W_β(φ), defined as the integral over adelic Hermitian matrices b of the Fourier transform of φ along the Gram map, twisted by the character of −tr(βb)/2. The companion statement `SiegelND` covers nonsingular β.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: Proved by bringing β to a block normal form by a rational congruence (both sides are invariant under such a change of variables), then splitting into two cases: β is represented by a rank-r tuple (`siegel_weil_rank_coefficient`) or it is not (`frame_integral_eq_coefficient_nonrepresented`). It feeds the head of the project's proof of the Weil–Siegel formula (`head_of_deg`).
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.caveat: The definitions `SiegelDeg`, `Hyp`, `IfrB`, `W`, `Jt`, `gramQ` were read. The Schwartz space `schwartzA`, the automorphic measure and the 'descend' operation were taken at face value from their names. The datum `D7` enters only through its CM field and Hermitian space.

literature.basis: This is the coefficient-by-coefficient form of the Siegel–Weil formula in Weil's convergent range (rank greater than 2r) for unitary groups, here for singular coefficients; the project itself lists the full formula among its literature hypotheses as `Published.WeilSiegelFormulaUnitary`. Exact agreement of normalisations with a reference was not checked.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Siegel–Weil Euler product for singular block-form Gram matrices
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Let E/F be a CM extension of number fields with conjugation σ, J a non-degenerate Hermitian matrix of size M over E, and T an n-by-n Hermitian matrix that is zero outside an invertible upper-left t-by-t block with t < n (so T is singular). Assume 2n < M and that there is at least one linearly independent n-tuple of vectors in E^M whose Gram matrix with respect to J is T. Then the project's property `SWFree` holds: for standard Haar measures and any fundamental domain for the rational points of the unitary group of J in its adelic points, the normalised average over that domain of the translates of all rational linearly independent tuples with Gram matrix T is an Euler product, with constant 1, of the local fibre measures of the Gram map over T at the archimedean places and at each finite place.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: A re-export of `GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.WeilSiegel.Free.swFree_block`, which is a one-step specialisation of `swFree_singular` (the same conclusion for every Hermitian T of determinant zero, proved by induction on n) to block-form T.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.caveat: `SWFree`, `thetaMeas`, `IsEulerProd` and the fibre-family condition were read; the Haar-measure normalisations (`IsHaarH`, `coordW`, `coordHerm`) were not. The proof of `swFree_singular` (about 500 lines) was not examined.

literature.basis: The statement is a measure-theoretic form of the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups in Weil's convergence range, restricted to one Fourier coefficient and to linearly independent tuples; the formula is classical (Weil), though this exact formulation is the project's.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups, convergent range
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: The statement `Published.WeilSiegelFormula` is proved with no hypotheses. Take the CM extension E/F of one of the project's data objects, a Hermitian space V over E, and n ≥ 1 with 2n < rank V. Fix a non-trivial additive character of the adeles of F trivial on F, a unitary Hecke character of E whose restriction to the ideles of F is the rank-th power of the quadratic character of E/F, and a Weil representation ω of the quasi-split unitary group of rank 2n acting in the Schrödinger model on adelic Schwartz functions on rank V × n matrices. Then for every Schwartz function Φ, the Siegel Eisenstein sum over cosets of the Siegel parabolic of the values (ω(γ)Φ)(0) equals the average, over the automorphic quotient of the unitary group of V, of the theta sum Σ over rational matrices ξ of Φ(h^(-1) ξ).
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: Final step for this formula: it applies `head_of_deg` (which already contains the non-degenerate Fourier-coefficient case `siegelND`) to `siegelDeg`, the statement handling the degenerate (singular) Fourier coefficients, which is proved in the imported file `SiegelDeg.lean`.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.caveat: The structure `IsWeilSch` (the defining formulas of the Weil representation), the notion of Schwartz function used (`schwartzA`) and the normalisation of the measure on the automorphic quotient were read only at the level of their signatures, and the group `G D n` on which the Weil representation is defined was taken to be the rank-2n quasi-split unitary group from its use with the Siegel parabolic, not from its definition. The formula is stated at the identity element of the group.

literature.basis: This is the Siegel–Weil formula for a unitary dual pair in Weil's convergent range (Weil 1965), and the project itself places the statement in its `PublishedTheorems` folder under the name `WeilSiegelFormula`.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Siegel–Weil density identity for anisotropic hermitian spaces, equal-rank case
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Let E/F be a CM extension of number fields, J a non-degenerate anisotropic hermitian form of rank M ≥ 1 over E, and T a non-degenerate hermitian M×M matrix. For a factorisable test function (Schwartz at the infinite places, a pure tensor at the finite places) and any admissible choice of Haar measure on the adelic unitary group, fundamental domain, additive character and self-dual measures, the statement says there are continuous local density functions (one archimedean, one for each finite place) such that the normalised product of the finite densities converges and twice the average over the unitary-group quotient of the theta sum restricted to tuples with Gram matrix T equals the archimedean density times the Euler product of the local densities times the limit, as s tends to 1 from above, of the product over places of 1 − ε(v)·N(v)^(−s), where ε(v) is −1 at inert places and +1 otherwise. The existence of the admissible measures and characters is part of the conclusion.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: Final assembly of the density form of the Siegel–Weil formula: it combines the rank-one base case `baseOne` (proved just above from a chain of imported statements about Tate integrals, equidistribution, local density formulas and the Hasse principle for hermitian forms) with the local statement `massOne` (normalised local masses equal 1 at almost all places) through `densEq_of_one`.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.caveat: I read the definitions of `DensEq`, `BaseOne`, `MassOne`, the theta sum, the mean and the density predicate, but not the predicates fixing the measures (`IsHaarH`, `IsFDH`, `SdW`, `SdHerm`) or the test-function conditions; their meaning is inferred from names and types. The induction from rank one to rank M inside `densEq_of_base` was not examined.

literature.basis: The statement is a form of the Siegel–Weil formula (Fourier-coefficient / local-density version) for anisotropic hermitian spaces over a CM field, which is classical (Siegel, Weil; Ichino for unitary groups). The exact normalisation used here is the project's own.

Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.title: Covolume of the adelic unitary quotient equals the standard mass
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.summary: Let D be the project's global datum (it supplies a CM field E over its totally real subfield F), and V a Hermitian space over E with a unimodular base lattice whose signature is the same pair (P, Q) at every complex embedding. Take any Haar measure μ on the adelic unitary group of V, any fundamental domain 𝓕 for its rational points, Haar measures m on the real groups U(P, Q) normalised by a fixed density at the identity, and a continuous homomorphism rp to the product of these real groups that reads off the archimedean components in given frames. Then for every measurable set B in the product, μ(𝓕) · m(B) = μ{h : h stabilises the adelic base lattice and rp(h) ∈ B} · volU(n)^f · mass, where n is the rank, f the degree of F, volU(n) an explicit constant, and mass is the mass (sum of reciprocals of automorphism-group orders over the genus) of the standard positive definite unimodular Hermitian lattice of rank n. In words: the covolume of the rational points, measured against the lattice stabiliser, does not depend on the signature and equals the definite mass.
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.role: Assembled in the same file from the lemma `pi_cd_eq_map` (the product of the compact-dual-normalised real measures is the pushforward of the restricted adelic measure), the project's volume tie for the datum (`retie_volTieG_and_cdScaleTie`), the identity `vol_eq_massI_all_sig` (volume equals rank mass for all signatures) and a rescaling between two normalisations of Haar measure on U(P, Q). It is a volume identity later used for the upper and lower Tamagawa-type bounds (`up`, `low`).
Development.WeilBound.RepresentationTheo.caveat: The statement `VolSt`, the Hermitian-space structure, the lattice stabiliser, `IsMinf`, `massI` and `mass` were read. The datum `D7` is a very large bundle of which only the host field and the indexing of embeddings matter here; the frame conditions `IsFrames`, `IsRealPart` and the compact-dual measure `D.cd` were taken from their names and types. The file name refers to the auxiliary lemma, not to this last theorem.

literature.basis: The content is the classical fact that the Tamagawa-type volume of a unitary group is the same for all inner forms, so the covolume for any signature equals the mass of the definite genus (Siegel–Weil mass formula, Tamagawa numbers of unitary groups); the Lean statement is phrased for the project's datum and normalisations, so the match with a specific reference was not verified.

Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.title: Theta integrals of two unitary dual pairs agree
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.summary: Hypotheses: fourteen named propositions, among them a Siegel-set statement for unitary groups from the `Published` folder, a Siegel-Weil statement, meromorphic continuation of Eisenstein series, existence of Weil representations, a ramified multiplicity-one statement, finite-place statements at ramified, split and inert places, a spherical statement, two archimedean Lie-algebra statements, existence of archimedean matching maps, and two implications about coinvariants. Setting of the conclusion: a CM-type extension E/F of number fields, Hermitian spaces V of rank a and V' of rank a' < a and a skew-Hermitian space W of rank a + a', two Hecke characters alpha and beta, and Weil representations for the pairs (U(V), U(W)) and (U(V'), U(W)). Conclusion 1 (`ThetaIntegralsAgree`): the theta integrals converge with moderate growth; for any matched local data there is a unique constant c, and it is non-zero, such that the theta integral over U(V) of a function equals c times the theta integral over U(V') of every matching function; the finite-place maps are coinvariant quotients at good places; and there are universal signs such that when a hyperbolic plane is removed from V or from V' the constants change by an explicit factor made of ideal-character values, local epsilon factors and a value of the partial Hecke L-function of alpha/beta. Conclusion 2 (`LocalMatching`): matched local data always exist.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.role: Final assembly for this block: about 150 intermediate statements are derived one by one from the hypotheses and from unconditional project lemmas, collected into the bundle `ThKG.Leaves`, and passed to `agree_of_leaves`. The second component comes from existence of the archimedean and finite matching maps.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.caveat: Only the head and tail of the proof were read. The matching relation (`Match`, `PolMatch`), the local map structures (`RealMaps`, `FinMaps`) and several hypotheses (`FinRam`, `SphTri`, `LieSecond`) were read as definitions but not fully unfolded; which hypotheses are literature statements is judged from names and folders.

literature.basis: The comparison is in the tradition of Siegel-Weil and Rallis, but the statement is about the project's own matching data and constants and is conditional on named hypotheses, so it is not a restatement of a published theorem.

Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.title: Comparison of theta integrals for two unitary dual pairs (conditional)
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.summary: Seven hypotheses are assumed: Bernstein's theorem that the parabolically induced product of two irreducible unitarisable smooth representations of p-adic general linear groups is irreducible; `SiegelCore` (reduction theory for adelic unitary groups over CM extensions: Siegel sets, Iwasawa decomposition, rapid decay of cusp forms); `EisBL` (convergence and meromorphic continuation of Siegel Eisenstein series on doubled unitary groups); `SiegelWeilStd` (the Siegel–Weil formula for a definite unitary group paired with a doubled one); and three local statements at finite places for the Weil representations in a 'triple' (`SphSplit` at split places, `HoweInert` and `SphFun` at non-split places, about spherical vectors, Howe's generation property for the vacuum vector, and equality of spherical functionals). Conclusion: `ThetaIntegralsAgree` and `LocalMatching`. For a CM extension E/F, Hermitian spaces V (dimension a) and V' (dimension a' < a) and a skew-Hermitian space W of dimension a + a' with compatible Hecke characters, matching data exist at the real and finite places; the theta integrals over the unitary group of V and over that of V' converge, and for matching Schwartz functions they agree up to one nonzero constant which is unique; two recursion steps relate these constants when a hyperbolic plane is removed, with an explicit factor containing a partial Hecke L-value and local epsilon factors.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.role: Final assembly of the project's 'Theorem K' in its spherical form: it calls `Tr.closeSph` with facts derived from Bernstein's theorem (coinvariants, multiplicity one at ramified and split places), the three local hypotheses, project-proved archimedean facts and the Siegel-domain, Eisenstein and Siegel–Weil inputs.
Development.WeilBound.ThetaLifts.Spheric.caveat: The conclusion's definitions (`IsTriple`, `Match`, `IsConst`, `StepAlpha`, `StepBeta`) were read; the real and finite 'matching maps' (`IsRealMaps`, `IsFinMaps`) and the internals of the proof term `closeSph` were not unfolded. The label 'Theorem K' comes from the theorem name.

literature.basis: Several hypotheses are literature statements (Bernstein's irreducibility theorem is in the project's `Published` namespace; the Siegel–Weil formula and Eisenstein continuation are classical), but the conclusion is an identity between theta integrals with project-specific matching data and normalisations, which I could not identify with a named published theorem.

Formalism.FourierDecayAlt.P.CutMP.Smooth.title: Every built real place has a model place
Formalism.FourierDecayAlt.P.CutMP.Smooth.summary: No hypotheses. It proves `ModelPlaceBuilt2`: there is a constant Cc such that for every CM number field, every setting S of the project's analysis at real places, and every tower, test functions f, cutoff χ and auxiliary data forming a 'built place' with constant Cc (which includes unramifiedness, grid conditions, a long cut interval, smoothness of f and a size budget), under a validity condition at each place and two word conditions, the following holds for every cut with cutoff χ and every real place v. There exist level data L, a map j into a space of smooth functions, real parameters lam and positive constants Cm, σ such that `IsModelPlace` holds: the level and interlacing conditions on the cut interval, square-integrability of j under words of bounded length, an adjointness identity, an eigenvalue identity where a degree-(k+2r+1) operator acts on j by the product of (Y + lam_s), the identity principal Hermitian form of the ε-cut-off of f = Cm × model cutoff energy form at scale σ·ε for every admissible word, and agreement of admissibility and sizes with the model system.
Formalism.FourierDecayAlt.P.CutMP.Smooth.role: A two-line corollary: `modelPlaceBuilt2_of_chartEqs` applied to `chart_equations_holds`, the latter being a statement that solutions of the project's invariant differential equations satisfy, in local charts, a system of differential operators whose common characteristic directions are confined to nilpotent directions; that statement is in turn deduced from three Capelli-type identities. It is one of the three inputs bundled in `carrierNeedsFromD`.
Formalism.FourierDecayAlt.P.CutMP.Smooth.caveat: `IsModelPlace`, `IsBuiltPlace`, the setting structure and `ChartEqs` were read; the objects inside them (level data, the algebra acting on j, the principal Hermitian form, the cutoff energy form, the model system) were not unfolded, so the summary follows the structure of the definitions. The description of the proof route through regularity of solutions rests on reading `ChartEqs` and on the namespace name.

literature.basis: The statement is entirely about the project's own notion of 'built place' and 'model place'; nothing in it restates a named theorem.

Formalism.L2.G.linkG_concrete5.title: Group compatibility and one admissibility condition give the link condition
Formalism.L2.G.linkG_concrete5.summary: The statement concerns the project's parameter families `FamP`: for each real x and index i, a master datum with size data, parameter choices and many attached constants. For a class of such families, 'closed' means: for every sufficiently small ε there are threshold constants such that the property holds for every family in the class whose constants exceed the thresholds. Hypotheses: (1) closedness of 'group compatibility', i.e. for large x every member carries a compatibility package (Hermitian data, forms, a comparison of lattices, ring compatibility, and a description of its local data as coming from a level structure); (2) closedness of the second admissibility condition, which bounds the size of a selected index set between n·δ/2 and 2n·δ and bounds a quantity `BTT` by that size times x^(−2+ε). Conclusion: closedness of `LinkG`, which asserts constants C, x0 and a function δ(x) → 0 such that for x ≥ x0 every member satisfies a five-part local condition: bounds on local lattice lengths at each place, a bound on certain orbit sums by 2m·N·a/p, an inequality at inert places of small residue characteristic comparing sums of von Mangoldt-type class sums (minus explicit error terms) with 'gains', containment of served orbits, and a mean bound.
Formalism.L2.G.linkG_concrete5.role: A reduction step: it is the preceding lemma `linkG_concrete_noKer` with its extra hypothesis `Loc` discharged by `loc_proved`. That lemma derives trivial stabilisers, a standard-subgroup property and a descent property from group compatibility and feeds them into the closed forms of the project's 'first' and 'second' theorems.
Formalism.L2.G.linkG_concrete5.caveat: The parameter family structure `FamP` has dozens of fields and the five clauses of the link condition involve further project quantities (`VV`, `Sv`, `gain`, `tau`, `vonMangoldtClassSum`, `BTT`) that I read only at the level of their use in the statement. Their mathematical meaning is not established here.

literature.basis: All objects (parameter families, group compatibility, link condition) exist only inside this project's construction; no standard theorem is restated.

Formalism.LocalToGlobal.IndefiniteReal.T.title: Record of real-place data and its frame-existence condition
Formalism.LocalToGlobal.IndefiniteReal.T.summary: The file contains no theorem. It defines the predicate `TrISepWith` (a given family of transformations of index-valued functions keeps distinct points of a certain finite index set distinct), a few auxiliary constructions, and the large structure `RealT`: a record with about forty fields attached to the project's datum `D7`, tying a 'real data' package to previously built row-side, column and spectral objects (equalities between them, a conjugate-linear map into a space of automorphic functions with a norm identity, sign and level conditions, standard orthonormal lattice frames, positivity of the Hermitian spaces). The last definition, `RealT.FramesEx`, is the proposition that there exist lattices in the Hermitian spaces of the datum and finite-adelic matrices that form 'SD frames' and satisfy the 'normal frame conditions' at the finite set of places recorded in the real data.

Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.title: Explicit counting constant equals the ratio of mass-data volumes
Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.summary: Setting: one of the project's global configurations (`HidaSetting` over a record `D7`, with a CM extension, a hermitian lattice, two words u and u′ indexing members of a family, fundamental sets, measures and auxiliary records). Hypotheses: a covolume identity for reference measures (`CovolRef`), a Siegel–Weil type input for the hermitian space (`SWXS`), standing compatibility conditions on measures and the additive character, non-vanishing of two Gram determinants, convergence of a product of local volumes, local tie conditions at u and u′, positivity of four quotient volumes, a congruence between two integers attached to u and u′ modulo the square of a fixed integer, and that a finite set of lattices is a system of representatives; three further facts are assumed as instance arguments. Conclusion: the explicit constant `cExpl` (a mass constant of the CM extension, times a power of the discriminant of the totally real field, times a product of L-values, divided by a weighted count of lattice representatives) equals n0c · ngFac / (al · kapN), where n0c and al are entries of the project's mass-data record for this configuration and ngFac, kapN are explicit normalising factors.
Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.role: Bookkeeping reduction: it is `NcAllS.ncTie0All_of` with its real-bracket hypothesis discharged by `RealBracket_holds` applied to the covolume identity, so one hypothesis is replaced by a simpler one.

The reading of the factors of `cExpl` as mass constant and L-values rests on names.
