Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.title: Kernel expansion holds in every tied concrete setting
Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.summary: No hypotheses. The statement is the proposition `KernelExponentAgreement`: for every datum `D`, every concrete unitary-group setting X for it (a Hermitian space over the CM field with a basis, a lattice, discrete-series parameters at the infinite places and a level), every completion Y of that setting, and every pair of indices u, u', if the bundle `ConcTie X Y` of normalizations and compatibilities holds, then the kernel expansion holds for (u, u'). The kernel expansion says that there is a continuous linear operator K between the two coefficient spaces such that an explicit family of terms sums to K, and K represents the normalized inner product between the two families of functions on the adelic group attached to u and u'.
Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.role: Assembly of earlier unconditional results: folding and integrability statements (`FoldOKC_outright`, `OOIntAllC_outright`), existence of fundamental domains, membership in the Hilbert space, independence and well-definedness of the amplitudes, and absolute convergence are fed into `KExpansionC_holds`. It discharges one of the nineteen hypotheses bundled in `TheoremSClosedHypotheses`, which the file's main theorem `theoremS_of_conj` consumes.
Formalism.LocalToGlobal.SiegelLatticeThe.caveat: Despite its name, the proposition is a series expansion of a kernel operator (`KExpansion`), not a statement about exponents. The terms of the series (`aTerm`, indexed by `GTerm`) and the functions being paired (`PuFun`) were not unfolded. The file's larger result `theoremS_of_conj` comes earlier in the file; by the stated convention the last theorem is the one described.

literature.basis: The statement is a kernel series expansion for objects that exist only in this project's construction (the datum `D7`, a `HidaSetting` for it, the bundle `ConcTie`); nothing in the names or folders marks it as a literature statement. Expansions of this general kind are familiar from Poincaré-series and relative-trace-formula arguments, but this instance is specific to the project.

Formalism.SharpRestriction.GlobalSchurBo.title: Operator-norm bound with a constant depending only on Cn
Formalism.SharpRestriction.GlobalSchurBo.summary: For a fixed real constant Cd there is a function K from reals to reals such that for every constant Cn, every data object D of the project, every real x and every constant Cth: if the theta-factor hypothesis `adm2` holds (at each step i the free theta value equals a fixed local factor, and the average over complex embeddings of the log of its square is at most Cth · f · N_i · N_{i+1} · L), then `Conclusion2` holds with constant K(Cn). `Conclusion2` bounds, for each step i < m and each complex embedding s, the squared operator norm at s of the rational kernel map between the i-th and (i+1)-th Hermitian lattices by the exponential of: a sum over places τ of log of a hook-length quantity of the lifted weight minus its total weight times the log of the period at τ, plus the log of the squared theta factor, plus K(Cn) · f · m² · N_{i+1}² · (L + log T + log(g_0 g_1)); this is required under the size conditions `Nums`, the weight conditions `Wts`, the class-separation condition `ClsTie` and conditions on the kernel data.
Formalism.SharpRestriction.GlobalSchurBo.role: Bookkeeping: it turns the existence statement `VolumeRatio₂` (for each Cn and Cd a constant exists) into a single function of Cn by choice. `VolumeRatio₂` in turn combines the uniform class-count bound `mass_count_uniform_holds` with `opNorm_estimate_of_theta_mass`. The file is named after an earlier, unrelated one-line theorem in it, `log_X_lower_family_of_theorems`, which derives a family input `proportionalityInputFamily` from three lattice-volume hypotheses via `log_X_lower_of_corollary_five_six`.
Formalism.SharpRestriction.GlobalSchurBo.caveat: `adm2`, `Conclusion2`, `Nums`, `Wts`, `ClsTie`, `Conclusion1` and `hook` were read; the objects inside them (the kernel maps `KL`, the lattices `lat`, the periods `Om`, the theta value `thFree`, the conditions on `KerData`) were not unfolded, so their descriptions rest on names and on the shape of the formulas. The described statement is the last theorem of the file, not the one the module is named after.

literature.basis: The bound concerns kernel maps, lattices and weights attached to the project's own data objects (`D7`), and the statement is only a repackaging of constants for such bounds.

FunctorialResolution.EmbeddedResolution..title: Functorial strong resolution of singularities in characteristic zero
FunctorialResolution.EmbeddedResolution..summary: No hypotheses. Conclusion: there is a rule that assigns to every reduced scheme X of finite type over a field k of characteristic zero a finite sequence of blow-ups ending in a scheme X' such that X' is smooth over k, the map from X' to X is proper and is an isomorphism over the smooth locus of X, the preimage of the smooth locus is dense, all blow-up centres lie over the singular locus, and the reduced preimage of the singular locus is a strict normal crossings divisor. The rule commutes with pullback along smooth morphisms and with extension of the base field.
FunctorialResolution.EmbeddedResolution..role: Final assembly of the resolution part of the project: it applies a general theorem that turns a functorial principalization algorithm for ideals on smooth varieties into a resolution rule, using the project's algorithm with radical centres and the affine case proved just above in the same file.

literature.basis: This is Hironaka's theorem in its functorial form (Hironaka 1964; Villamayor, Bierstone–Milman, Włodarczyk, Kollár).

GlobalTheory.ArcCM.known_holds.title: The bundled background facts on abelian varieties all hold
GlobalTheory.ArcCM.known_holds.summary: No hypotheses. The conclusion is the project's bundle `Known`, a structure with 14 fields, each a general statement about polarized abelian schemes and their moduli. The fields are: a list of about 24 algebraic laws for polarized abelian varieties and semi-abelian schemes (rank of global sections, theorem of the cube and of the square, rigidity, Weil pairing and its nondegeneracy, ampleness, Serre-type statements, extension of semi-abelian schemes and cubical structures, quotients, unramified extensions of complete discrete valuation rings); further base-change laws for sections and for the uniformization of degenerating abelian varieties; complex-analytic theta uniformization of a polarized complex abelian variety (lattice, Hermitian form, semi-character, theta functions corresponding to sections, Weil pairing given by the exponential of the Riemann form); existence of moduli spaces with level structure for abelian schemes with an action of the integers of a CM field of signature (p, q), with integral models at every prime, families of complex uniformizations with theta functions with half-integer characteristics, and an archimedean condition on arcs into the toroidal boundary; unique extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes over a discrete valuation ring; a 'key formula' giving a canonical unit attached to a polarized abelian variety with theta section and Lie basis; existence of CM points over number fields; a formula equating twice the degree of a CM eigen-line with a logarithmic period quantity built from a Kronecker character; and well-definedness and base-change laws for evaluating forms at framed points of the moduli space.
GlobalTheory.ArcCM.known_holds.role: Final assembly of a hypothesis bundle: each field is filled by a theorem proved elsewhere in the project (the 'first five laws', the moduli existence theorem, the theta-uniformization theorem, the key formula, CM existence, the eigen-line degree formula, and so on). Its effect is that later results stated conditionally on `Known` become unconditional.
GlobalTheory.ArcCM.known_holds.caveat: I read the definitions of all 14 fields only at the top level; the supporting notions (degeneration data, moduli objects `Moduli`, models, arcs, frames) were not unfolded, so the short descriptions of the moduli, toroidal and 'key formula' fields rest partly on names. The exact strength of each field relative to the literature theorem it resembles was not checked.

literature.basis: The bundle is called `Known` and its fields restate classical theorems in the project's language (theorem of the cube, Weil pairing, Appell-Humbert/theta uniformization, Mumford and Faltings-Chai degeneration theory, moduli of PEL type, a Moret-Bailly style key formula, a Chowla-Selberg type degree formula). The project-specific formulations of the moduli and arc clauses could not be matched to a precise reference.

GlobalTheory.ArithmeticHeightTower.Arake.title: Arithmetic intersection calculus from Poincaré–Lelong and resolution
GlobalTheory.ArithmeticHeightTower.Arake.summary: Hypotheses: the arithmetic Poincaré–Lelong formula in the project's formulation (the integral of the log-norm of a section against Chern forms equals a sum over horizontal components of its divisor minus a correction integral), and embedded resolution of singularities over fields of characteristic zero (a projective variety with a dense open set admits a projectively embedded smooth modification that is an isomorphism over the open set and has normal-crossing coordinates on the complement). Conclusion: the seven-part package `ArCalc` for Hermitian line bundles on arithmetic varieties: existence of heights and of arithmetic and geometric intersection functionals; the effect of changing a metric by a smooth function; the effect of a constant shift of the metric; the inductive formula expressing an intersection number through the height of a divisor minus an archimedean integral; the projection formula for generically finite maps; invariance under isometry and under integer linear combinations; and a second metric-change formula.
GlobalTheory.ArithmeticHeightTower.Arake.role: Assembly of a toolkit statement. It builds a full intersection system from the two hypotheses (`arith_intersection_system_of_poincare_lelong`), proves three intermediate statements in the same file (heights form a polynomial functional, the mixed formula, the projection formula), passes them through `bridge3`, and concludes with `arithIntersectionCalculus_of_form_mixed_projection`.
GlobalTheory.ArithmeticHeightTower.Arake.caveat: The seven components of `ArCalc`, the Poincaré–Lelong statement and the resolution statement were read. The underlying notions `HermLB`, `IsArithVar`, `IsArFun`, `IsArithHeight`, `chInt`, `archInt` were not unfolded, so the paraphrase of each component follows its formula and its name.

literature.basis: The conclusion `ArCalc` sits in the project's `Published` namespace and has the shape of the standard arithmetic intersection theory of Hermitian line bundles (Gillet–Soulé, Bost–Gillet–Soulé); the theorem derives it from two other literature statements. The exact formulation is the project's own.

GlobalTheory.BigOn.ontoX_of_hypotheses_a.title: The 'onto' inequality at family points from twelve published inputs
GlobalTheory.BigOn.ontoX_of_hypotheses_a.summary: Hypotheses: twelve propositions, ten of them in the project's `Published` list and two of the same kind: Green's cuspidal characters of finite general linear groups, Clozel's theorem that regular algebraic cuspidal representations are cohomological, l-adic characters attached to algebraic Hecke characters (two versions), Chebotarev density with degree-one primes, existence of l-adic Galois representations for polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representations over CM fields (`CuspUAlt`), base change for definite unitary groups, Bhatt–Scholze crystalline lattices, rapid decay of cusp forms, existence of a local reciprocity map for GL_n satisfying the project's list of laws, a parametrisation of discrete series, and the Casselman–Wallach theorem. Conclusion `SurjectiveOntoX`: for every parameter family in the project's class `FamHyp` (small ε, large parameters) satisfying a divisor condition `DIVinN`, there is C0 ≥ 0 such that at all sufficiently large points of the family meeting the point conditions, and all C ≥ C0, the numerical condition `ON` holds. `ON` is a system of inequalities at the twisting places: a sum of local index terms at a place and its conjugate is bounded by ramification-weighted main and error terms times a global factor, the error terms are nonnegative, and a weighted sum over places is bounded by a prescribed quantity.
GlobalTheory.BigOn.ontoX_of_hypotheses_a.role: Final assembly of one condition: from the hypotheses it derives global Artin reciprocity and the ray class field statement, then five intermediate project statements (export, twist bound, share, bad places, exponent bound) and feeds them to `ontoX_of_twist_shares_exp_alt`. Some ingredients (the page, geometric, rank, model and share statements) are taken from earlier results that need none of the hypotheses.
GlobalTheory.BigOn.ontoX_of_hypotheses_a.caveat: The definitions of `SurjectiveOntoX`, `ON`, `EventuallyAtPoints`, `FamHyp` and seven of the hypotheses were read; the point data (`Pt`, `More`, the quantities Iw, F0, err0, J0, E1 inside `ON`) were not unfolded, so the inequality is described by shape only. Descriptions of base change, the Hecke 'above' statement and Green's theorem rest on their names.

literature.basis: All hypotheses are literature-labelled statements, but the conclusion is an inequality about point data of this project's parameter families.

GlobalTheory.CarrierGap.theoremS_leaves_.title: Carrier bound and four inputs give the Theorem S hypotheses
GlobalTheory.CarrierGap.theoremS_leaves_.summary: Hypotheses: `CarrierP` (the 'carrier' statement: uniform constants exist such that for every project datum, pair of distinct words u ≠ u' and auxiliary choices meeting the size conditions, the property `CarrierFull` holds); `RowNGP` (a 'non-generic row' bound for kernel rows indexed by pairs of words, with uniform constants); `RowsFinDim` (finite-dimensionality of the range of a product of two operators on L² of an adelic unitary-group quotient, one a finite-level convolution and one built from discrete-series matrix coefficients at the real places); `UniqGap` (two Bessel functionals on the smooth vectors of a discrete series representation of a unitary group U(p,q), whose Harish-Chandra parameter has a large gap, are proportional); `SWXS` (finite volume of the adelic unitary quotient and a Siegel–Weil-type identity in the range 2n < M, in the project's formulation). Nine further side facts appear as instance arguments; all are supplied by instances elsewhere in the project. Conclusion: `TheoremSClosedHypotheses`, a conjunction of 19 project statements (local models, density inputs, row inputs, the carrier and non-generic row statements, convergence and finiteness statements, counting formulas, mass-data inputs, linkage and splitting).
GlobalTheory.CarrierGap.theoremS_leaves_.role: Final collection step before 'Theorem S': each of the 19 conjuncts is supplied either by a hypothesis or by an earlier result (for example independence of a choice from the Bessel uniqueness, decay from the same uniqueness, normalizing constants and mass data from Siegel–Weil). The bundle is exactly the input of `theoremS_of_conj`, which yields the off-diagonal bound ‖K0(u,u')‖² ≤ (1 + b^(−6))·d(u)d(u')/D* for u ≠ u'.
GlobalTheory.CarrierGap.theoremS_leaves_.caveat: The five hypotheses were read at top level; `CarrierFull`, the row predicates and most of the 19 conjuncts of the conclusion were not unfolded, so their one-word descriptions follow their names. Two different definitions named `TheoremSClosedHypotheses` exist; the one meant here (by the opened namespaces and by the shape of the proof) is the 19-fold conjunction in `TheoremSConclusion`.

literature.basis: The conclusion is a bundle of statements about the project's own kernel construction. Two of the hypotheses (Bessel uniqueness, Siegel–Weil) are of literature type, but the statement as a whole is proof-specific bookkeeping.

GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Br.flatD.title: Flat sections exist and have an explicit arithmetic degree
GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Br.flatD.summary: Hypotheses: embedded resolution of singularities in characteristic zero, and a GAGA statement (compatible holomorphic local data on a smooth proper complex variety come from an algebraic section of a line bundle). Conclusion (`FlatDegreeSt`): for every CM field E with a 'host' structure, a Kronecker character χ modulo the host's integer d, a signature datum (p,q), level, moduli data, coefficient field and complex uniformisations satisfying a list of laws, on every component and for every embedding τ in the chosen CM type there is a 'flat section': an invertible section of the line bundle of parallel weight −1 at τ whose norm is constant at each archimedean place and whose valuation is constant at each finite place. Every such section has arithmetic degree (p−q)/2 · Re(γ + log(2π / rootdisc E) − L'(1,χ)/L(1,χ)) + q·(log d − lrd E), where γ is Euler's constant.
GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Br.flatD.role: A reduction. It takes the constant section with zero finite-place defect and degree (p−q)/2 · Re(...) from `exists_const_section_kronecker_char`, renormalises its finite-place data to the required defect, recomputes the degree, and uses the lemma that all such sections on a component have the same degree.
GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Br.flatD.caveat: Read: `FlatDegreeSt`, `FlatDegree`, `FlatExistsAt`, `ConstSec`, `flatWt`, `flDefect_vw`, `flatDegVal`, `logOm`, the `Laws` structure, and both hypotheses. Not unfolded: `Host`, `IsHostField`, `Moduli`, `Unf`, the algebra `Rul` of functions on framed points, and `lrd` (by its name a logarithmic root discriminant). The degree formula has the shape of a Chowla–Selberg type period formula; that identification is mine and is not stated in the code.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are literature statements and the constant resembles known CM period formulas, but the statement itself is about sections on the project's own moduli and uniformisation data and is filed under the project's statements, not its published theorems.

GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Link.goo.title: Good towers exist and the volume theorem holds
GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Link.goo.summary: Hypotheses, ten statements phrased as known results: existence of a full arithmetic intersection system; a triple of arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel type statements; Moriwaki's bigness inequality (arithmetic self-intersection bounded by arithmetic volume); embedded resolution of singularities in characteristic zero; unique extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes over a normal base; a Fargues-type Hodge–Tate statement for p-divisible groups; a GAGA statement for sections of line bundles; a 'line of large degree' statement; quotients of abelian schemes by finite flat subgroups; Zarhin's trick. Conclusion (1): for every CM field, signature (p,q) with p,q ≥ 1 and integral model of the moduli problem that is 'global' with split components, there is a 'root tower' (an index j, finitely many components, a finite set of bad primes, a rational weight, and a projective 'root model' for each bound B and component) together with a good origin with extra local properties. Conclusion (2): there is a universal constant C such that for abelian CM fields, q ≥ 1, 3q+1 ≤ p+q and not too many bad primes, every such tower satisfies six properties: proportionality of geometric intersection numbers to flag-variety degrees, equal volumes of all components, a limit formula for arithmetic intersection numbers, an asymptotic formula with error O(log B / B), and lower bounds for arithmetic self-intersection and for the mean slope in terms of the root discriminant and L'/L(1,χ) of a quadratic character.
GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Link.goo.role: Final assembly for this block: `given_of_use` turns eight of the hypotheses into a list of fourteen working statements, and `GlobalTheory.T.final_theorem_of_inputs_right` is applied to them together with three facts proved without hypotheses (integrability of points from resolution, `topAvoid`, `thetaUnifAV_closed`).
GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Link.goo.caveat: Read: both conclusions, `RootTower` and its predicates (`Proportional`, `VolEq`, `T1`, `ThmB`, `T2`, `MeanSlope`), `GoodOrigin`, `IsGlobal`, and seven of the ten hypotheses. Not unfolded: `RootModel`, `Host`, `Datum`, `Moduli`, `Model`, the three components of `HSUse` and the 'line of large degree' statement, which are described from names.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are named after published results (Moriwaki, Zarhin, GAGA, resolution of singularities), but the conclusion is about 'root towers' and 'good origins', which are objects of this project; the volume and slope bounds are not a named theorem.

GlobalTheory.ConjClassSum.conj_lifts.title: Theta lifts of Galois-conjugate data have conjugate cusp-form expansions
GlobalTheory.ConjClassSum.conj_lifts.summary: Setting: the project's data type D with a family of characters indexed by tuples t in a finite set, real data R, a face F, weights κ, vectors v₀, 'one-map' data O, phases ph, and an index i. Hypotheses: a chart-independence statement for germs of sections (`ChartIndepSt2`), a size inequality 8·f·r + 4 ≤ nV, and several tie and pinning conditions on the data. Conclusion: for every field automorphism τ of C that fixes the base data (the coefficient field, the host CM field, a CM curve, and certain character values), there is a root of unity ζ0 such that for any two tuples t, t' that are τ-conjugate (same quadratic datum, character of t' equal to τ applied to the character of t) there is an idele s with the following property: for τ-conjugate definite forms y, y', the theta-lift function ph_i·θ(t, y) is a finite linear combination of the reference cusp-form family, and whenever it has coefficients a_k, the lift for (t', y') has coefficients ζ0 · ξ_{t'}(s) · τ(a_k) on the same family.
GlobalTheory.ConjClassSum.conj_lifts.role: A Galois-equivariance statement for the theta lifts used in the construction. The proof normalises the data over a normal coefficient field, then combines an earlier 'one-map' result at core constants, a result that conjugating a theta class sum gives a root of unity times the conjugate tuple's sum, and descent of conjugate definite forms to a number field.
GlobalTheory.ConjClassSum.conj_lifts.caveat: The predicates `ConjFun`, `ConjTup`, `ConjForm`, `FixBase`, `IsRoot1` were read; the function `thF` was taken to be a theta lift from its name and the file name, and `ChartIndepSt2`, `OMPins`, `PhaseTie`, `FWTie`, `IoExt`, `QGuard`, `ExtC` were not unfolded.

literature.basis: Rationality and Galois-equivariance of theta lifts is a known theme (Shimura, Harris), but this statement is formulated for the project's own data and one-map normalisations and I found no marker tying it to a published theorem.

GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.Exh.Top.downNe_k_of.title: Theta lift to a smaller unitary group is nonzero
GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.Exh.Top.downNe_k_of.summary: Hypotheses: `DM`, a doubling-method package (meromorphic continuation with finite pole orders of Siegel Eisenstein series on the doubled unitary group, the basic identity for the doubling zeta integral of two cusp forms, and continuation of that integral); and `SimplePole`, which says that a partial L-function whose unramified parameters have 'lift shape' (r bounded parameters, twisted, together with a string of length t ≥ r+5) has a simple pole at s = (1+t)/2. Conclusion: for every master record D for which the Euler-product identity `EulerRight` holds (unramified doubling integrals yield the partial L-function divided by a normalising factor), the property `DownNe` holds. `DownNe` says: for a positive definite Hermitian space A and a Hermitian space W of positive rank with rank A = rank W + t, a cusp form u on U(A) invariant under a principal level subgroup whose unramified parameters have lift shape, and a Fock-type Schwartz function Φ whose archimedean matching integral is nonzero, the theta lift of u to U(W) is not identically zero.
GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.Exh.Top.downNe_k_of.role: Direct application of `downNe_of_core`, with the project's proven residue statement `resCore` substituted for one of its hypotheses. It is a bookkeeping step that removes a hypothesis.
GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.Exh.Top.downNe_k_of.caveat: `DownNe`, `NoLift`, `Form`, `Occ`, `Defin`, `Places`, `EulerRight`, `DM` and `SimplePole` were read. The meaning of the Weil-representation datum, the Fock and spherical conditions on Φ and the theta-lift operator `up` is taken from names.

literature.basis: The shape matches the known criterion relating poles of L-functions and nonvanishing of theta lifts via the doubling method (Rallis inner product formula; Kudla–Rallis; Ginzburg–Jiang–Soudry), but the statement is phrased for the project's records and is conditional on two hypothesis bundles, so I cannot match it to a specific published theorem.

GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.ScalarsRow.scalars.title: Theta-chain steps scale inner products by positive L-value multiples
GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.ScalarsRow.scalars.summary: Hypotheses: seven statements named after published results (covers by discrete series, Harish-Chandra finiteness, Harish-Chandra modules, Casselman–Wallach, rapid decay of cusp forms, Howe duality in the unramified case, the unramified doubling computation for GL), plus the unitary Siegel–Weil formula and continuation of Siegel Eisenstein series; the project's 'Hecke form' statement for every master datum (a Rallis-type formula expressing the Petersson pairing of two theta lifts through a value of a partial L-function); the standing conditions `Given` on the real datum R and a face F (a core package, existence of parameters, absolute irreducibility of characters, type and guard conditions, and gaps of size at least 100·r^4 between consecutive Harish-Chandra parameters); and a condition on the host field. Conclusion (`Scalars`): there are positive constants κ_1..κ_m such that for every label t and every Hecke eigensystem c with nonzero row part, an L-function parameter exists, and at each step k of the chain of m theta lifts there is a positive real number l, the value of a partial twisted L-function at the point (1+T)/2, where T is a rank parameter of the master datum, such that every vector reached at step k lifts to step k+1 and the lift multiplies inner products by κ_{k+1}·l; the same holds for the last step into the top space.
GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.ScalarsRow.scalars.role: A wrapper: it forwards to the preceding lemma `scalars_of_heckeFormNS`, which applies the project theorem `thetaChain_steps_positive_multiple_of_LValue` after deducing a separation of Harish-Chandra parameters from the cubic gap. The Siegel–Weil, Eisenstein-continuation and host-field hypotheses appear in the signature but are not used.
GlobalTheory.Core.Rk.ScalarsRow.scalars.caveat: The seven literature hypotheses were identified from their names only. The spaces in the conclusion (`MMap`, the 'row part', the multiplicity inner product) and the bundle `Given` were read at the level of their definitions without unfolding the underlying real datum.

literature.basis: It is conditional on literature-named hypotheses and on a project statement, and concludes a scaling property of the project's own chain of theta lifts; the general type (Rallis inner product formula) is classical, the statement is not.

GlobalTheory.CovTop.FlatDegProof.flatDeg.title: Flat-section degree formula along the project's families
GlobalTheory.CovTop.FlatDegProof.flatDeg.summary: Hypothesis: `PublishedHodgeBundleTheorems`, a bundle of 28 assumed literature statements (toroidal compactification, volume and nefness statements, de Rham and Dieudonné theory, class field theory, semistable reduction, strong approximation, Chern–Weil, Kawamata–Viehweg and Nadel vanishing, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel, heights of cycles, resolution and algebraisation, and others). Conclusion: `FlatDegreeCondition`: for all sufficiently small ε and all sufficiently large members of the project's families of data, at every construction point, every index i below the top one and every 'good' cover Y, the flat-degree property holds for the uniformisation attached to Y. That property says that on each component and for each CM type component a flat section exists and every flat section has the same degree, equal to ((p − q)/2)·log Ω + q·(log d − log of the root discriminant of E), where (p, q) is the signature and log Ω = γ + log(2π / root discriminant) − Re L'(1,χ)/L(1,χ) for the quadratic character χ.
GlobalTheory.CovTop.FlatDegProof.flatDeg.role: Bookkeeping lift: the pointwise formula is the earlier statement `FlatDegreeSt`, obtained from `flat_tensor_swap_isIso`, and is transported to the 'eventually along families' form with trivial constants. The lemma producing `FlatDegreeSt` discards its three arguments, so the literature bundle is not actually used in this proof.
GlobalTheory.CovTop.FlatDegProof.flatDeg.caveat: `FlatSec` (flat section) and its degree, the cover structure `Cov`, `GoodCov` and the family class `FamHyp` were not unfolded in detail. The sign convention of the degree was read off two nested definitions and should be checked before quoting. The 28 field names of the hypothesis bundle were read, not their definitions.

literature.basis: The conclusion is stated for the project's own families, construction points and covers. The underlying degree formula is of Chowla–Selberg / Colmez type, but it is proved inside the project and not taken from the literature bundle.

GlobalTheory.CovTop.GoodDom.weight_latti.title: Integral cusp forms of dominant weight span all cusp forms
GlobalTheory.CovTop.GoodDom.weight_latti.summary: Hypotheses: the bundle `PublishedHodgeBundleTheorems` (28 named literature statements, among them toroidal compactification, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel, Kawamata–Viehweg, Nadel vanishing, semistable reduction, strong approximation); a master datum D of the project with its core package T; an index j whose Hermitian datum has signature (p, q) with p, q ≥ 1; a 'deep' cover Y of the j-th unitary moduli space (larger coefficient field, extra level) satisfying the project's goodness conditions with parameters (e, o); the CM field has degree at least 6 over the rationals; and a weight λ whose rows are non-increasing with a gap of at least 1 between positions p and p+1. Conclusion: inside the space of cusp forms of weight λ on Y (a vector space over the coefficient field), the lattice of integral forms, those with nonnegative valuation at every valuation of the project's set attached to finite places, spans the whole space. Equivalently, every such cusp form has a nonzero scalar multiple that is integral.
GlobalTheory.CovTop.GoodDom.weight_latti.role: A bounded-denominators step. It combines an earlier result that some power of a form times an auxiliary form is cuspidal of a matched weight, a result that a suitable multiple of that product has nonnegative valuations, and an algebraic lemma passing from integrality of a power to integrality of a multiple of the form. Together with finite generation (previous lemma) it gives the regularity of the weight lattice used next in the file.
GlobalTheory.CovTop.GoodDom.weight_latti.caveat: The 'deep cover', its goodness conditions (about 14 clauses) and the valuation set defining integrality were read only at the level of their declarations. The space of cusp forms is the project's `cuspW`, defined by holomorphy conditions on uniformizations, which I did not unfold further.

literature.basis: The statement is conditional on a bundle of literature theorems and concludes a property of lattices of cusp forms on the project's own covers of unitary moduli spaces; no standard reference states it in this form.

GlobalTheory.DeRham.charpoly_push_eq.title: Characteristic polynomial on de Rham homology equals the l-adic one
GlobalTheory.DeRham.charpoly_push_eq.summary: Let k be an algebraically closed field, A an abelian scheme over k, and f an endomorphism of A as a group scheme. Suppose L is a free ℤ-module of finite rank with an endomorphism φ, l is a prime invertible in k, and for each j there is a map ev_j from L to A(k) that is additive, intertwines φ with f, has kernel exactly l^j·L and image exactly the l^j-torsion points; so L with φ models the l-adic Tate module of A with the action of f. Assume the de Rham homology of A (defined as the dual of the primitive part of first de Rham cohomology) is finite-dimensional over k. Conclusion: the characteristic polynomial of the map induced by f on de Rham homology equals the characteristic polynomial of φ, with coefficients mapped from ℤ to k.
GlobalTheory.DeRham.charpoly_push_eq.role: Combines two earlier results: the lattice model computes the project's integer characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of an abelian variety (`l_power_torsion_endomorphism_evaluation`), and that integer polynomial maps to the characteristic polynomial on de Rham homology (proved separately in characteristic p and characteristic 0). A short assembly after packaging A as an abelian variety.
GlobalTheory.DeRham.charpoly_push_eq.caveat: The de Rham homology `HdR` and the pushforward were traced to a dual of primitive classes in a first cohomology group for the trivial divided-power structure; the underlying cohomology definition and `IsAbelianScheme` were not unfolded further.

literature.basis: This is the classical independence of the characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of an abelian variety from the cohomology theory (l-adic Tate module versus de Rham or crystalline H^1; in general Katz–Messing), stated with an explicit lattice model for the Tate module.

GlobalTheory.Fc.StageOneU.member_bundles.title: Mass ratio, staged membership and bundle existence from literature bundle
GlobalTheory.Fc.StageOneU.member_bundles.summary: Hypotheses: a bundle `UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses` of about sixty propositions, almost all named after published theorems (Clozel, Chebotarev, global Artin reciprocity, Siegel–Weil, doubling method, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, Harish-Chandra, Casselman–Wallach, discrete series classification, strong approximation, local Tate duality, and others); a project-specific 'row rationality' condition `RowRat`; existence of a local reciprocity map for GL_n satisfying the project's laws; a real number cDep; and a property A of twisted base data that holds for all sufficiently large bases. Conclusion, three parts: (1) the Siegel mass ratio for CM fields: for an 'unramified' CM field and M ≥ 3, the ratio of the masses of the standard Hermitian lattices of ranks M and M−1 equals an explicit expression; (2) `MemberE` for the slot system built from a specific 'extension' (the origin extension with parameter cDep, restricted by A): a base condition plus three construction stages (a core exists, it exports, and a second pass produces a good core); (3) eventually, at every good point of that slot system there exists a bundle satisfying the linkage `BundleLinkage`.
GlobalTheory.Fc.StageOneU.member_bundles.role: An assembly step: it unpacks the hypothesis bundle and combines earlier results (`compatibleSystem_member_hypotheses`, rational weights, weight-one saturation, multiplicative closure of members, existence of a base lattice, and non-emptiness of Weil blocks) to produce the three outputs for the restricted extension.
GlobalTheory.Fc.StageOneU.member_bundles.caveat: The structure of `MemberE` (`BaseCond`, `FirstG`, `ExportF`, `SecondG`), `ExBL`, the mass ratio statement and the field list of the hypothesis bundle were read; the construction objects (slots, cores, stages, the two extensions, `BundleLinkage`, `RowRat`) were not unfolded to ordinary mathematics. The phrase 'large unramified exponents' in the name is not reflected in anything I could identify in the statement.

literature.basis: Part (1) is a classical mass-formula statement, but parts (2) and (3) are existence statements about the project's own staged construction, conditional on literature hypotheses.

GlobalTheory.FinMatch.exists_finite_plac.title: Two theta lifts to one unitary group match
GlobalTheory.FinMatch.exists_finite_plac.summary: Hypotheses: a bundle `ThetaLocalInputs` of about 50 statements named after published theorems (Howe duality, Weil representation, discrete series, doubling method and others); a project statement `LocalMatching` saying that matched local data exist for every admissible triple; and a concrete setting: three Hermitian spaces A, A', W over the CM extension of the project's global datum with rank A + rank A' = rank W, Weil representations for the pairs (A, W) and (A', W) attached to Hecke characters α and β, a condition that α/β is ramified exactly at places below a given finite set, and test vectors f, f' of the required finite type. Conclusion: there is a single irreducible module Π for the unitary group of W (finite adelic part together with Lie algebra actions at the infinite places) and maps p, p' from the two Weil representation spaces onto coinvariant quotients in Π, such that for suitable polynomials P, P' the vectors built from f and P and from f' and P' have the same nonzero image in Π.
GlobalTheory.FinMatch.exists_finite_plac.role: Existence of an object with a comparison: it builds local lattice data at the ramified places, applies `LocalMatching` to get local models, assembles a restricted tensor product, and uses earlier results (surjectivity, equivariance and irreducibility of the triple assembly) to check the properties; it is then used for the theorem `finite_place_theta_matching` in the same file.
GlobalTheory.FinMatch.exists_finite_plac.caveat: The predicates `IsMatch`, `IsTriple`, `Tri.Is` were read, but the notions under them (coinvariant map, 'Fock' vectors, finite type of test vectors) were not unfolded, so 'theta lift' is my reading of the structure. The literature bundle was read as field names only.

literature.basis: The statement is conditional on literature inputs but concludes a matching between objects defined inside the project's construction (its global datum, its triples of Hermitian spaces and test vectors).

GlobalTheory.FlipRun.cuspStep_of_large_f.title: Theta lifts along grid arrows preserve cusp forms
GlobalTheory.FlipRun.cuspStep_of_large_f.summary: Hypotheses: `LiftsCuspidal`, a project statement that for every datum the theta lifts between neighbouring unitary groups of the project's grid send cuspidal functions to cuspidal functions (in a multiplicity form and a smooth form), and `ThetaLocalInputs`, a bundle of sixteen published statements (Bernstein-Zelevinsky finiteness, Bernstein irreducibility, the geometric lemma, Jacquet-Shalika, finiteness of automorphic forms on GL_n, temperedness of cohomological conjugate-self-dual representations, Galois representations of polarised cuspidal representations, local-global compatibility above l, purity, global Artin reciprocity, l-adic Hecke characters, de Rham implies potentially semistable, Chebotarev and others). Conclusion, for all sufficiently large scales and every admissible 'choice' in the project's Hida-type setting: for every index t and every system of Haar measures and fundamental domains on the grid of unitary groups, and for every arrow of the grid (rightward or downward), every local test vector and Fock-model polynomial, and every smooth cuspidal automorphic function F on the source group that is 'listed', the theta-kernel integral defining the lift of F converges and the lift is again a smooth, cuspidal, listed automorphic function on the target group.
GlobalTheory.FlipRun.cuspStep_of_large_f.role: It first derives smoothness of cuspidal lifts at the cusps, then joins two earlier results, one for rightward arrows (`cusp_transition_rightward`) and one for downward arrows (`flipRun_descending_cusp_transition`), into a single statement for all grid arrows. A case-merging step.
GlobalTheory.FlipRun.cuspStep_of_large_f.caveat: `CuspStep`, `Big`, `Vol`, `liftA`, `LiftConv`, `IsGridArrow`, `LiftsCuspidal` and `ThetaLocalInputs` were read. The grid data (`GridData`, the Weil-representation data `W`, `RealMatch`, the `HidaSetting` conditions) and the predicates 'listed', `IsAutFunSm`, `IsCuspFun`, `IsLocVec` were not unfolded; that the nodes are unitary groups of Hermitian spaces and that the kernel is a theta kernel is inferred from the surrounding definitions and names. The individual entries of `ThetaLocalInputs` are described by their names only.

literature.basis: Preservation of cuspidality under theta lifts in a tower is a classical theme (Rallis), but this statement concerns the project's own grid of spaces, levels and 'listed' functions and is conditional on a project-specific hypothesis in addition to published ones.

GlobalTheory.HeightCounting.Up.all_stage.title: All stages of a level-by-level construction hold at every state
GlobalTheory.HeightCounting.Up.all_stage.summary: Hypotheses: Casselman–Wallach, Harish-Chandra modules, the Weil representation for unitary pairs, existence and uniqueness of discrete series for U(p,q), two bundles of further inputs (`MultiplicityCoverHypotheses`, `PublishedInputsThirdLayerAlt`, mostly literature-named statements plus two project-specific multiplicity conditions), a bundle `SerN` of six series rationality and Hecke integrality conditions, existence of a local reciprocity map, an 'archimedean comparison' bundle, and a 'point statement'. Conclusion: a conjunction of thirteen statements, each quantified over all 'states' x of the project's construction at eventually-all large bases. They assert that successive levels of data over a state can be produced: a level with the same Galois data exists; multiplicity, rationality and cuspidality data exist; from an intermediate level one gets a first, then second, then third intermediate level (each adding one more piece of data); the final level's character data is non-empty; a finiteness statement holds; and, for every real cDep, the three level-raising steps and the finiteness step also hold in a version that preserves a list condition.
GlobalTheory.HeightCounting.Up.all_stage.role: A collecting step: each conjunct is taken from an earlier result (`sMt_of_published_inputs'`, `sRat_of_isotInternal_inputs`, `sCusp_of_parSt_alt_alt`, the three `...ExistList_of_inputs_serN` results, `stage_c_nonempty_of_prints_third_layer`, `sFin_and_sFinl_of_archCmp_sEta_thetaData`, and others) and the list versions at cDep = 0 give the plain versions.
GlobalTheory.HeightCounting.Up.all_stage.caveat: The level structures (`SameGaloisLevel`, `IntermediateLevel`, first/second/third levels, `StrictHenselianAcyclicLevel`) were read only as records whose fields are further project data; states, `ListSt`, the hypotheses `ArchimedeanComparison'` and `PointStatement` were not unfolded. Names such as 'strict henselian acyclic' and 'height counting' do not match anything visible in the definitions and should not be taken literally.

literature.basis: The statement is about levels and states of this project's construction; only its hypotheses are literature statements.

GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.inputsNet_re.title: Input bundle with finite net for the extended point system
GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.inputsNet_re.summary: The statement asserts the existence of an absolute constant CL and two real functions Cq and Z₀ of two variables such that the following holds for every master record D, every 'Top' record T over D satisfying the law bundle `LawsP`, every index j with 1 ≤ j ≤ m, all weights ka, wL, wF and numerical parameters. If the parameter conditions `ParOK` and page conditions `PageOK` hold and the base size is at least Z₀(CA, CK), then (a) the bundle `InputsNet` holds, with explicit constants (1, 4, Cq(CA,CK), 4, 7), for the recorded graded system of cusp forms at step j after its point sets have been enlarged to all valuation points, and (b) the support conditions `PageSupp` hold. `InputsNet` is a large conjunction: base hypotheses (a lattice condition, a lower bound for log sup-norms of integral forms, a recursive lattice bound when j < m), existence of a family G of global forms together with a finite net of bounded log-cardinality, about a dozen tie, share and domination conditions on G, and local point data at every finite place satisfying a combined valuation bound and height bounds.
GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.inputsNet_re.role: Assembly step. It combines about ten earlier results (absolute lower bound for log sup-norms of integral forms, recursive page lattice bound, polynomial domination, run hypotheses from parameter conditions, existence of admissible theta lattice generators and of an auxiliary scalar-weight form, share statements for cusp-form bases split into the cases j < m and j = m, a combined bound for run scalars, a net construction, existence of prime data with height bounds) and then transfers them from the recorded system to the one with extended points.
GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.inputsNet_re.caveat: I unfolded `InputsNet`, `BaseIn`, `FamIn`, `PtIn`, `NetIn`, `PageOK`, `ParOK`, `PageSupp` and the graded-forms structure `PJ` one or two levels, but not their leaves (`HypC`, `LatAt`, `TiedW`, `ShareRd`, `PolyDom`, `CombBound`, `Heights`, ...). The descriptions of those leaves, and of the ingredients in the proof, rest on names.

literature.basis: Every object in the statement (the master record, the recorded graded system of forms, the extended point system, the page and tie conditions) exists only inside this project's construction.

GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.sharesAt_all.title: Cusp-form generators share a basis with controlled index counts
GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.sharesAt_all.summary: Setting: a master datum D of the project, its top-level package T satisfying the law bundle `LawsP`, a level j between 1 and m, size data, numerical constants, three weights (κ, w_L, w_F) and integers. Hypotheses: parameter conditions `ParOK`; the 'page' numerical conditions `PageOK`; the bundle `HypC` (eight groups of conditions on parameters, scalars and a weighted prime sum); the integral cusp forms of weight κ form a lattice; a family datum G (a finite list of cusp forms of weight w_L and auxiliary forms) that is admissible, meaning the forms generate the designated integral lattice, are few, have no common zero, and satisfy a lower bound on their size; an auxiliary form condition when j < m; and a set Sh spanning the cusp forms of weight w_F. Conclusion (`SharesAt`): there are a number δ and forms θ'_1..θ'_δ taken from Sh such that, however the remaining slots of the family datum are filled, at every finite place the images of the θ' form a basis of a local quotient module; δ times a binomial coefficient is at most the rank of the weight-κ lattice; two auxiliary dimensions are at most 22·(dim)^2·rank/T; and the span of a 'highly vanishing' subspace of weight-κ forms is contained in the span of monomials in the generators times the θ' together with an auxiliary family.
GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.sharesAt_all.role: Case assembly: for j < m it is the 'indefinite' theorem `cuspFormBasisShares_indefinite_liftIndex`, for j = m the 'definite' one, both proved elsewhere. It supplies one of the inputs to the theorem `inputsNet_recPlus` that follows it in the file.
GlobalTheory.InputsAtRecord.sharesAt_all.caveat: The hypotheses are deep project bundles (`LawsP`, `ParOK`, `PageOK`, `HypC`, `GenOK`, `EtaOK`) that I read only at the level of field names, and the objects in the conclusion (the local quotient modules, the families `zAll` and `MggK`, the rank `rhoP`) were read one level deep. The summary of the conclusion follows the definition of `SharesAt` literally; its mathematical purpose is not established.

literature.basis: Every object in the statement belongs to the project's internal construction of cusp-form lattices and family data; nothing corresponds to a named theorem.

GlobalTheory.LocalRows.sLp_sO_hTF_of_sie.title: Three selection conditions follow from the unitary Siegel–Weil formula
GlobalTheory.LocalRows.sLp_sO_hTF_of_sie.summary: Hypothesis: the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups in the convergent range, in the project's formulation (for a CM extension E/F and a nondegenerate Hermitian form in M variables, the unitary quotient has finite volume, and for 2n < M the average of theta series over representations of a Hermitian matrix T equals a product of local densities). Conclusion: for every 'slot' Q (a predicate on stages of the project's construction) and every linkage Lk attaching bundles of data to construction points, three conditions hold. They say that for every family class and every selection of bundles built at points of slot Q: (1) a 'loop row' bound holds, i.e. certain kernel rows indexed by pairs of words are small relative to a threshold; (2) the 'Theorem S' off-diagonal estimate holds for distinct words u ≠ u', bounding the squared norm of a kernel entry by (1 + b^(-6)) · d(u)d(u')/D*; (3) a 'frame' lower bound holds for the family. Each is asserted eventually along the family, for small enough ε and large enough parameters.

GlobalTheory.NLinkE.main_alt_alt.title: Congruence bound holds eventually along a parameter family

GlobalTheory.RowTestAssembly.test_vector.title: Rational separating functionals for theta rows at every datum

GlobalTheory.SqTower.tower_alt_bis.title: Theta constant ratios along the Witt tower via Hecke L-values
GlobalTheory.SqTower.tower_alt_bis.summary: Hypotheses: a bundle `ThetaLocalInputs` of 53 statements named after published theorems (Howe duality, Weil representation, Siegel–Weil, Rallis inner product, doubling method, discrete series, Bernstein–Zelevinsky and others); two project statements on theta integrals for pairs of unitary groups (`ThetaIntegralsAgree`, `LocalMatching`); and `LNe`, non-vanishing of certain Hecke L-functions at a range of integers. Conclusion (`Tower`), in the project's large-parameter regime: for every grid datum, labels t and base label μ0, indices i, j, suppose c and c0 are the constants relating the 'big' and 'small' theta-kernel integrals at t and at μ0, and c0(·) is the constant of a bottom-stage triangle, and Λ, Λ0 are the entire Hecke L-functions of two explicit Hecke characters. Then (c/c0) times a product of q ratios Λ(n)/Λ0(n) at consecutive integers equals an algebraic number that is a unit away from a fixed integer, times a product of p+q 'step ratios' (each again such a unit times ratios of divisors of prime powers), times the ratio of bottom constants, times a product of p ratios Λ(n)/Λ0(n) at other integers. Here p and q are about (m−j)/2.
GlobalTheory.SqTower.tower_alt_bis.role: Assembly by descent along the tower: it combines a top-stage norm formula, a factorisation of stage constants, norm-step results for small and large rank, and a comparison at the bottom stage (all proved elsewhere under the same hypotheses), then cancels using the non-vanishing of the L-values.
GlobalTheory.SqTower.tower_alt_bis.caveat: The kernel integrals defining the constants, the notions of grid datum, matching and bottom triangle were read only at the level of their definitions' headers; the description of the hypotheses `ThetaIntegralsAgree` and `LocalMatching` rests partly on their names. literature.basis: The statement is conditional on literature hypotheses and concludes an identity between constants of the project's own theta-tower construction, of the general type of a Rallis inner product formula but not a statement found in the literature.

GlobalTheory.SupFull.bdd_mem_span_shortG.title: Bounded automorphic sections are spanned by short theta series
GlobalTheory.SupFull.bdd_mem_span_shortG.summary: Setting: a CM field E, a unitary PEL moduli problem over it with level structure, a coefficient field with a 'good' complex embedding sigma, and a complex uniformisation of the moduli space by finitely many components, each given by a Hermitian form, a lattice and an arithmetic group, of rank r at least 1. Hypotheses include chart-independence of certain power-series expressions (`ChartIndepSt2`), triviality of one level parameter, all components sharing the same Hermitian form, the arithmetic groups containing the principal congruence subgroups, technical conditions on an auxiliary level datum d, a dominant weight a with n even and n at least 4[E:Q]r + 4, triviality of the automorphy character on the arithmetic groups, and total definedness of the 'short values' (`ShortValTot`). Conclusion: every tuple of functions on the components that are holomorphic, equivariant of the weight determined by (a, n), have bounded pointwise Petersson-type norm, and vanish outside the domain, lies in the complex span of the uniformisation readings of the short generators, i.e. of those algebraic sections of weight (a, n) whose values are given by short theta-type sums attached to a unimodular rank-n Hermitian lattice, a level and a harmonic polynomial.
GlobalTheory.SupFull.bdd_mem_span_shortG.role: The main spanning step of this file. It moves all components to one level family, identifies readings of short generators with classical theta series, uses invariance of pulled-back bounded sections under a stabiliser, applies a result that stable forms are sums of theta series with free lower rows, and rewrites harmonic rows as integral harmonic polynomials; the next theorem in the file uses it to get a span statement over the coefficient field.
GlobalTheory.SupFull.bdd_mem_span_shortG.caveat: `IsBddSec`, `IsSec`, `Unf`, `IsUnf`, `rdU`, `laU`, `shortGen`, `ShortValTot`, `HasPrinc`, `ChiOne`, `Dom` and `ChartIndepSt2` were read. GlobalTheory.SupFull.fullAt_of_pins.title: Integral cusp forms form a full finitely generated lattice
GlobalTheory.SupFull.fullAt_of_pins.summary: Hypotheses: a project datum D, a 'core' T over it (moduli data with a coefficient number field F, complex uniformisations for each index j and each embedding of F, and related dictionaries), the pinning conditions on the parameters of T, an index j with 1 ≤ j ≤ m, the condition that the uniformisation at index j and the base embedding is a genuine uniformisation (`IsUnf`), and a weight w for index j with positive parallel part n. Finite generation uses finite-dimensionality of the cusp form space and, for each non-zero form, evaluation at a suitable CM point with bounded denominators; spanning uses that a power-type multiple of any cusp form lies in the span of a short explicit datum and that some non-zero scalar multiple is integral. It supplies the lattice statement used later for all weights (`FullKappa`).

GlobalTheory.T.exists_member_of_construc.title: Slot-system membership from two passes of construction steps

Conclusion: `MemberE S`, a four-part statement: the base condition holds, a built core exists in the untwisted case, built cores export, and after retwisting there is a core that is built, has all twists admissible, and is good.

GlobalTheory.T.exists_short_integral_vec.title: Short integral cusp form with non-degenerate level determinant

GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.title: Mumford-type uniformisation from degeneration data over complete normal base
GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.summary: Let R be a local domain that is noetherian, integrally closed, complete for its maximal ideal, and of characteristic zero. Let D be degeneration data over R relative to the maximal ideal: a polarized abelian scheme over R with a rigidified, cubical, symmetric line bundle, a free abelian group X of finite rank mapping additively to its points, and trivialisations ψ(χ) of the pulled-back inverse line bundle at the generic point, with ψ even, the associated τ bimultiplicative, ψ(χ) lying in the maximal ideal for χ ≠ 0, and ψ(χ) lying in the n-th power of the maximal ideal for all but finitely many χ. Then there exist a commutative group scheme G over Spec R that is semi-abelian and a polarized abelian variety A over the fraction field such that G is uniformised by D: G is smooth and separated with generic fibre A, compatibly with line bundles, its reductions modulo powers of the maximal ideal are related to the abelian part and the torus with character group X, and sections of powers of the line bundle correspond bijectively to theta-type expansions.
GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.role: A restatement under the project's theorem namespace of `GlobalTheory.Mum.has_of_base`. That proof reduces the data to a factor of unitary PEL type, passes to a finite extension carrying a labelled cover, obtains the uniformisation there, descends along the finite extension, and cuts out the required factor by an idempotent.
GlobalTheory.T.hasSemiAbelianUniformisat.caveat: `Base`, `AdmBase`, `Has`, `DegPre`, `DegData` and the first fields of `UnifPre` were read; the remaining fields of the uniformisation structure (compatibilities at each thickening and the expansion bijection `ExpBij`) were only skimmed, and `IsSemiAbelian`, `PolAV`, `CubicalStr` were taken at face value.

literature.basis: The statement has the form of Mumford's construction of degenerating abelian varieties over a complete normal base (Mumford 1972; Faltings–Chai, Chapter III), and the project's namespace `Mum` points to it; the exact packaging of 'uniformised' is the project's own, so the match is not verified in detail.

GlobalTheory.T.volume_theorem_of_inputs.title: Volume theorem for towers over unitary moduli, from ten inputs
