GlobalTheory.UChartJoin.rigidForFan_of_u.title: Smooth toroidal model with rigid boundary charts, from compactification
GlobalTheory.UChartJoin.rigidForFan_of_u.summary: Hypothesis: the statement `UStB`, i.e. for every unitary PEL moduli space and admissible polyhedral cone decomposition φ there is a projective normal compactification, its normalized blow-up along a boundary ideal with the right vanishing orders, and a separation property. Conclusion (`RigidForFan`): in the same setting there is a normal projective model Y over the coefficient field carrying a semi-abelian family that extends the universal abelian variety, with an effective Cartier divisor, such that Y is smooth of the expected dimension, its boundary is a strict normal crossings divisor, the divisor is supported on the boundary, every boundary point has a formal chart (a power series ring in which the boundary is a product of coordinates, the degeneration is monomial with forms from a cone of φ, and the divisor is the corresponding monomial), a combination of the determinant bundle and the divisor is ample, and every closed boundary point has a 'rigid' chart: a first-order deformation of the chart that keeps the degeneration data constant is trivial.
GlobalTheory.UChartJoin.rigidForFan_of_u.role: A reduction between two packaged statements: from the compactification it obtains charts at boundary points, a model structure, and smoothness with normal crossings boundary from three earlier theorems, then transports the divisor and the ampleness along an isomorphism by a computation in the Picard group.
GlobalTheory.UChartJoin.rigidForFan_of_u.caveat: The definitions of `RigidForFan`, `HasChartOf` and `HasRigidChart` were read; the inner notions (monomial degeneration, `IsRigid`, `IsConstAlong`) were followed only one level, and the plain-language reading of rigidity is an interpretation.

literature.basis: The conclusion resembles known properties of smooth toroidal compactifications of PEL Shimura varieties (Faltings–Chai, Lan), and the chart notion sits in the project's `PublishedTheorems` folder, but the implication is between two project-specific packages and the rigidity clause was not matched to a published statement.

GlobalTheory.UPel.HT.model_nonempty.title: Unitary PEL moduli problem has a smooth quasi-projective model
GlobalTheory.UPel.HT.model_nonempty.summary: Let p be a prime and D a PEL datum of unitary type: a CM field F containing an imaginary quadratic element whose minimal polynomial splits modulo p, an order O of rank m^2 over the integers of F with an involution of the second kind and split at p, an O-lattice with an alternating form that is perfect up to a factor prime to p, and signature data given by a set of `a` complex embeddings. Let R be a Noetherian ring in which every integer prime to p is invertible, with base data (a root of the quadratic and homomorphisms from the integers of F to R that are pairwise distinct in every characteristic-p fibre), and let N be at least 3 and prime to p. Then there exists a model: a scheme X quasi-projective over Spec R and smooth of relative dimension a(n-1), carrying a universal object (an abelian scheme with O-action, a symmetric rigidified relatively ample line bundle giving a polarisation of degree prime to p and compatible with the involution, a Lie-algebra condition of the prescribed signature, and a level-N structure compatible with the Weil pairing) such that every such object over any R-scheme is the pullback of the universal one along a unique morphism.
GlobalTheory.UPel.HT.model_nonempty.role: Final assembly of the representability statement: it combines the existence of a quasi-projective representing family (`exists_quasiProjective_harrisTaylor_family`) with the smoothness and relative-dimension computation for such a family (`smoothOfRelativeDimension_repFam_of_isQProjOver`).
GlobalTheory.UPel.HT.model_nonempty.caveat: The structures `Datum`, `Base`, `Obj` and `Model` were read in full; auxiliary notions inside `Obj` (line bundles on the product, `LieMult`, the Weil-pairing predicate) were taken at the level of their signatures.

literature.basis: This is the representability, quasi-projectivity and smoothness of the integral model of a unitary PEL Shimura variety at a prime of good reduction with level at least 3 prime to p (Kottwitz 1992; the case used by Harris-Taylor, after whom the project names it), which rests on Mumford's construction of moduli of polarised abelian schemes.

GlobalTheory.UPoincTop.uPoinStX_sep.title: Compactifications of unitary moduli spaces with separation property
GlobalTheory.UPoincTop.uPoinStX_sep.summary: Setting: a CM field E with extra structure (a 'host': a prime d ≡ 7 mod 16 with a square root of −d in E, E unramified over its real subfield), a PEL datum of unitary type with signature (p, q), p + q ≥ 1, a level, a fine moduli space X of abelian varieties with that structure, a coefficient number field F, and a function φ on positive semidefinite Hermitian forms that defines an admissible polyhedral cone decomposition without self-intersections. Conclusion: there exist a normal projective F-scheme Z containing X over F as a dense open subscheme, with an ample line bundle whose pullback is a power of the determinant (Hodge) bundle and with extension of degenerating families across discrete valuation rings; an ideal sheaf J supported on the boundary; and the normalized blow-up S of Z along J, projective, containing X as a dense open subscheme, with an effective Cartier divisor whose ideal is the pullback of J, such that the order of vanishing along a one-parameter degeneration is d times φ of its monodromy form and a large power of the ample bundle twisted down by the divisor is ample. In addition a separation property `SepB` holds for the open immersion of X into S: for a degenerating family with monomial degeneration data over a local domain, the non-boundary coordinates of the limit point are determined over the algebraically closed field of definition of the point.
GlobalTheory.UPoincTop.uPoinStX_sep.role: Assembly of an existence statement: it takes the integral minimal-type compactification, an ideal sheaf on its boundary and the separation property from three earlier theorems, passes to the generic fibre, forms the normalized blow-up and checks ampleness of the twisted bundle. The lemma `uStB` after it restates the result as the named proposition `UStB`.
GlobalTheory.UPoincTop.uPoinStX_sep.caveat: The bundles `UPoinOnX` and `SepB` were read, but their inner notions (monomial degeneration data, the valuation condition, `SepAtB`) were followed only one level; the wording of the separation property is an interpretation of that definition. Calling Z a minimal (Baily–Borel type) and S a toroidal compactification is my reading of the properties, not the project's wording.

literature.basis: The content matches the standard theory of minimal and toroidal compactifications of PEL Shimura varieties (Ash–Mumford–Rapoport–Tai, Faltings–Chai, Lan), with the toroidal one obtained as a normalized blow-up of the minimal one. The exact packaging, in particular the separation clause, is the project's own and was not matched to a specific published statement.

GlobalTheory.carrierNeedsFromD.title: Three archimedean inputs for the carrier bound, bundled
GlobalTheory.carrierNeedsFromD.summary: No hypotheses. It asserts three project-specific statements about analysis at the real places of a CM field at once. (1) `ThmPActualCpt` ('Theorem P', compact-support version): for the data of one real place (ranks k and r, parameters z, z', two finite-dimensional representations, a Haar measure and level data satisfying the project's `IsData` conditions) there is a chain of subspaces K_0, ..., K_r of a space of radial functions on which a family of forms indexed by admissible words is given by integrals of explicit densities, is sesquilinear and positive semidefinite, is stable under the slice operators, satisfies a composite integral formula at level zero, and such that K_0 contains the radial restriction of every smooth compactly supported coefficient function supported away from the singular set. (2) `ModelPlaceBuilt2`: there is one constant such that in every 'built place' setting over a CM field, each real place admits model data (level data, a map j, real parameters, positive constants) for which the principal Hermitian form of the cut-off test function equals a positive constant times a model cutoff energy form, together with decay, adjointness and eigenvalue properties. (3) `BuiltBounds2Cpt`: assuming (1), for every constant there are further constants such that every 'leading form setting' satisfies a positivity statement, integrality conditions, existence of wave and lift level data with barriers and thresholds, and a concrete sum-form bound.
GlobalTheory.carrierNeedsFromD.role: Bookkeeping: it pairs three earlier results (`actual_compact_theorem`, `model_place_built_holds`, `pb_builtBounds2Cpt`) into one conjunction. The conjunction is consumed by `carrierP`, which feeds the off-diagonal 'Theorem S' estimate.
GlobalTheory.carrierNeedsFromD.caveat: The three statements were read at their top level and one level below (`ThmPOn`, `IsModelPlace`, `IsBuiltPlace`, the setting structure). The inner predicates (the forms, densities, 'slice' and 'wave' operators, `IsLeadingFormSetting`, `SumFormConcrete`) were not unfolded, so the wording for them follows the structure of the definitions and their names. The setting structure is called `HidaSetting` in the source, but nothing in it refers to Hida theory.

literature.basis: All three conjuncts are about objects defined only inside this project (radial function spaces, word-indexed forms, 'built place' settings), and no standard theorem is restated.

Main.title: Zeros of primitive Dirichlet L-functions lie on the critical line
Main.summary: For every modulus N ≥ 1 and every primitive Dirichlet character χ modulo N, if s is a complex number with 0 < Re s < 1 and the (Mathlib) L-function of χ vanishes at s, then Re s = 1/2. There are no other hypotheses. The same file states four companion results before this one: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`, the project's own wording of it for the zeta function, non-vanishing of every Dirichlet L-function for Re s > 1/2 (away from the pole of the trivial character at s = 1), and the critical-line statement for all Dirichlet characters.
Main.role: Top-level final statement. It is a one-line restatement of `critAll`, which is obtained in `Supplements.Kernels.MainTheorems` from `allChi` (non-vanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions to the right of 1/2, i.e. `UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter`) through `Formalism.VW.critLine`.
Main.caveat: Only the statement, its definition in `Statements.lean` and the one-step proof terms were read; the chain of results behind `allChi` was not examined here.

literature.basis: The statement is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for primitive Dirichlet L-functions (and the file also concludes RH itself); no accepted proof of either existed in the literature.

PositivityTheory.AdelicQuotientData.rsPo.title: Rankin–Selberg partial L-function has a pole only for equal representations
PositivityTheory.AdelicQuotientData.rsPo.summary: No hypotheses. For a totally complex number field E, cuspidal automorphic representations π of GL_m and π' of GL_k with 1 ≤ k ≤ m, both invariant under the split centre, and a real number u, there is a finite set S0 of primes such that for every finite S containing S0 and every choice of Satake parameters α of π and β of π' outside S the following holds. There are functions Z and ZS holomorphic on Re s > 0, with ZS non-vanishing at all points σ + iu with σ > 0, such that Z(s) = (s − 1)·ZS(s)·L^S(s) for Re s large, where L^S(s) is the Euler product over primes outside S of the factors (1 − α_a·conj(β_b)·N(w)^(−s))^(−1); and Z(1) = 0 whenever π and π' are different (as classes, including the case m ≠ k). In classical terms: the partial Rankin–Selberg L-function of π and the contragredient of π' continues to Re s > 0 along the line Im s = u with at most a simple pole at s = 1, and has no pole there unless π = π'.
PositivityTheory.AdelicQuotientData.rsPo.role: Final assembly of this result from about twenty earlier lemmas in the same folder (Whittaker functionals, mirabolic induction step, multiplicity one, almost-everywhere sphericity, local Cauchy identity, the Jacquet–Shalika bound on Satake parameters). It is the analytic input from which the file then derives `JacquetShalikaRigidity` (strong multiplicity one for isobaric sums).
PositivityTheory.AdelicQuotientData.rsPo.caveat: The definition of cuspidal representation (`CuspSub`: an irreducible stable subspace of cusp forms) and of `HasSat` (Satake parameters) were taken at face value. The auxiliary factor ZS is a project device; the statement is weaker than full holomorphy of (s − 1)·L^S(s) on Re s > 0.

literature.basis: It lies in the project's `PublishedTheorems/JacquetShalikaRigidity` folder and is a weak form of the Jacquet–Shalika / Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika theorem on poles of Rankin–Selberg L-functions; the exact formulation with the auxiliary factor is the project's own.

PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2.bci_of.title: Base change from definite unitary groups to GL(n), reduced
PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2.bci_of.summary: Hypotheses: three project statements `FrameEx`, `FrameBound`, `FrameRead`. They concern auxiliary data ('frames') attached to an automorphic representation π of a definite unitary group and finite sets of places: the first says a run frame exists for every finite set of places, the second is a growth bound for traces of powers of operators in a star-algebra generated by Hecke-type operators, the third says that suitable characters of that algebra produce candidate base-change data. Conclusion (`BaseChangeIsobaricN`): for every CM field E unramified at all finite places over its real subfield, every n ≥ 1 and every automorphic representation π of the definite unitary group in n variables, there are discrete conjugate-self-dual automorphic representations of GL(N_i) over E with N_1 + ... + N_c = n whose isobaric sum is a base change of π: local components match at split places and at unramified inert places (through Satake parameters), unramified goes to spherical, and the infinitesimal characters match the weight of π.
PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2.bci_of.role: A reduction: the three hypotheses are combined with facts already proved in the project (finiteness of the discrete spectrum, a diagonal algebra statement, a limit statement and an initial frame) to produce the needed data for every finite set of places, and a rigidity argument then gives the base change.
PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2.bci_of.caveat: The conclusion was read in full. The three hypotheses were read only at the level of their statements; the structures `Frame0`, `RunFrame` and `GenIn` they refer to have many fields and were not unfolded, so their description is approximate.

literature.basis: The conclusion is the base change (weak transfer) from unitary groups to GL(n) as an isobaric sum, known from Labesse and later work; the project keeps a nearly identical statement in its `PublishedTheorems` folder. The hypotheses are internal to the project's own proof of it, so the implication as stated is not a literature result.

PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2B.bci_of.title: Three frame hypotheses imply isobaric base change for unitary groups
PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2B.bci_of.summary: Hypotheses: three project statements about 'frames'. A frame is a large package of data attached to an automorphic representation π of the definite unitary group U_n over a CM field E (unramified over its totally real subfield) and finite sets of places: weights at infinity, a Hecke character, level subgroups, auxiliary operators and a distinguished eigenvector. `FrameEx` says that every initial frame extends to a 'run frame' for every finite set of places; `FrameBound` says that the operator data derived from a run frame satisfies a trace-growth bound (traces of k-th powers bounded polynomially times operator norms); `FrameRead` says that characters of the generated star-algebra that match the eigenvector yield the desired output datum. Conclusion: `BaseChangeIsobaricN`: for every such E, every n ≥ 1 and every automorphic representation π of U_n, there are integers N_1 + ... + N_c = n and discrete automorphic representations of GL_{N_i} over E, conjugate self-dual in the project's sense, together with irreducible representations P_w of GL_n over each completion E_w that are subquotients of the product built from their local components, such that: at split places P_w is the local component of π, at unramified inert places the Satake parameters of P_w are the base change of those of π, and the weights of π at infinity determine the infinitesimal characters.
PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2B.bci_of.role: A reduction: the conclusion is obtained from a 'run' statement, itself assembled from finiteness of the discrete spectrum, a diagonal-algebra statement, existence of initial frames and a limit statement, all proved elsewhere, plus the three hypotheses. It leaves exactly those three frame statements open.
PositivityTheory.Rg.BcB.Plug2B.bci_of.caveat: The frame structures (`Frame0`, `RunFrame`) have 30+ and 20+ fields and were read only superficially; the predicates for local components, Satake parameters and 'conjugate self-dual' in the conclusion were taken from their names and field names.

literature.basis: The conclusion is a variant of weak base change from unitary groups to GL_n, which the project also lists among published theorems (`Published.BaseChangeIsobaric`; in the literature Labesse, Mok, Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White), but this declaration is an implication from frame statements that exist only in this project.

PositivityTheory.Rg.Rs.ascSeed_holds2.title: Discrete spectrum of GL_N: Speh-type embedding and local components
PositivityTheory.Rg.Rs.ascSeed_holds2.summary: No hypotheses. The statement `AscSeed` has two parts, for a totally complex number field E. (1) Every discrete (square-integrable, irreducible) automorphic representation V of GL_N over E whose infinitesimal character at some embedding is regular with integral differences admits integers a, d with ad = N and a unitary cuspidal representation π of GL_a, normalised to be trivial on the split centre, such that V embeds equivariantly into the space of automorphic forms parabolically induced from d twists of π by prescribed powers of the adelic absolute value. (2) Whenever a discrete V embeds in this way for a unitary normalised cuspidal π, each local component of V at a finite place is the Speh representation built from the corresponding local component σ of π, i.e. the unique irreducible quotient (cosocle) of the product of σ|·|^((d-1)/2 - i), i = 0..d-1.
PositivityTheory.Rg.Rs.ascSeed_holds2.role: Assembly: `ascSeed_of_locSub` gives part (1) from `ascAll_holds` (which uses Jacquet–Shalika rigidity and several slice/induction lemmas) and part (2) from a local sub-representation statement `LocSub` plus a local duality lemma; `LocSub` is proved just above from a restriction-at-a-point statement, an existence-of-projection lemma and Frobenius reciprocity.
PositivityTheory.Rg.Rs.ascSeed_holds2.caveat: `AscAll`, `Clause3Asc`, `AscEmb`, `IsDiscrete`, `RegInt`, `IsSpeh`, `spehFactor` were read. The exact exponents in `AscEmb` ((a-1)·((d-1)/2 - i) in the project's convention for induced forms) were not reconciled with the usual normalised-induction exponents, and `indForms`, `IsLocComp`, `IsCosocle` were not unfolded further.

literature.basis: This is the Mœglin–Waldspurger description of the residual spectrum of GL_N (discrete representations are Speh representations attached to a cuspidal π), restricted to regular integral infinitesimal character and stated in embedding form; the companion definitions live in a `PublishedTheorems` file and the proof cites Jacquet–Shalika from the project's published list.

PositivityTheory.SiegelWeilCoefficients..title: Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups beyond the convergent range
PositivityTheory.SiegelWeilCoefficients..summary: Setting: the CM extension E/F carried by a project master record, a Hermitian space V of rank m over E, and the quasi-split unitary group G in 2n variables, with n < m ≤ 2n and n + (Witt index of V) < m (Weil's convergence condition for the theta integral). Data: an additive character ψ of the adeles of F, a Hecke character χ of E whose restriction to the ideles of F is the m-th power of the quadratic character of E/F, a Weil representation ω of G(A) on Schwartz functions on V^n given by the usual Schrödinger-model formulas on the Siegel Levi, the unipotent radical and the Weyl element, a height function H adapted to the Siegel parabolic P, and a Schwartz function Φ that is polynomial times Gaussian at the infinite places and Schwartz–Bruhat at the finite places. Conclusion: for every g, the Siegel Eisenstein series, i.e. the sum over P(F)\G(F) of H(γg)^(s−s0)·(ω(γg)Φ)(0), has as a function of s a meromorphic extension that is analytic at s0 = (m−n)/2, and its value there equals the average of the theta series θ(g,h;Φ) over the automorphic quotient of U(V).
PositivityTheory.SiegelWeilCoefficients..role: Obtained by feeding three earlier results into the project's continuation theorem `top7`: a generation statement `genA_hf`, an idelic statement derived from convergence of Weil's theta integral (`wtc`), and `coefND` (each nondegenerate Fourier coefficient of the Eisenstein series has value at s0 equal to that of the theta integral). The proof itself only repackages the hypotheses into the project's bundles; it is the final assembly of this formula.
PositivityTheory.SiegelWeilCoefficients..caveat: The record of global data (`D7`) is a very large project structure; only its CM-field part matters here. The exact meaning of several side conditions (`IsInfFam`, `IsCovolOne`, `IsCartanInv`, the half-plane-agreement clause inside the meromorphic-extension predicate) was taken from names or read only superficially. The classical name is my identification from the unfolded formulas.

literature.basis: The statement type is `GlobalTheory.Published.SiegelWeilUnitarySchrodingerLit` in a `PublishedTheorems/SiegelWeilSchrodinger` folder, and the unfolded content is the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups in the range n < m ≤ 2n under Weil's convergence condition (Weil; Ichino for this range). Here it is proved inside the project rather than assumed.

PositivityTheory.ThKR.theoremK_head2.title: Theta integrals of two unitary dual pairs are proportional
PositivityTheory.ThKR.theoremK_head2.summary: Hypotheses: (1) `EisBL`: Siegel Eisenstein series on the doubled unitary group attached to a Hermitian or skew-Hermitian space over a CM-type extension E/F converge in a half-plane and continue meromorphically in s, with finite-order poles and control against linear forms of moderate growth; (2) `SiegelWeilStd`: the Siegel–Weil formula when one space is definite, expressing the value of the Eisenstein series at s = (m-n)/2 as 1 or 2 times the average of the theta function over the unitary quotient. Conclusion, for all 'triples' (a good CM extension with Hermitian spaces V, V' of dimensions a > a' and a skew-Hermitian space W of dimension a + a', Hecke characters α, β, and Weil representations ω of U(V)×U(W) and ω' of U(V')×U(W)): local matching data (irreducible archimedean and finite quotient maps relating the two Schwartz spaces) exist; the theta integrals converge with decay bounds; for any matching data there is a unique constant c, nonzero, with I(Φ) = c·I'(Φ') as functions on U(W) for all matched Schwartz functions; local coinvariant statements hold at good split places; and two recursion formulas relate the constants c for neighbouring signatures through an explicit factor and a value of the partial L-function of α/β.
PositivityTheory.ThKR.theoremK_head2.role: Final assembly of the project's 'Theorem K': it specialises `theoremK_head2_of_mod` to the proved statement `modSt2`, which in turn calls `Tr.closeSph` with about a dozen proved inputs (coinvariant and multiplicity-one statements at ramified, split and inert places, Howe duality at inert places, local lifts and archimedean statements, a Siegel-set statement, existence of Weil representations) plus the two hypotheses.
PositivityTheory.ThKR.theoremK_head2.caveat: `ThetaIntegralsAgree`, `LocalMatching`, `IsTriple`, `IsMatched`, `IsConst`, `Decay`, `OneConst`, `Coinv`, `StepAlpha`, `StepBeta`, `EisBL`, `SiegelWeilStd` were read. The theta integrals `Model.I`, the Schwartz subspaces `So`, `Pol`, the predicate `IsWeil` and the factor `stepFac` were not unfolded, so the summary gives the shape of the identities rather than exact normalisations.

literature.basis: The two hypotheses are literature statements (continuation of Siegel Eisenstein series, Siegel–Weil with a definite space). The conclusion is an identity between theta integrals from two different unitary groups, in the spirit of Siegel–Weil/seesaw arguments, but it is the project's own 'Theorem K' and I could not match it to a named published theorem.

SquareStatements.good_tower_antisymmetry.title: Root-tower height defect is antisymmetric under adjacent weight swaps
SquareStatements.good_tower_antisymmetry.summary: Hypotheses: three assumed statements, namely `CmpSt` (for two analytic realisations of the same multi-projective arithmetic variety with the same singular metrics, the degree-weighted difference of arithmetic intersection numbers tends to 0), `Given` (a bundle of about seventeen statements: toroidal compactification compatibilities, a 'key formula', and items named after literature results such as extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes, a Hodge–Tate statement attributed to Fargues, GAGA for sections, a slope bound, Zhang-type height bounds), and existence and bilinearity of the Weil pairing on polarised abelian schemes. Setting: a CM field E, unitary PEL-type data of signature (p,q) with p,q ≥ 1, moduli spaces at all levels, a normal projective flat integral model Y at one level, a 'root tower' T (a family of multi-projective arithmetic models indexed by a bound B and a component), a 'good origin' tying T to Y and satisfying an extra immersion condition, and a full arithmetic intersection system. Conclusion: for every B ≥ 2, component c, embedding τ, adjacent indices a, a+1 with a+1 different from the tower's distinguished index, and every weight λ, the number P(B,c; ℓ_λ^(d+1)) − vol(c)·h_Fl(ℓ_λ^(d+1)) changes sign when the a-th and (a+1)-th entries of λ at τ are swapped. Here ℓ_λ is the linear form attached to λ, d is the flag-variety dimension, P is the limiting arithmetic intersection number on the tower model, and h_Fl is the corresponding intersection number on the flag variety.
SquareStatements.good_tower_antisymmetry.role: A one-line application of `antisymmetry_of_singular_statement` to the project's proven singular-metric statement `stSing`; that lemma in turn combines seven sub-statements (base, embedding, form, height cancellation, comparison, transposition factor). It is a reduction step that discharges one hypothesis.
SquareStatements.good_tower_antisymmetry.caveat: The conclusion `I8`, the structures `RootTower`, `GoodOrigin`, `Extra`, the hypothesis lists `CmpSt`, `Given`, `WeilSt` and the definitions of P and h_Fl were read. The individual members of `Given`, the meaning of 'good origin', and the content of `stSing` were not unfolded and are described from names.

literature.basis: The conclusion concerns 'root towers' and 'good origins', which are constructions of this project; the statement is conditional on hypothesis bundles (partly named after literature results) and concludes something specific to the proof.

UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.Conclus.title: Base change for definite unitary groups, in the project's datum
UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.Conclus.summary: Hypotheses: (1) `DefiniteN`: for a CM field E unramified over its maximal real subfield at all finite places, every automorphic representation of the rank-n unitary group has a base change to GL_n over E, written as an isobaric sum of discrete conjugate-self-dual pieces with matching local components, Satake parameters and infinitesimal characters; (2) three published local statements about GL_N over a p-adic field (Bernstein's irreducibility of a product of irreducible unitarisable representations, the classification of generic unitary representations as complementary products, and existence of the irreducible quotient of a standard product); (3) existence of a local Langlands reciprocity map with a list of laws; (4) a project datum D whose abstract 'automorphic side' is realised by actual objects: its abstract cuspidal GL classes correspond bijectively to genuine unitary cuspidal representations over the host CM field with matching local parameters, twists, infinitesimal characters and conjugate self-duality, and its abstract unitary-group classes are realised by genuine automorphic representations whose local parameters at split places are given by local Langlands. Conclusion: the datum's `Conclusion1` holds, i.e. if the fields F and K generate E, then (for E/F unramified CM, [F:Q] at least 2, 2 not in any non-split prime) every automorphic representation of a definite unitary group in the datum that is spherical at all non-split places has a base-change parameter: a multiplicity-free list of conjugate-self-dual cuspidal GL classes with Speh-type multiplicities, of total rank nV, matching the representation at split places, at non-split places (unramified base change of the Satake parameter) and at infinity.
UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.Conclus.role: A thin wrapper: it discards the unused Bernstein hypothesis and calls `aux_of_cgTrue_of_auTrue` with the project's theorem `ascComp` (discrete automorphic representations of GL_N sit above cuspidal ones as Speh-type components). It is a transfer step that moves a base-change statement from concrete automorphic representations to the project's abstract datum.
UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.Conclus.caveat: The datum type `D7` is a very large structure whose fields `nd`, `naut`, `nbc` (abstract Galois, GL-automorphic and unitary base-change data) were read only through the definitions that use them; `WDTie` (an identification of the abstract local parameters with Weil-Deligne representations) and the laws inside `RecTExists` were read only in part. The first hypothesis `DefiniteN` is itself a strong base-change statement, proved elsewhere in the project from a further hypothesis.

literature.basis: The conclusion is the weak base change from definite unitary groups to GL_n (Labesse, Clozel-Harris-Labesse) restated for the project's datum, and it is derived from a hypothesis that is the same theorem in concrete form plus hypotheses in the project's `Published` namespace. The packaging in terms of the project's datum is specific to this proof.

UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.baseCha.title: Isobaric base change from definite unitary groups to GL_n
UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.baseCha.summary: No hypotheses. For every CM field E that is unramified over its maximal real subfield at all finite places, every n ≥ 1 and every irreducible automorphic representation π of the definite unitary group U(n) of E (a space of functions on the adelic points, stable and irreducible under right translation), there is a base change to GL_n over E: a partition n = N_1 + ... + N_c, discrete (square-integrable) automorphic representations V_i of GL_{N_i} with local components σ_i,w and infinitesimal characters m_i, and irreducible local representations P_w of GL_n(E_w). Each V_i is 'conjugate self-dual of Speh type' in the project's sense (it embeds in the space induced from absolute-value twists of a unitary, conjugate self-dual cuspidal representation); P_w is a subquotient of the parabolic induction of the σ_i,w, is spherical where π is unramified, has the base-changed Satake parameters at inert places, is the local component of π at split places, and the m_i add up to the infinitesimal character given by the weight of π.
UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.baseCha.role: Final assembly of the project's own proof of this base-change statement: `bci_of` is applied to three inputs, namely existence of 'frames' (from a finiteness statement for candidate eigen-systems), a frame bound, and a 'frame reading' statement. It is an existence theorem for the base-change data.
UpperTheory.BaseChangeIdentities.baseCha.caveat: The target proposition `BaseChangeIsobaricN` and its structure `IsBaseChangeN`, the definitions of automorphic representation of U(n), discrete representation, `CsdAsc` and `AscEmb` were read. The notions `HasSatAt`, `bcParam`, `HasWeightAt`, `infOfWeight`, `locProd` were taken at face value from their names and use. The three inputs of the proof (`FrameEx`, `FrameBound`, `FrameRead`) were not unfolded.

literature.basis: The statement is a variant of the project's own literature item `GlobalTheory.Published.BaseChangeIsobaric` (file `PublishedTheorems/.../BaseChangeIsobaric`, base change for definite unitary groups in the style of Labesse), with the conjugate-self-duality clause replaced by the project's `CsdAsc`. Here it is proved inside the project rather than assumed.

UpperTheory.ConvolutionTheory.R2.quadBC2.title: Quadratic base change for GL(2) from totally real to CM
UpperTheory.ConvolutionTheory.R2.quadBC2.summary: Let F be a totally real number field and E a totally complex quadratic extension of F. Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over F (in the project's model: a nonzero stable space of cusp forms whose infinitesimal characters at each real place are distinct and integral after the standard shift). Conclusion: either there is a Hecke character η of F that is the quadratic character of E/F at almost all places and π is isomorphic to its twist by η, or there is a cuspidal representation P of GL(2) over E that is a base change of π. Base change here means: the infinitesimal characters match at infinite places, the local components are isomorphic at places where the completions of F and E agree, and at almost all places the Satake parameters of P are the f-th powers of those of π, f being the residue degree.
UpperTheory.ConvolutionTheory.R2.quadBC2.role: Proved by a theta-correspondence argument assembled from named lemmas in the same folder: existence of the quadratic-space datum, a Weil representation and measures; a case split on whether the 'trivial orbit terms' of the theta lift vanish; in one case the span of lifts is nonzero and contains an irreducible cuspidal piece with the base-change properties, in the other π is dihedral for E. Final assembly of this statement.
UpperTheory.ConvolutionTheory.R2.quadBC2.caveat: `QuadBC2`, `IsBC`, `IsoTwist`, `IsQuadCharOf`, `CuspSub` and `IsRegAlg` were read. The lemmas used in the proof (`datEx`, `weilEx`, `irr`, `cap`, `split`, `unr`, `dih`) were not opened; the description of the method rests on their names and the shape of the proof.

literature.basis: This is quadratic base change for GL(2) (Saito, Shintani, Langlands; Jacquet), here restricted to regular algebraic representations and a CM quadratic extension; the project's general version of the same statement is named `QuadBaseChange` and sits in a `PublishedTheorems` folder.

UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.title: Non-vanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions from a Galois-representation hypothesis
UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.summary: Hypothesis `Row0b`: for every CM field E, prime l, isomorphism of the algebraic closure of Q_l with C, and every regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_a over E that is polarized by a Hecke character of the maximal real subfield, there is a continuous semisimple a-dimensional l-adic representation of the Galois group of E with prescribed Hodge–Tate weights, compatible with π at places away from l in a weakened sense (equal dimension, equality in the toral case, matching characteristic polynomials on inertia-degree-zero elements in a tame case) and crystalline or de Rham / potentially semistable above l; compatibility is measured against any local map satisfying the project's local-Langlands laws. Conclusion: for every modulus N ≥ 1, every Dirichlet character χ mod N and every s with Re s > 1/2 (excluding s = 1 when χ is trivial), L(χ, s) ≠ 0.
UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.role: A reduction of the main theorem to one input. The hypothesis is used twice to fill the three-field bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements` (the middle field, existence of a local reciprocity map, is supplied by a theorem of the project), then `every_character_of_literature_of_vWin` is applied with the condition `VWin` obtained from the same hypothesis by `vwin_of_row`. The next declaration in the file discharges the hypothesis and deduces RH.
UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter.caveat: The fine conditions inside `Row0b` (the predicates for crystalline, de Rham, tame, and the Weil–Deligne comparison) were not unfolded beyond their names. `VWin` (a bound on sums of lengths of Tate–Shafarevich-type groups over fields cut out by χ) was read but its role in the proof was not followed.

literature.basis: The conclusion is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions in non-vanishing form, which had no proof; the hypothesis itself resembles known theorems on Galois representations of polarized automorphic representations (Harris–Taylor, Shin, Chenevier–Harris, Caraiani).

UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.steps_holds.title: All steps for Galois representations cut from towers hold
UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.steps_holds.summary: No hypotheses. The conclusion is the bundle `Steps`, 17 statements about l-adic Galois representations of a number field E attached to a 'tower': a smooth projective variety over E with a family of finite etale correspondences, together with an eigenvalue system θ. The statements say: for a nice tower there is a continuous semisimple representation that is a graded piece of the θ-part of the cohomology; at places not above l it is unramified and Frobenius is killed by the polynomial whose roots are given by the Hecke eigenvalues; at places above l it is crystalline, has prescribed Hodge–Tate jumps, and crystalline Frobenius is killed by the corresponding polynomial; a comparison between two forms of the local conditions; the same properties survive twisting by a character; l-adic characters exist for algebraic Hecke characters; a Satake multiset has the expected cardinality; and semisimplicity and continuity pass to summands, isomorphic representations and twists.
UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.steps_holds.role: Final assembly of a bundle: three of the fields (the crystalline step, the Hodge–Tate jump step, the Frobenius step) are supplied by named earlier theorems, the jump step being the lemma just above, and the remaining fourteen by `steps_of` from results proved elsewhere. The bundle is then used to realise weight-one data geometrically.
UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.steps_holds.caveat: I read the top-level definitions of the 17 fields, but the notions `HTower`, 'piece of cohomology', the crystalline and Hodge–Tate predicates and the congruence conditions were not unfolded, so the descriptions of individual fields follow their definitions only one level deep and partly their names.

literature.basis: The contents resemble standard facts (Eichler–Shimura type congruence relations, crystalline comparison, Galois characters of algebraic Hecke characters), but they are formulated for the project's own 'tower' objects and I could not match them to specific published statements.

UpperTheory.Gal.KunnethLefschetz.Core.in.title: Full list of étale cohomology inputs from five core facts
UpperTheory.Gal.KunnethLefschetz.Core.in.summary: Hypothesis: a bundle `Core` of five statements about étale cohomology with twisted Z/q coefficients, q invertible: vanishing in degrees ≥ 2 for finite-type Dedekind algebras over an algebraically closed field (C2); an invariance statement for étale algebras over a polynomial ring over an absolutely integrally closed local domain on passing to the fraction field (C3); invariance under A → A[T] (C4); the cohomology of Laurent polynomials over a strictly henselian ring (C5); and the projective bundle formula (D1). Conclusion: the bundle `In` of 24 statements holds: invariance under quasi-isomorphism, smooth Čech descent, level-wise and Mayer–Vietoris equivalences, killing of positive-degree classes on étale covers, naturality/ring axioms/support and additivity properties of cup products, first Chern classes and Kummer classes, the coefficient long exact sequence, change of coefficient ring, negative-degree vanishing and H^0 as sections, compatibility with reduction of coefficients and with filtered colimits of rings, acyclicity of strictly henselian rings, a fibrewise base-change criterion, homotopy invariance, the projective bundle formula, proper base change over a strictly henselian local ring, a smooth generic-fibre comparison (E3), finiteness for proper schemes over an algebraically closed field (E4), Gysin maps in every codimension, and a Kummer-theory goal.
UpperTheory.Gal.KunnethLefschetz.Core.in.role: Bookkeeping assembly: most fields are filled by theorems already proved in the project, C4 and D1 come from the hypothesis, E3 and E4 are derived just above in the same file from the hypothesis, the duality/diagonal-class field and the Gysin field come from affine proper base change. It collects everything into one record used by the Künneth and Lefschetz arguments.
UpperTheory.Gal.KunnethLefschetz.Core.in.caveat: The propositions A1–E4 were read in `GlobalTheory.EtC`; the cohomology theory itself (`Ht`, `Spc`, `Eqv`, `tw`, `Shv`) is the project's own construction and was not unfolded, and the meanings of `SH` (strictly henselian) and `AIC` (absolutely integrally closed) rest on their names. The fields `gys` and `kun` of `In` were not read.

literature.basis: Hypotheses and conclusion are standard theorems of étale cohomology (SGA 4, SGA 4½: cohomological dimension of curves, homotopy invariance, projective bundle formula, proper base change, finiteness, Gysin sequences), restated for the project's own model of étale cohomology; the implication itself is a packaging step.

UpperTheory.Gal.Seam.HT.htBij.title: Hodge-Tate decomposition for smooth projective good-reduction models
UpperTheory.Gal.Seam.HT.htBij.summary: No hypotheses. For every prime l and every finite extension K of Q_l inside a fixed algebraic closure, there is a 'Hodge-Tate pairing' package: for each scheme X over the ring of integers of K, pairings between the l-adic etale cohomology of the geometric generic fibre in degree n and the duals of the graded pieces (index a) of the de Rham-type cohomology of the generic fibre, with values in C_l, semilinear in both arguments, Galois-equivariant up to the a-th power of the cyclotomic character, natural in X, and compatible with cup products, the unit class and first Chern classes of line bundles. For every model that is projective, strictly semistable and smooth over the integers of K, the pairing is injective in every degree and non-degenerate in top degree when the generic fibre is connected; if the model is smooth of some relative dimension d, the pairing is also surjective in every degree, and the Q_l-dimension of the degree-n etale cohomology equals the sum over a from 0 to n of the K-dimensions of the graded pieces.
UpperTheory.Gal.Seam.HT.htBij.role: Final assembly of the Hodge-Tate comparison: it applies `htBij_of` to the existence and injectivity of the Hodge-Tate map (proved just above from the etale-side input for smooth models) together with three etale-side facts proved elsewhere (a diagonal/square-exactness statement, a diagonal class statement, and finite-dimensionality of etale cohomology).
UpperTheory.Gal.Seam.HT.htBij.caveat: The graded pieces `Hdg` are defined as cohomology of the a-th graded piece of a filtered functor on a site of thickenings; I did not verify that this agrees with the usual Hodge cohomology H^(n-a)(X, Omega^a). The etale cohomology groups and the fields of the pairing package concerning Chern classes were read only at the level of their signatures.

literature.basis: The statement is the Hodge-Tate decomposition (bijectivity of the Hodge-Tate comparison and the resulting dimension formula) for smooth projective schemes with good reduction over a p-adic ring of integers, a theorem of Faltings; the formulation through the project's own pairing package is not standard.

UpperTheory.GalC.linkN_of_twGood_galoisP.title: The N-link bound for a family with Galois preconditions
UpperTheory.GalC.linkN_of_twGood_galoisP.summary: Hypotheses: (1) a bundle of seven literature statements (Fontaine's B_cris, global Artin reciprocity, Bloch–Kato local theory, local Tate duality, the local Euler characteristic formula, local finiteness, and an integral comparison attributed to Bhatt–Scholze); (2) the project hypothesis `CutGivesAlt`: every datum satisfying the 'Galois preconditions' and a four-part tie condition admits a good 'cut' (a restriction to selected localisations and eigen-systems) whose cut datum satisfies the full list of 'norm choice facts' and the tie condition again; (3) a family of data Fm with good twists, all of whose members beyond the starting point satisfy the Galois preconditions and the tie condition. Conclusion: `LinkN` for Fm, i.e. there are constants C and x0 such that for x ≥ x0, every member with finite odd Sha condition and every lift index j satisfy an explicit inequality: the sum over twisted places in the support of (log-weight) × (ramification index) × (η-exponent) is at most a rank d_Z0(j) times C·(f·m·b·L² + log²x·N_c) plus a sum over primes l of log l times lengths of Sha groups (when that sum converges).
UpperTheory.GalC.linkN_of_twGood_galoisP.role: A reduction. The proof chooses a good cut at each member, proves the bound for the cut family from local bounds at 2 and 3 (`at23_family_alt`), a uniform constant from `exists_const_tieChi_bound_of_facts` and the chain 'family facts → local conclusion → LinkN', and then transfers it back to the original family with `linkN_of_gd` using a multiplicity-at-most-rank lemma.
UpperTheory.GalC.linkN_of_twGood_galoisP.caveat: `LinkN`, `GaloisPreconditions` (18 fields), `NormChoiceFacts`, `Tie4`, `CutD`, `CutD.Good` and the literature bundle were read; the individual fields of the precondition bundles (admissible datum, residual irreducibility, depth-zero conditions, etc.) and the quantities in the inequality (η-exponents, d_Z0, the size parameters b, L, N_c) are taken from their names and signatures only.

literature.basis: The conclusion is an inequality about the project's own families of data and the hypotheses include a project-specific cut hypothesis; only the first hypothesis bundle is literature.

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.arith_hil.title: Arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel theorem for nef Hermitian line bundles
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.arith_hil.summary: Hypothesis: the bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements`, three assumptions named after a local-global compatibility result of Caraiani (two fields) and the existence of the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n. Conclusion: the project's statement `ArithHilbertSamuel`. It says: let X be an integral scheme, projective and flat over the spectrum of a domain k that is finite over the integers, of Krull dimension D+1; let L and N be Hermitian line bundles on X (smooth metrics at every complex embedding, compatible with complex conjugation), with L nef (semipositive metric, nonnegative degree on vertical and horizontal curves) and with arithmetic self-intersection number a. Then for all large m the set of global sections of L^m ⊗ N of sup-norm at most 1 at every complex point is finite, and the logarithm of its cardinality equals a·m^(D+1)/(D+1)! + o(m^(D+1)).
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.arith_hil.role: A one-line derivation: it applies the project's theorem that principalisation of ideal sheaves (resolution-type statement in characteristic zero) implies arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel, to the project's own proof of principalisation. The hypothesis bundle is carried in the signature but is not used in the proof; the result feeds the volume bounds and the bundle of 'published Hodge bundle theorems'.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.arith_hil.caveat: The three fields of the hypothesis bundle were identified from their names; only the local Langlands field was read (as existence of a reciprocity map satisfying a list of laws), and they play no part in this proof. The self-intersection number is defined in the project through a recursively characterised height function, which I read but did not compare line by line with the standard definition.

literature.basis: The conclusion is the arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel theorem (Gillet–Soulé, Abbes–Bouche, and Zhang for nef bundles), and the project places its statement in the namespace `Published`.

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.grothendi.title: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory for abelian schemes
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.grothendi.summary: Hypothesis: the bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements` (three literature assumptions about Galois representations and local Langlands); it is not actually used in the proof. Conclusion: let R → R0 be a surjection of rings whose kernel carries nilpotent divided powers. Then (1) for an abelian scheme A over R with reduction A0, the comparison map from the crystalline to the de Rham realization is bijective and the Hodge filtration of A is an admissible lift of that of A0; (2) every admissible filtration (a direct summand lifting the Hodge filtration of A0) comes from an abelian scheme over R lifting A0; (3) a homomorphism A0 → B0 that respects the lifted filtrations lifts uniquely to a homomorphism A → B.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.grothendi.role: A two-line combination of two results proved inside the project: the structure of the first de Rham cohomology of abelian schemes, and lifting of abelian schemes and homomorphisms along nilpotent divided-power thickenings.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.grothendi.caveat: The notions of crystalline realization and of the comparison map are the project's own constructions and were not unfolded.

literature.basis: This is the Grothendieck–Messing theorem (Messing 1972; Mazur–Messing), and the project states it in its `PublishedTheorems` folder under the name `GrothendieckDeformation`.

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.title: Global automorphic and Galois literature bundle from three open inputs
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.summary: Hypothesis: the structure `OpenLiteratureStatements`, which has three fields: existence of the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n over completions of number fields (in the project's axiomatised form), and, under two different field names but with the same type, existence of l-adic Galois representations attached to regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representations of GL_a over CM fields, with local-global compatibility away from l and prescribed behaviour at l. Conclusion: the 16-field bundle `GlobalAutomorphicGaloisHypotheses'`: rapid decay of cusp forms, Harish-Chandra finiteness, finite-dimensionality of spaces of automorphic forms on GL_n, Jacquet–Shalika, the cuspidal spectrum of GL_n, isobaric base change, Gelfand–Kazhdan duality, the Galois representations for polarized pairs, the local-global statement itself, Clozel's purity and cohomological statements, global Artin reciprocity, ray class fields, two statements on l-adic characters attached to algebraic Hecke characters, and de Rham implies potentially semistable.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.role: Bookkeeping: it fills each field with a separately named theorem `..._of_literature`. Most of these ignore the hypothesis and point to results proved elsewhere in the project (for example Jacquet–Shalika, Clozel purity, Artin reciprocity); only the Galois-representation field and the local-global field use the open inputs.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.caveat: The three hypothesis fields (`RecTExists`, `Row0b` with `PropsB`) and the field `PairUAlt` were read. The other fifteen conclusion fields are described from their names in the `Published` namespace; their definitions were not opened. The proofs of the individual `..._of_literature` theorems were not checked beyond which constants they refer to.

literature.basis: Every field of the conclusion is a statement the project labels as published (namespace `Published`, names of standard theorems), and the three hypotheses are likewise literature statements (local Langlands for GL_n; Galois representations for polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representations).

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.title: Assembly of the 'non-endoscopic' literature hypothesis bundle
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.summary: Hypothesis: the bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements`, which has three fields. Two of them are the same proposition, that every regular algebraic polarised cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_a over a CM field has an attached l-adic Galois representation with the project's list of properties (labelled as Caraiani's local-global compatibility and as Galois representations of polarised pairs); the third is existence of the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n over completions of number fields, in the project's formulation. Conclusion: the structure `NonEndoscopicHypothesesAlt` holds. It bundles five parts: nineteen statements on representations of p-adic GL_n (Bernstein–Zelevinsky finiteness, geometric lemma, Zelevinsky and Langlands classification, local converse theorem, Moy–Prasad, and others), sixteen global automorphic and Galois statements (rapid decay of cusp forms, Jacquet–Shalika, base change, Clozel purity, Artin reciprocity, and others), twelve Galois-cohomology statements (Poitou–Tate, local Tate duality, Euler characteristic formulas, Greenberg–Wiles, a local Bloch–Kato statement), a five-part statement `JoinOut` on denominators of zeta values and transport of lattices, and the Hecke–Tate functional equation.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.role: Pure packaging: each field is filled by an earlier theorem named `..._of_literature`. Only a few of those use the assumed bundle (the Galois-representation and local Langlands fields); others, for example the Hecke–Tate functional equation, are proved in the project without it.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.literatur.caveat: The bundle structures and the three assumed fields were read. The individual statements inside the bundles (in the `GlobalTheory.Published` namespace) were not unfolded and are listed by name; the contents of `JoinOut` have project-specific names and were only skimmed.

literature.basis: The conclusion is a conjunction of statements that the project places in `Published` / `LiteratureTheorems` namespaces and names after published theorems, derived from three further literature-labelled assumptions. One component (`JoinOut`) has project-specific naming and I did not verify that it restates published results.

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.title: Bundle of twelve analytic and representation-theoretic published inputs
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.summary: Hypothesis: the bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements`, which has three fields (two statements of a type called `Row` whose field names refer to Caraiani's local-global compatibility and to Galois representations of polarised pairs, and existence of the local Langlands reciprocity map for GL_n). Conclusion: a record of twelve propositions named after published theorems: the Weil representation for unitary dual pairs, existence of discrete series of U(p,q), Harish-Chandra's analyticity, classification of discrete series, trace-class property of convolution operators on the cuspidal spectrum, the Dixmier–Malliavin factorisation, Flath's tensor product factorisation, the Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups, the doubling method for local zeta integrals, unramified doubling for GL, continuation and non-vanishing on Re s ≥ 1 of partial Hecke L-functions, and a statement `HtCard` about continuity and Hodge–Tate-type weight counts of l-adic Galois representations.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.role: Bookkeeping: each field is filled by citing a theorem proved elsewhere in the project (names ending in `_holds`, `_fromLibrary`, or similar); the open-literature hypothesis is passed along and is not visibly needed for most fields.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.caveat: Seven of the twelve target statements were opened and match their names (Flath, Siegel–Weil, trace class, Dixmier–Malliavin, Hecke L partial continuation, discrete series existence, `HtCard`); the other five are identified by name only. The `Row` type of two hypothesis fields was not unfolded. The name of the record type (`GeometricGaloisRepCompatibility`) does not describe its contents.

literature.basis: Every field of the conclusion lives in the project's `Published` namespace / `PublishedTheorems` folder and restates a theorem with a standard name; the statement only packages them.

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.title: Bundle of twenty-eight published arithmetic-geometry theorems
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.summary: Hypothesis: the three-field bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements` (existence of Galois representations for polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representations over CM fields, stated twice, and existence of a local reciprocity map for GL_n). Conclusion: the structure `PublishedHodgeBundleTheorems`, whose 28 fields are propositions from the project's `Published` list: toroidal compactification, arithmetic volume lower bound and nef volume, an Arakelov calculus statement, de Rham cohomology of abelian schemes, ray class fields, semistable reduction, strong approximation for special unitary groups, a Green series statement, good Chern–Weil forms, Landherr's theorem on Hermitian forms, the Hasse norm theorem for quadratic extensions, extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes, a lowest-alcove statement for induced modules, a section for principal polarisations, the count n^(2g) of n-torsion points of an abelian variety, Grothendieck–Messing, prismatic Dieudonné theory, Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing, nef numerics, L² extension, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel, existence of Chow forms, heights of cycles, Serre's holomorphic sections, Nadel vanishing, principalisation, and formal algebraisation.

That the hypothesis is unused was checked by pattern matching within this file, not by the Lean kernel.

literature.basis: Every field lives in the project's `Published` namespace and those inspected restate standard theorems; the declaration only packages them. The exact Lean formulations are project-specific, so a full match with the literature was not verified for all fields.

UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.title: Bundle of 60 literature inputs from three open assumptions
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.summary: Hypothesis: a bundle `OpenLiteratureStatements` with three fields. Two of them (with the same type) say that every regular algebraic polarized cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(a) over a CM field has an l-adic Galois representation with the expected Hodge–Tate weights and a weak form of local–global compatibility; the third says that a local Langlands correspondence for GL(n) over completions of number fields exists, with a list of compatibility laws. Conclusion: the bundle `UnitaryGroupThirdPlaceHypotheses` holds. That bundle has 60 fields; 50 of them are statements in the project's `Published` namespace named after published theorems (Clozel, Green, Bernstein–Zelevinsky, Jacquet–Shalika, Harish-Chandra, Casselman–Wallach, Siegel–Weil for unitary groups, doubling method, class field theory, p-adic Hodge theory, and so on), and the rest are smaller sub-bundles and Galois-theoretic statements of the same kind.

Almost all of those ignore the hypothesis and cite proofs made inside the project; only the fields about Galois representations and local–global compatibility actually use the three assumed statements.
UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published.caveat: The 60 target fields were not unfolded one by one; their content is described from their names and namespace. The three assumed statements were read (the Galois-representation statement down to its list of properties, the local Langlands statement only at the level of its list of laws).
