Whether each project formulation matches the published one was not checked.

UpperTheory.Top.recS.title: Existence of design families from Minkowski's divisibility bound
UpperTheory.Top.recS.summary: Let QO be a property of pairs (datum, object over it) depending on a parameter record, and cT any real function of two real variables. Hypotheses: Minkowski's divisibility statement (the order of every finite subgroup of GL_n over the rationals divides an explicit Minkowski number), and the claim that this statement implies an existence property `RecExP` for QO strengthened by an extra condition: for all sufficiently large scales and all admissible input data there exist auxiliary sizes and a datum of the construction whose points satisfy the property. Conclusion (`ExD`): for every window parameter lambda > 1 and every requirement G on host fields such that hosts satisfying G exist at all large scales in windows, the 'design choices' exist: for every small eps and every threshold K there is a parameter family in the class defined by QO, satisfying G at all its points, with constants above K and satisfying a fixed list of about a dozen side conditions (thick-set, code-size, box, divisibility and tame-distinctness conditions).
UpperTheory.Top.recS.role: An existence step. It assembles `designS` and `kitS` from: a small-prime statement obtained from an unconditional primes-in-progressions estimate, existence of objects from an admissible twist datum, host existence with window shares (`hostWW`, `hostQ`), the preceding lemma `objC_true`, and a closed-form window-share requirement.
UpperTheory.Top.recS.caveat: `MinkDiv`, `ExD`, `DesignChoices`, `HostExW`, `RecExP` and `clsP` were read, but the notions inside them (`Par`, `Obj`, scales, `ChGood`, `HostGood`, the side conditions of `DesignChoices`, the class `cls7`) were not unfolded; the description of what the families and objects are rests on the shape of the definitions and on names.

literature.basis: The only literature input is Minkowski's bound on finite subgroups of GL_n(Q); the conclusion asserts existence of parameter families that exist only inside this project's construction.

UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v.title: GRH for all primitive Dirichlet characters from three inputs
UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v.summary: Hypotheses: (1) `Green`: for every prime g and every d > 0, the cuspidal irreducible characters of GL_d over the field with g elements are parametrised bijectively by monic irreducible polynomials of degree d with nonzero constant term, with the expected character values on elliptic elements and degree equal to the product of (g^i - 1) for i from 1 to d-1; (2) `VWin`: for every primitive Dirichlet character and certain auxiliary abelian number fields attached to it (subfields of cyclotomic fields cut out by the character and two auxiliary primes q, d in prescribed windows), the Tate-Shafarevich-type groups of Q_l/Z_l twisted by powers of the cyclotomic character have finite length for twists below a bound, and the sum over primes l of log l times these lengths is at most exp(x^eps / 2); (3) the bundle `HypsAlt` is inhabited: a family class together with a selection of auxiliary data and about forty-five properties of it (bounded rows, divisibility rows, class-number formulas, counting bounds, spectral conditions, period and point-integral conditions, mass formulas and others). Conclusion: for every primitive Dirichlet character, including the trivial one of conductor 1, the L-function has no zeros with real part greater than 1/2.
UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v.role: A top-level reduction. It combines `zeroFreeAll_of_topG` (zero-freeness from the project's connectivity statement `TopG` with window parameter 3/2), `forall_goal_of_shape_of_hyps` together with `shape_closed_link_n_of_green` (which derive `TopG` from the bundle and from Green's parametrisation), and `supplyChi` (which turns `VWin` into existence of suitable host fields for each character).
UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v.caveat: The conclusion and the hypotheses `Green` and `VWin` were read down to their definitions. The bundle `HypsAlt` was read only as a list of fields; the meaning of most of its fields (families of data `FamP`, selections, rows, ties) was not unfolded, so I cannot say which of them are literature statements and which are internal claims of the construction.

literature.basis: The conclusion is the Riemann Hypothesis together with GRH for all primitive Dirichlet characters, which had no proof before; the statement is conditional on a large bundle of project-specific hypotheses and on a bound for Tate-Shafarevich-type groups.

UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReducti.title: Window bound on Sha lengths from the literature bundle H'
UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReducti.summary: Hypothesis: the bundle `HypothesesH'`, a nested record of literature-type statements (a rank-n literature package with local, automorphic, cohomological and CM parts; Clozel-type cohomological and conjugation statements; a Borel injectivity statement; Galois representations for totally real GL_2; strong multiplicity one; Gelfand–Kazhdan; quadratic base change; newforms; a weak descent from GL_n over a CM field to a unitary group for n between 2 and 4; cyclic base change of prime degree; existence of definite quaternion algebras; semisimplicity of cusp forms). Conclusion: `VWin`. For every primitive Dirichlet character ψ, every ε in (0, 1/52) and every choice of exponents e(x) with x^(2+8ε) ≤ 2^e(x) ≤ 2x^(2+8ε), there is J ≥ 1 such that for all large X and all prime pairs (q, d) in a prescribed size window with congruence conditions (q ≡ 3 mod 8, d ≡ 7 mod 16, q | d+1, d+1 divisible by all small odd primes), there is Y with X^(1/J) ≤ Y ≤ √X such that for all x in [Y, Y²] and every subfield E of a cyclotomic field cut out by ψ, the quadratic characters of q and d and the condition a ≡ ±1 mod 2^(e+2): the groups Sha¹ of Q_l/Z_l twisted by the (−e')-th power of the cyclotomic character have finite length for 0 < e' < x^401, and the sum over primes l of log l times these lengths is at most exp(x^ε / 2).
UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReducti.role: Final assembly of the V-window: combines a 'Lemma K' derived from the literature package, two end-point statements, and four counting bounds (labelled I, II, III, V, obtained from Kato-type input with automorphy, an Sp4 input, and a reduced unitary lift) through `Core.of_four_alt`.
UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReducti.caveat: `VWin` was unfolded completely down to Sha lengths. The hypothesis bundle was read at the level of field names and three of its fields (weak descent, cyclic base change, the rank-n package header); the remaining fields are described from their names. The counting lemmas used in the proof were not opened.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are literature-type, but the conclusion is a uniform bound on Tate–Shafarevich lengths in special cyclotomic subfields that the project then uses (with further literature) to derive its statement for every Dirichlet character; no such bound is a standard published theorem.

UpperTheory.V.Z.Bc.seedIIs_alt.title: Existence of an automorphic rank-four seed in case II
UpperTheory.V.Z.Bc.seedIIs_alt.summary: Hypothesis: the literature bundle `HypothesesH'` (a nested record of automorphic and Galois-theoretic statements: a rank-n literature package, Clozel-type statements, Galois representations for totally real GL_2, strong multiplicity one, quadratic and cyclic base change, weak descent to unitary groups, and others). Conclusion: `SeedIIAlt`. For every prime l, coefficient ring, 'raw' datum D (a list of l-adic characters of the absolute Galois group of Q defining a diagonal four-dimensional representation with characters θ, Ψ, α, 1) and tower T over D (a totally real abelian field F, an imaginary quadratic field K and L = FK, with places above l) satisfying the case-II context, and the conditions `Ok`, `Two`, `Deep`, and for every identification of the algebraic closure of Q_l with C, there exist a larger coefficient ring and a framed deformation Q of the Galois group of F over it such that: Q pairs with the frame, is continuous, has the prescribed residual shape, is irreducible on a subgroup, and after restriction to L and a twist by a character it is attached to a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_4 over L with weights differing by even integers at least 4; in addition its reduction lies in a prescribed support pattern and has a nonzero entry in one of two specified positions.
UpperTheory.V.Z.Bc.seedIIs_alt.role: Existence of an object, obtained by reduction: the proof packages the bundle with a weight-one Hilbert Eisenstein statement and one further literature item, derives an induction-of-automorphy statement from quadratic base change, a cyclic rank-two lift and `indCs`, and applies `seedII_Z_alt`.
UpperTheory.V.Z.Bc.seedIIs_alt.caveat: `SeedIIAlt`, `IsSeedAlt`, `SeedPairAlt`, `Raw`, `Tower`, `Ctx2` and `Deep` were read; the framed-deformation type `PD`, the conditions `Ok`, `Two`, `IsPair`, `Res`, `InV` and the precise meaning of 'attached' (`AttC`) were read only as signatures. Most fields of the hypothesis bundle are described from their names.

literature.basis: The hypothesis is a bundle of literature statements, but the conclusion is an existence statement about seeds for towers and raw data that are defined only in this project's modularity argument.

UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.adjoint_lift_w_of_.title: Adjoint lift from definite U(2) to U(3), with alternative
UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.adjoint_lift_w_of_.summary: Hypotheses: a bundle `LiteratureRankNHypothesis` of literature statements (four sub-bundles: local representation theory of GL(n), automorphic forms and Galois representations, cohomological results, CM theory), and a form-level statement `SpecOutS`. Conclusion (`AdLiftW`): let L be a CM field unramified over its maximal totally real subfield, S0 a finite set and P a set of finite places, disjoint, all split over the real subfield, with distinct restrictions to it, and S0 covering the places above 2. Let π be an automorphic representation of the definite unitary group in 2 variables over L, of weight difference j ≥ 1 at every infinite place, unramified away from S0, whose local components at places of S0 and P are principal series with characters (ψ0, ψ1), unramified and with regular ratio at P. Then either there is an automorphic representation of the definite unitary group in 3 variables, unramified away from S0, whose components at S0 and at almost all places of P are subquotients of the principal series with characters (ψ0/ψ1, 1, ψ1/ψ0); or there is an automorphic representation of the 2-variable group whose components at almost all places of P have character ratio (ψ0/ψ1) squared.
UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.adjoint_lift_w_of_.role: A passage from forms to representations: `SpecOutS` gives the same dichotomy for individual eigenforms at a fixed level and for every finite subset of P; finiteness of automorphic representations at fixed level and weight plus a pigeonhole argument gives one representation that works for almost all of P.
UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.adjoint_lift_w_of_.caveat: The automorphic and local notions (automorphic representation of the definite unitary group, local component, principal series subquotient) were read in the project's definitions. The contents of the literature bundle were read only as field names. `SpecOutS` is proved elsewhere in the project as `specOutS`; that proof was not read.

literature.basis: The first alternative is a form of the adjoint (Gelbart–Jacquet type) lift from rank 2 to rank 3, which is a known kind of result, but the two-way alternative and this formulation on definite unitary groups are specific to the project, and the statement is conditional on a project-specific hypothesis.

UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.unitary_three_auto.title: Automorphic three-dimensional adjoint lifts in arbitrarily large weights (conditional)
UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.unitary_three_auto.summary: Hypotheses: (i) `HypothesesH'`, a bundle of about fifteen assumed statements from the literature (a 'literature rank n' hypothesis, statements named after Clozel and Borel, Galois representations for GL2 over totally real fields, strong multiplicity one, Gelfand–Kazhdan, admissibility, quadratic and cyclic base change, descent, newforms, existence of definite quaternion algebras, semisimplicity of cusp forms); (ii) `RowT`: every regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representation of GL_a over a CM field has an attached l-adic Galois representation with the project's list of local and global properties. Conclusion: let K be an imaginary quadratic field, L an abelian CM field, l a prime, and χ', η, θ l-adic characters of the absolute Galois group of ℚ satisfying the project's field-and-character conditions (η cuts out K, splitting conditions at an auxiliary level, the parity χ'(c) = (−1)^j, a non-congruence condition), with χ' ≠ η and an integer M divisible by 2l controlling ramification. Then for every bound B there is m ≥ B with m ≡ j mod (l − 1) and a continuous 3-dimensional l-adic representation r of the Galois group of L, irreducible on every open subgroup, which preserves a symmetric pairing compatible with complex conjugation, has characteristic polynomials congruent to those of ε^j χ' ⊕ 1 ⊕ (ε^j χ')^(−1) (ε the cyclotomic character), has prescribed type (χ', 1, χ'^(−1)) away from l, is ordinary of weights (m, 0, −m) above l, and whose twist by ε^(−1) is automorphic in the project's conjugate self-dual sense.
UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.unitary_three_auto.role: Assembly of three earlier conditional results: existence of 2-dimensional representations congruent to Eisenstein series in all large weights, the fact that their restrictions to L (after a character twist) lie in a class W, and automorphy of the trace-zero adjoint for that class (the only place the hypothesis (ii) is used). It is a reduction step; the next theorem in the file removes hypothesis (ii) by deriving it from the bundle (i).
UpperTheory.V.Z.Sym.W.unitary_three_auto.caveat: The predicates for 'automorphic in the conjugate self-dual sense' (`IsAutCsdA`), 'ordinary' (`OrdAt`), 'type away from l' (`TypeAway`), the auxiliary condition `SlopeTestRemainingChoices`, the condition `UnrSplit` on L and M, and the property list `PropsB` in `RowT` were not unfolded. That r is the trace-zero adjoint of a 2-dimensional representation is read from the definitions of the proof ingredients (`AdAutW`, `SeedInW`, `PropEGW`), not from the conclusion itself, which only asserts existence of r.

literature.basis: The statement is conditional on literature bundles and concludes existence of representations with the project's own 'seed' package of properties. Adjoint (symmetric square) lifting from GL2 is classical, but this formulation is specific to the project's construction.

UpperTheory.V.Z.Win.Dn.ends0_alt.title: Automorphy of points on two rank-3 ordinary deformation problems
UpperTheory.V.Z.Win.Dn.ends0_alt.summary: Hypothesis: a bundle `HypothesesH'` of 15 assumptions, all formulated as literature results on automorphic forms and Galois representations (a rank-n literature bundle, two Clozel statements, Borel injectivity, Galois representations for totally real GL2, strong multiplicity one, Gelfand–Kazhdan, admissibility, quadratic and cyclic prime-degree base change, a weak descent to unitary groups in rank 2 to 4, a rank-2 descent alternative, existence of definite quaternion algebras, semisimplicity of cusp forms). Conclusion, two statements about homomorphisms from the absolute Galois group of Q into the group GL3 ⋊ {±1}. (1) For every CM field K and every datum of the project's type `Dat` (two characters η, Ψ and a complex conjugation), there is a marked group element g₁ such that: residual characteristic polynomials of all 'ordinary points' agree with a reference representation on a finite-index subgroup; every ordinary point over a discrete valuation ring that stays irreducible on all open subgroups of ker η becomes, after restriction to K and a cyclotomic twist, automorphic in the project's conjugate-self-dual sense; and for points of block type the associated 2-dimensional representation is attached to a newform of weight 2e+1. (2) For K = Q(i) and every 'host frame' (a deformation problem unramified outside lN built from the character mod 4 and a Dirichlet character ψ), there is a marked element such that for every universal deformation a certain weight-zero module is finite over the coefficient ring and every characteristic-zero point that is irreducible on ker η is automorphic over K after twisting by the inverse cyclotomic character.
UpperTheory.V.Z.Win.Dn.ends0_alt.role: A one-line assembly: it applies `ends_u_alt` to the hypothesis bundle and discharges that lemma's remaining input `LinkedUnlE` using `linkedUnlE_holds_alt`, which in turn is fed a second 'seed' automorphy case (`seed2_alt`) and a density statement for unitary-three automorphy (`unitary_three_automorphy_dense_of_prints`).
UpperTheory.V.Z.Win.Dn.ends0_alt.caveat: The definitions of the two conclusions (`GdEndAlt`, `ThmS6Core_s`) and of `OrdPt`, `FinEnd`, `AutEnd3Alt`, `AutEnd2Ao`, `HostData`, `IsHostFrame`, `IsAutCsdA`, `AutOnAlt` were read; the notions `IsUniv`, `Frame`, `wpart`, `WitAQ`, `AutCsd0` and the full `Dat` structure were not unfolded. Most fields of the hypothesis bundle are described from their names (e.g. `ClozelCohC`, `StrongMultOneReal`); `DescWeak`, `CycC`, `Desc2`, `DefQuatExists`, `CuspSemisimpleReal` were read.

literature.basis: The hypotheses are literature statements, but the conclusion is an automorphy (modularity-lifting type) statement for the project's own deformation frames and 'ordinary point' conditions; it is not a named published theorem.

_private.Development.AutomorphicArithmet.title: Unlinked principal series persists under CM quadratic base change (GL_2)
_private.Development.AutomorphicArithmet.summary: Setting: F totally real, E a CM quadratic extension of F, a prime l with an isomorphism of an algebraic closure of Q_l with C, and a continuous representation r of the absolute Galois group of F into GL_2 over that closure whose restriction to E is irreducible. Hypotheses: π is a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2 over F to which r is attached (r is semisimple and at almost all places Frobenius has the characteristic polynomial given by the Satake parameters of π), and P is a regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GL_2 over E to which the restriction of r is attached. Conclusion: for every finite place w of E with v the place of F below it, if π is 'plain' at v (its local component has cuspidal support consisting of characters, no two differing by the absolute value) or π is unramified at v, then P is plain at w.
_private.Development.AutomorphicArithmet.role: Private lemma proved by a detour through auxiliary fields: a second CM quadratic extension E' in which v splits (`splitCM`), quadratic base change of π to E' (`quadBC2`, the self-twist case excluded by `noTw`), cyclic base change to the compositum M (`upCycle`), comparison of the two base changes via attached Galois representations (`attBC`), and transfer of 'window' bounds on the support characters up and down (`winPt`, `winUpDown`, `plainOf`, `thruTr`, `splitTr`). It is the only input of the public theorem `awReal` in the same file.
_private.Development.AutomorphicArithmet.caveat: `RealUp`, `PlainAt`, `PlainAtR`, `PlainTor`, `Unlinked`, `AttachedSys`/`AttC`/`AttR`, `IsRegAlg` and `HasSat` were read. The types of cuspidal representations (`CuspSub`, `TR.CuspSub`), `IsLocComp` and `HasSupport`/`IsCuspSupport` were taken at face value. The cited lemmas in the proof were not opened; their roles are inferred from their statements' shapes and names.

literature.basis: The conclusion is what compatibility of quadratic base change with local base change at every finite place (Langlands, Arthur–Clozel) gives for principal-series components; the formulation with the project's predicates `PlainAt`/`PlainTor` is its own, so this is not marked as plainly known.
